News.title: Erika Kirk appears to blast Dave Chappelle over ‘disgusting’ joke about husband’s murder
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Erika Kirk, the widow of conservative activist Charlie Kirk, has blasted controversial comedian Dave Chappelle over what she called a “disgusting” joke about her husband’s assassination.

Kirk, the founder of Turning Point USA, was gunned down in September 2025 at the age of 31 during an event on a college campus in Utah. While both sides of the aisle condemned the violence, some made light of or even celebrated his murder and were strongly rebuked.

But that didn’t stop Chappelle, known for his unapologetically offensive jokes, from making a crack about Kirk’s assassination at a show at Madison Square Garden in New York City on Saturday.

“Ever since that guy Charlie Kirk got murdered and I shouldn’t say this publicly, but I feel better,” Chappelle said to laughter.

Erika Kirk, who has taken over her late husband’s political operation since his death, didn’t name Chappelle specifically, but it was clear who she meant when she called out “comedians” who “laugh about political assassination” in an X post Sunday.

open image in gallery Erika Kirk, the widow of conservative activist Charlie Kirk, has blasted controversial comedian Dave Chappelle over what she called a 'disgusting' joke about her husband’s assassination ( Getty Images )

“To see leftist podcasters, comedians, and commentators laugh about political assassination as though it’s entertainment and the destruction of a human life is a punchline, is beyond disgusting,” she said.

Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan from the popular progressive I’ve Had It podcast were also under fire this week for laughing at a joke about Kirk.

The pair were reading social media posts reacting to Republicans’ midterm election defeat when they laughed at one that said, “We’re digging up Charlie Kirk and doing it again.”

Welch and Sullivan issued an apology as they lost sponsorships from brands, including the payment platform Cash App, which said, “We do not condone violence of any kind.”

open image in gallery ‘Ever since that guy Charlie Kirk got murdered and I shouldn’t say this publicly, but I feel better,’ Chappelle said to laughter at a show at Madison Square Garden in New York City on Saturday ( Getty Images )

“My husband, Charlie Kirk, was killed in an act of political violence, something our two children and I will live with every day for the rest of our lives,” Erika Kirk’s post continued.

“A culture that laughs at assassination is one of profound moral decay. It threatens the very foundation of our country and the principles that hold our democracy together,” Erika Kirk said. “You do not have to agree with someone’s politics to recognize the value of their life. This should not be so hard.

“Political violence must never be something this country tolerates, excuses, or celebrates.”

open image in gallery “To see leftist podcasters, comedians, and commentators laugh about political assassination as though it’s entertainment and the destruction of a human life is a punchline, is beyond disgusting,” Erika Kirk said ( Getty Images )

Other figures of President Donald Trump’s MAGA movement that Kirk was part of also shared their outrage.

Podcaster Benny Johnson said of Chappelle’s joke, “This isn’t even comedy It’s just sick.”

Alec Lace called Chappelle a “scumbag.”

“Dave Chapelle [sic] feels better ever since Charlie Kirk was murdered. He feels better knowing a father was taken from his kids just for having different opinions,” the podcaster wrote. “What a scumbag.”

The Independent has reached out to Chappelle’s representatives for comment.

News.title: Popular progressive podcast sees sponsors flee after ‘insensitive’ Charlie Kirk joke
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A popular progressive podcast has seen its sponsors flee after laughing at a joke about the slain conservative influencer Charlie Kirk, which the hosts later admitted was “insensitive.”

Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan read social media posts reacting to Tuesday’s midterm election — in which Democrats took control of the House and Senate and won key governors’ races — on Thursday’s episode of their I’ve Had It podcast.

They both cracked up to a post that read, “We’re digging up Charlie Kirk and doing it again.”

The clip has since been cut from the episode, and the two apologized for laughing at the joke. But the damage has already been done.

Kirk’s widow, Erika Kirk, blasted “leftist podcasters” and others who laugh about political assassination “beyond disgusting” in an X post Sunday.

open image in gallery A popular progressive podcast has seen its sponsors flee after laughing at a joke about the slain conservative influencer Charlie Kirk, which the hosts later admitted was 'insensitive' ( Getty )

When an outraged social media user told his followers to boycott Cash App for sponsoring “these rotten women,” the peer-to-peer payment platform wrote on X Friday, “We do not condone violence of any kind, and we are no longer sponsors of this podcast.”

Pet brand Chewy announced Saturday that it currently has no ties to the podcast.

“We do not sponsor or support the ‘I’ve Had It’ podcast. We unequivocally condemn violence in all forms. The comments made by the hosts do not reflect Chewy’s values or what we stand for as a company,” Chewy wrote on X.

Eyewear brand Zenni also announced that it “does not condone violence of any type.”

“We have canceled advertising on I’ve Had It and are reviewing our podcast placements against our brand safety standards,” Zenni wrote on X.

Organic bedding brand Boll & Branch said it “does not currently advertise with the ‘I’ve Had It’ podcast and will not in the future.”

open image in gallery Payment platform Cash App, pet brand Chewy and other companies have announced they currently don’t have ties with podcast hosts Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan, adding that they don’t condone violence ( Getty )

Kirk, the founder of the conservative youth organization Turning Point USA, was assassinated at age 31 during an outdoor event on a college campus in Utah in September 2025.

Both Republicans and Democrats condemned the assassination of Kirk, who was seen as a steward of Trump’s MAGA movement and even a potential presidential nominee in the future. Some critics made light of or even celebrated Kirk’s death, and they were swiftly rebuked.

Amid backlash for their response to a joke about Kirk’s assassination, Welch and Sullivan wrote on Instagram, “On Thursday’s show, we laughed at a joke about Charlie Kirk. It was an insensitive joke, and we should not have laughed. We regret it, and we apologize.”

“Whatever our political differences, there is nothing funny about gun violence. We’ve long supported common-sense gun safety reform,” the hosts said. “To that end, we’ve made a donation to Everytown for Gun Safety, the largest gun violence prevention organization in America. We’ll keep using our platforms to fight for the safety of all Americans.”

News.title: Man arrested on suspicion of murder also under investigation over five aggravated burglaries
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

For free real time breaking news alerts sent straight to your inbox sign up to our breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

A man in his 30s has been arrested on suspicion of murder while also being investigated over five aggravated burglaries, Greater Manchester Police has said.

The arrest comes after a man in his 70s was found dead during a search of an address on Whitstable Close in Chadderton, Oldham. He is believed to have died between November 4-7.

Police said his death is being treated as suspicious and his loved ones have been informed.

The suspect has been arrested on suspicion of aggravated burglary and murder.

He had already been arrested in relation to five aggravated burglaries between January and October this year when detectives linked him to the murder case.

The victims in the burglaries had all been targeted similarly, with the suspect attempting to or gaining entry to their properties before demanding they hand over their bank cards and pin codes, the force said.

open image in gallery The suspect remains in custody for questioning ( Alamy/PA )

The suspect remains in custody for questioning.

Detective Superintendent Amber Waywell said: “First and foremost, our thoughts are with the gentleman who has sadly died and with his family and loved ones at what will be an incredibly difficult and distressing time.

“This remains a complex and developing investigation, and we are working hard to establish the full circumstances surrounding his death.

“I would like to thank the outstanding work of our detectives, who have shown real determination and persistence throughout this investigation.”

She added: “Let me be clear: we take offences like these incredibly seriously, and we will not tolerate those who seek to prey on vulnerable members of our communities.”

Police have urged any potential victims of a similar crime which could be linked to get in touch with them.

People can contact GMP on 0161 856 9577, quoting the log number 2908, or through their online portal or anonymously through Crimestoppers.

News.title: Nvidia launches investigation after CEO Jensen Huang admits to affair with suspected Chinese spy
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair with a woman whom U.S. intelligence reportedly suspects is a Chinese spy.

Huang, who heads a leading AI chipmaker and is an ally of President Donald Trump, apologized in a message to the company, saying, “I was unfaithful to my wife,” according to The New York Times.

“My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Nvidia announced in a press release Sunday that its board was opening an independent investigation “in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.”

open image in gallery Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair with a woman whom U.S. intelligence reportedly suspects is a Chinese spy ( Getty )

Late last month, the Times reported that Huang had formed a close relationship with Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, a Chinese executive at a Singapore-based data center.

Alice Huang is considered by U.S. officials to be a Chinese spy, feeding information to Beijing, according to the report, which cited sources briefed on the surveillance of Alice Huang and other officials and industry experts.

When asked about Alice Huang being suspected of spying for China, Liu Chang, the spokesman for the Chinese Embassy in Washington, told the Times the U.S. was pursuing a campaign of “groundless smears and slanders” against the Asian country.

Nvidia’s board “prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” Sunday’s company press release read.

“While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information.”

open image in gallery Nvidia announced Sunday that its board was opening an independent investigation ‘in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort’ ( Getty )

CEO Huang supports the investigation and has agreed to cooperate, the board said. There was no word of Huang’s position being in jeopardy, with the board saying it “has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.”

Nvidia is one of the hottest companies in the stock market right now, given the popularity of its chips. It has a market capitalization of roughly 4.5 trillion and was trading at nearly $240 per share early last month.

“Today’s news will not slow Nvidia,” Nvidia spokesman John Rizzo told the Times on Sunday. “Jensen is committed to continuing to lead Nvidia as C.E.O. without interruption.”

Huang, like other tech leaders, has flocked to Trump as the president embraces AI. The Nvidia leader and his wife, Lori Huang, attended a state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House in September. His attendance wasn’t unusual, given that OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg were also there.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio refused to say whether Huang was excluded from U.S. briefings in light of the recent reporting. He told reporters Sunday before departing for France, “I just can’t comment because of the nature of it.”

open image in gallery Late last month, it was reported that Huang had formed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese executive at a Singapore-based data center who U.S. officials suspect was feeding information to Beijing ( AFP/Getty )

Trump is a major backer of AI, trying to rebrand the technology as SI for “Super Intelligence” and loosen regulations.

While Huang may be an ally to the president, it will be hard to overlook a potential security breach from not only a U.S. adversary, but also its top competitor in the AI race.

“We’re leading China in AI,” the president said in September amid concerns that AI could pose an existential threat to humans. “We’re the most sophisticated country in the world. And frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins.”

The Independent has reached out to the State Department and the White House for comment.

News.title: Pope Leo sends democracy warning to Trump-ally Milei in first Argentina visit for decades
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Speaking to president Javier Milei during the second stop of a 12-day tour across South America, Pope Leo on Sunday urged Argentina to protect its democracy.

The speech to Milei, a close ally of US president Donald Trump, was closely watched by political observers.

Leo told Milei, who has stated he plans to seek re-election next year, that political leaders must work to improve the lives of all citizens and recognise the limits of their authority. The president's austerity program has drawn criticism from the Church for heavily impacting the poorest, while Milei has also strongly backed the war in Iran.

"Authority is most authentic when it is exercised as service," the pope said in an address opening a three-day visit to Argentina, marking the first time a pope has visited the majority-Catholic country since 1987.

"Those who exercise authority have a duty to act with prudence, to acknowledge the limits of the power entrusted to them, and to direct their decisions toward the good of the entire community," said Leo, the first US-born pope, who sparked anger from Trump earlier this year after condemning the conflict in Iran.

The pope, who took the historic step for a Catholic leader of casting a vote by mail in the US midterm elections last week, added that democracy requires citizens to live together despite differing views and to maintain faith in the rule of law.

open image in gallery Milei is a close ally of Donald Trump ( AP )

"Democracy... is a part of Argentina's heritage that needs to be safeguarded," Leo said, noting that it is reinforced by "the patient search for agreement, and through the ability to see those who think differently as fellow citizens with whom we share a common future.”

Leo, 71, is undertaking one of the most demanding foreign trips by a Catholic leader in decades, coming less than a month after undergoing lung cancer surgery. He will visit four Argentine cities through Wednesday.

Following the pope's arrival at Buenos Aires' Jorge Newbery airport on Sunday, thousands of people lined his route to central Buenos Aires, waving small Vatican and Argentine flags, as Catholic nuns wearing tan habits chanted: "The pope is here, you can feel it."

"It's been almost 40 years, 39 exactly, that the pope hasn't come to Argentina," said Claudia Sona, who travelled from the northern province of Salta. "For Catholics, and I think for non-Catholics, this is a rebirth."

Milei, a theatrical figure known for provocative statements and untamed hair, came to power in 2023 campaigning with a chainsaw to symbolise major spending cuts intended to repair national finances.

He has faced accusations of weakening Argentine democracy through divisive language and attacks on journalists.

The president has defended his economic measures as essential for controlling inflation. Annual inflation has dropped from over 200 per cent to 33 per cent under his administration.

However, polls indicate his public approval has declined ahead of next year's elections as Argentines face reduced subsidies, public-sector job cuts and business failures caused by squeezed household budgets.

open image in gallery This is the first visit by a pope to Argentina for almost 40 years ( AFP/Getty )

Milei's cuts have reduced social support, including disability allowances, and poverty remains a key issue despite falling significantly from its peak during his first year in office.

Although Leo did not directly name Milei's austerity program, he urged that economic stimulus measures in Argentina should not harm the most vulnerable.

"Efforts should be made to promote whatever creates opportunities, stimulates private initiative and ensures that economic growth also benefits those who are disadvantaged," he said.

The pope, who has previously warned that artificial intelligence could trigger perpetual conflict, revisited the topic in Argentina, emphasizing that technological innovation must be accompanied by "ethical consciousness" in remarks touching on another priority for Milei.

Milei has advocated for AI growth and stated his ambition to transform Argentina into a major destination for data centres.

Leo is conducting an intensive 50-event, three-nation trip until 17 November. He visited Uruguay before arriving in Argentina and moves on to Peru on Wednesday.

The pope, who addresses host governments during foreign visits, typically relies on careful diplomatic phrasing but has recently taken a more direct stance on global affairs, criticizing the direction of international leadership.

Ahead of his arrival in Argentina, commentators expected domestic politicians to scrutinise his address to Milei carefully.

"Any interventions by Leo, particularly on poverty, the limits of markets or confrontational political rhetoric, could be read as implicit criticism of Milei and amplify existing opposition to the government's approach," said Nicolas Watson, a managing director at advisory firm Teneo.

open image in gallery Milei plans to run for re-election next year ( Reuters )

Fortunato Mallimaci, a sociologist at Argentina's Conicet research institute, said Leo's trip would offer unity and encouragement to those feeling sidelined by Milei's economic policies.

During his 18-month papacy, Leo has called on global leaders to treat migrants with greater humanity and urged measures on climate change, positions that have put him at odds with Trump and other right-wing figures.

The Vatican has described the trip as a "homecoming" for Leo, who worked for decades as a missionary in Peru and gained Peruvian citizenship. Officials in Argentina estimate up to 7 million people could see the pope during his visit.

The pope's schedule in Argentina features visits to a detention center and a care centre for people with disabilities, highlighting his focus on marginalised communities.

Milei previously launched sharp attacks against Leo's predecessor, Francis, an Argentine who did not return home during his 12-year papacy. Despite once calling Francis "an imbecile," Milei later sought to rebuild relations and visited him at the Vatican.

"Milei doesn't win anything by fighting with (Leo)," said Veronica Gimenez Beliveau, a sociologist at the University of Buenos Aires.

News.title: Police make arrest in a deadly shooting at Winston-Salem State during homecoming weekend
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Authorities on Sunday arrested a man in a shooting during homecoming weekend at Winston-Salem State University in North Carolina that left one person dead and at least one other person injured.

Winston-Salem police said officers who were on campus for homecoming events heard gunshots around 9:45 p.m. Saturday. They found a 19-year-old man with a gunshot wound. They rendered aid but the man died at the scene.

A 22-year-old woman who had what appeared to be a gunshot wound was taken to a hospital, where she was treated and later released.

Assistant Chief Jason Swaim said at a news conference the investigation led to Ziyaire Spinks, 20, who was arrested and being held without bond on charges of murder, assault with a deadly weapon and possession of a firearm on educational property.

According to police, the shooting stemmed from an argument between two groups of people. They confirmed Spinks was not a student at the university.

A second shooting on campus happened less than an hour later, with police responding when they heard shots. In that case, Swaim said two people were injured when gunfire erupted following an altercation.

Authorities said they were investigating to determine if there was any connection between the two shootings. No arrests have been made in the second case.

Chief William Penn, Jr. of the Winston-Salem Police Department vowed during a news conference that authorities will find all of those responsible for the violence at the school.

“It’s important that the blame of these tragic events go to the right people and that’s the folks who committed these acts,” he said, asking people not to point fingers while the investigation is ongoing.

University officials canceled the remainder of homecoming activities Sunday, saying instead that a local church planned to lead a call for prayers in support of the community.

On social media, community members were sharing their condolences and asking for prayers.

Chancellor Bonita J. Brown called the shootings “senseless violence.” In a statement, she assured students, faculty and parents that the campus was secure and that additional law enforcement would remain while the investigation continues.

The school offered counseling for anyone in need.

“We also recognize the concern and anxiety these events have created among our students, parents, families and broader community,” Brown said. “We take our responsibility for campus safety seriously."

Forsyth County Sheriff Bobby Kimbrough, Jr. echoed the sentiments of the chancellor and other law enforcement officials during the news conference.

“Right now, the community is in need of your prayers. The community is in need of us coming together,” Kimbrough said.

___

Montoya Bryan reported from Albuquerque, New Mexico.

News.title: An argument over Wi-Fi leads to double murder in Texas
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The latest headlines from our reporters across the US sent straight to your inbox each weekday Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

An argument over Wi-Fi led to the murder of a mother and her son in their home in Texas, authorities said.

Jeremiah McGee was arrested Friday and charged with capital murder in the October 23 shooting deaths of Maria Davalos, 62, and her son, Ariel Arellano Jr., 32, in their home, a duplex in Lufkin, about 157 miles southeast of Dallas, late last month.

“They determined Mr. McGee to be the main suspect and continued to work the information until they had enough to gain a warrant for his arrest and a second search warrant of his home,” Police Chief Travis Brazil said, according to KTRE.

Authorities apprehended McGee, 47, at his home on Friday afternoon. They also positively matched the gun used in the homicides with a weapon found at his home.

Investigators used the shell casings located at the scene of the crime and compared them to the gun. The ATF’s National Integrated Ballistic Information Network in Houston later confirmed the match, the Lufkin Daily News reported.

open image in gallery A Texas man was arrested and charged with capital murder after fatally shooting his two neighbors ( Lufkin Police Department )

A homicide investigation began last month after officers responded to a 911 call and found Davalos and Arellano dead with gunshot wounds.

The 911 caller was the son and brother of the victims, police said.

As authorities interviewed people for their investigation, all of them — including McGee — said there had been arguments over Wi-Fi before the killings. It was not immediately clear what regarding the Wi-Fi the group was arguing about specifically, but McGee and the victims lived side-by-side in a duplex, authorities said.

Authorities have not shared any other information about the dispute and subsequent shooting.

McGee was booked into the Angelina County Jail. His bond has been set at $2 million.

He was charged with capital murder due to the case involving the deaths of two people during the same criminal episode.

News.title: Burnham admits NHS faces difficult winter as he unveils £40m to help keep patients out of hospital
News.content:

Andy Burnham has warned this winter won’t be easy for the NHS as he announced a £40 million plan to try to keep patients out of hospital to take the pressure off overworked Accident & Emergency departments.

The money will help doctors give extra care to those at risk of becoming seriously unwell during the colder months, such as those with conditions like heart disease and frailty. Groups of GP practices will get £126 for each patients supported.

The prime minister said: “If we want to take the pressure off our hospitals this winter, we’ve got to keep people well at home. So we’re backing GPs to reach the most vulnerable people early, before a small problem turns into a trip to A&E.”

open image in gallery Ambulances wait outside an Emergency Department ( Getty )

He added: “I’m not going to pretend this winter will be easy. But with new technology, upgrades for hospitals and more care available closer to home, we’ll make sure the NHS is there for everyone when they need it.”

The health secretary Yvette Cooper warned the NHS had already faced a “heavy summer” as a result of a series of heatwaves.

The warning comes amid continuing concerns about overcrowding in hospitals and patients being treated in corridors as emergency departments struggle to cope with demand.

In January 2025 Wes Streeting, the then health secretary, said patients had been “let down” by being treated in makeshift wards and left waiting for hours for ambulances as a ‘winter crisis’ engulfed the NHS.

But last month the Royal College of Physicians warned there was still much the government had to do to ensure “corridor care becomes a thing of the past”.

open image in gallery Prime Minister Andy Burnham said ‘I’m not going to pretend this winter will be easy’ for the NHS ( AFP/Getty )

The money, reallocated from existing GP budgets, will help doctors’ surgeries identify and intervene with patients they believe are most at risk of becoming very unwell this winter.

Extra support will be targeted at patients with heart disease, frailty and lung conditions like emphysema and other types of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

Medication reviews, health checks and respiratory clinics led by nurses are among the support that will be available for up to 300,000 people.

Ed Kennedy, director of the Institute of General Practice Management, welcomed the move, saying: “General practice teams know their patients and are well placed to identify those most vulnerable, providing proactive and personalised care that helps people stay well and reduces avoidable pressure on hospitals.”

News.title: Energised England deliver statement win to take heat off Borthwick
News.content:
England’s players delivered on their self-created ultimatum to “do it for Steve” by annihilating an abysmal Australia. Barring an extraordinary sequence of events, Borthwick will now remain as head coach through to the World Cup.

Even if Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney’s vote of confidence in the head coach last week was delivered without caveats, he would still have been forced to play the role of reluctant Caesar if the crowd turned mutinous, as they did four years ago. That resulted in Sweeney delivering the thumbs down on Eddie Jones’s reign.

Yet this did not come to pass, as England showed plenty of fire and fury on behalf of their head coach after his control of the dressing room was questioned last week. With 14 minutes to go the crowd, who had been muted on Remembrance Sunday, broke into a rendition of Swing Low, indicating their own approval.

It was not perfect. Attack coach Lee Blackett will be hugely frustrated that they only scored seven tries from a staggering 22 entries into the Australia 22. They also took their foot off the Wallabies’ throats in the final quarter, although they did surpass their highest points total against the visitors. Probably the biggest disappointment was the injuries suffered by wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and centre Seb Atkinson, who had both enjoyed strong games until that point.

News.title: Lando Norris wins chaotic Sao Paulo Grand Prix but F1 season is fizzling out
News.content:
Lando Norris will start today’s Sao Paulo Grand Prix on pole position after a chaotic qualifying session at Interlagos yesterday. A red flag was thrown a matter of moments into qualifying, which led to a lengthy delay of around an hour and a half. When racing did resume, the conditions were treacherous but it was the 2025 world champion Norris who coped best by claiming his third straight pole at Interlagos.

“It has been a long day,” Norris said after taking pole. “It has been a great qualifying. To be on pole again here, two years in a row, different conditions to last year, but I am very happy. It is not easy conditions out there, especially when you know it is going to rain a lot more. It was about getting two laps in at the beginning, not making any mistakes, and that is exactly what we did, so it has been a very good day.

“This was my first time driving the car in the wet, so I think I figured it out pretty quick. It is tough because you are wet, intermediates, all different tyres, and it was very windy the last couple of laps. It was certainly a good day for learning for me and good to take into tomorrow [today]. These guys [Mercedes] are also very quick. Just happy. Today [yesterday] is about getting on pole. It does not really matter how you do it, so very pleased with that.”

News.title: Man Utd are in relegation trouble and Carrick must be sacked
News.content:
Michael Carrick says he has been given no assurances about his future beyond this afternoon’s crucial game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford.



United are searching for only their second Premier League win of the season and first in 70 days after the club’s worst start to a campaign for 40 years piled the pressure on Carrick.



They dropped into the relegation zone last night following Nottingham Forest’s victory over Manchester City and will be bottom by the end of the weekend if they lose to Villa and Crystal Palace and Sunderland both win.



The Old Trafford hierarchy opted to give Carrick more time to try to turn their season around following a 3-0 hammering by Bournemouth and 4-1 drubbing in Como, since when United have been beaten 2-0 by Chelsea and recovered from two goals down to overcome Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday night.



Asked if he had been told outright he would still be in charge next week, Carrick said: “No - no. Just carry on as absolute normal.”



Pressed on when he felt his future was uncertain, the head coach added: “No, no. Whatever happens and what’s going to happen is going to happen in terms of the game, we’ve got to prepare right.



“I’m really looking forward to playing at home on the back of the other night. The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming and energised and feeling good about what they might see and we’ve got to repay that.”



Another defeat would leave the United board with a big decision to make around Carrick’s future at a time when they are under severe attack from the fanbase.



United’s game against Roma was briefly interrupted when tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch in the first half of a game notable for more furious protests against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.



Three people were arrested by Greater Manchester Police for throwing items on to the pitch and are understood to have been hit with automatic three-year football banning orders as a consequence.



More in-stadium demonstrations are expected today with regular match going fans encouraged not to buy alcohol or drinks inside Old Trafford and again release green and gold balloons before kick-off.



Green and gold were the club’s original colours as Newton Heath and have become a symbol of protest against the ownership.



Asked why there had been such a big drop-off from last season, Carrick added: “It’s just inconsistency, that’s within games,” he said.



“It can be a number of things, it’s never just one thing: a bit of decision-making, a bit of concentration, things going against us in certain points, sometimes we haven’t helped ourselves. So there’s no excuses for it, it is what it is. The great thing is we can do something about it.”

News.title: Xabi Alonso disgusted after Chelsea bullied by Brobbey and Sunderland
News.content:
Today is must-win match: for both sides.

For Sunderland that argument is easy to make – they are bottom of the Premier League, are without a win since August and for morale, if nothing else need at least a point, though three is really what the doctor orders.

For Chelsea – fourth in the table and with three wins in their past four league outings – the argument that this is a must-win game is harder to make, but bear with me here...

Facing a Sunderland team who are suffering from the worst of both worlds – blunt in attack and pitiful in defence (what a difference from last season...) and have proven all too easy to beat (as their 2-0 home defeat Zagreb illustrated on Thursday) – the west Londoners are expected to win. Fail to return to the capital with the three points and there will once again be question marks over Xabi Alonso’s side. They are flaky and flashy in equal measure, able to play and win well in spurts, but once again unable to mount sustained pressure needed for a title challenge and forced to battle it out for the hope of a top-four spot at best. Those will be the arguments raised should they not win this afternoon.

The hosts doubtless wish that their ‘issues’ were as golden as today’s opposition. For Trai Hume, who scored in this fixture last season, the Sunderland players are at fault for the sorry start to the season and he wants to put right the wrongs so far, starting today.

“I couldn’t tell you what’s changed. We thought we’d addressed it after the Leeds game, where we were aggressive, strong, but we go out there tonight and see the old habits of the start of the season. Everything’s a bit laboured, and it’s something the staff can’t fix, it’s on us as players,” Hume said.

“We’re still together as a club, as a team. I think the run of form we’re on, it would be easy to think we’re not, but we are. We are really upset with how we’ve been playing, and the results don’t lie. We haven’t been good enough and we know that. We have to address that.”

News.title: Liverpool’s expensive attack feast on Palace to leave Sage looking doomed
News.content:
Major signings need to lay down a marker when arriving at Liverpool. Barcola has his hat-trick at LASK in the Champions League, but we are still waiting for a stirring big-match-defining contribution from him since his summer arrival. Arguably the same could be said for Wirtz, nearly 18 months since he joined.

Neither left Selhurst Park looking like the world-beaters they did occasionally for their previous clubs. Still, one misfiring attacker creating a goal for another represents progress and all great partnerships must start somewhere. Lennon and McCartney would improve after 1958’s Too Bad About Sorrows.

If there was ever a place for the least-productive expensively assembled attacking group in the league to find form it was surely south London on this Sunday lunchtime. Liverpool came in with two defeats in their previous two but, European trophy aside, it has been a lousy 2026 for Palace.

They have the most defeats of any ever-present Premier League team and began (and ended) the weekend with the worst defensive record. They have conceded twice as many goals from headers as any other team. Even their most loyal fan group has disbanded.

Alexis Mac Allister opened the scoring in gut-punching fashion, after a series of Palace near-misses. Chairman Steve Parish rubbed his face in the directors’ box, in the style of peak-stress era Guardiola. None of this looked good for Sage, who appears on the brink of dismissal, with Thomas Frank his most likely replacement.

Asked if he expected to remain in his job on the other side of the international break Sage said he deemed his prospects “better than you, I think”.

“We deserved better today,” the Frenchman said. “But football is not about what you deserve it is about how efficient you are and today we had a lack of efficiency”.

News.title: Lando Norris takes pole at Interlagos after chaotic qualifying session
News.content:
McLaren’s Lando Norris claimed pole for the São Paulo Grand Prix for a third consecutive year as he emerged victorious from a marathon, rain-affected qualifying session at Interlagos lasting two and a half hours.

But there was further frustration for his compatriot George Russell, who lashed out at his Mercedes pit wall after being told to abort a push lap in Q3 which he felt would have been good enough to finish qualifying in first place.

Whether Russell was right was debatable, but you could understand his frustration. The Briton has endured a miserable season, dropping from second to fourth in the drivers’ championship in Mexico last weekend after suffering yet another power unit issue.

Russell ended up leaving the Mexico paddock early while team-mate Kimi Antonelli celebrated becoming the sport’s youngest ever champion.

News.title: Man City look to be crumbling after guilty verdict
News.content:
Is this the day the xG gods reward Nottingham Forest? Oliver Glasner’s team sit 19th having won one game all season, but there is no doubt that their performances have been significantly better than results and they might need their luck to turn against Man City team full of firepower.

Despite all of the positive indicators in Forest’s underlying data, Glasner caused some alarm with his comments after last weekend’s defeat at Brentford.

The Austrian said: “We have to accept it’s not good enough. If we lose four of the last five games, it’s not good enough. And that’s why for me, it’s now time that we change things, that I change things, and that’s what I will do.

“I feel now maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff, and it’s always compromises. It’s a clear way. I will tell [the players] what we want to do, what we have to do, and if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround, and if not, the sixth manager [since the start of last season] will come in.”

Dangerous words perhaps when you work for Evangelos Marinakis, but John Percy reported this week that Glasner was backed by his players in a squad meeting.

City are smarting from back-to-back defeats by Aston Villa and Brighton, but they created more than enough in both games to claim some sort of result. Nevertheless, there is a persistent sense that their defensive unit remains too marshmellow-like over the course of 38 games, and Forest have the counter-attacking threat to test them.

Glasner has happy memories of playing City, beating them in the 2025 FA Cup final with Crystal Palace, but his Forest reign is in urgent need of a signature victory and performance.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Rees-Zammit delivers in best position but work to do for sloppy Wales
News.content:
Maybe it is an indication that Wales are improving that this latest close victory over Japan was greeted with a shrug instead of euphoria.

A year ago, almost to the day, Steve Tandy, the Welsh head coach jumped around and hugged his staff, after a one-point win over the Brave Blossoms and there were reports of red-shirted fans in this stadium crying in joy and relief.

Yet that was Wales’s first home success in 10 Tests and, despite the form since hardly raising itself anywhere near levels of excellence, much more was expected on this occasion.

Yes, Tandy’s men prevailed and it was a huge positive to watch player-of-the match Louis Rees-Zammit in great nick on the wing. Nobody should overestimate the Bristol man’s display because the game knows that he can operate even better, but after this there can now be no doubt that he is a wing rather than a full-back. The 25-year-old conjured five line breaks, beat 13 defenders and made 121 metres.

Yet most notably, Rees-Zammit scored his first try for his country in eight matches and that is exactly what he was put on the green-green grass to do. After assisting in fellow wing Josh Adams’s opening try – this other resurgent British and Irish Lion bagged a brace – Rees-Zammit showed his predatory instincts to go over after a wonderful deft offload from centre Eddie James.

Sports.title: Three points from Man Utd’s chaotic draw with Villa as Dalot at point of no return and defensive heart-surgery needed
Sports.content:
Next

THE chaos that comes with Manchester United surpassed all expectations as the final whistle blew in their 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

Alysson and Nicholas Jackson launched a brutal attack on the Red Devils, putting them two behind inside the first four minutes.



Bruno Fernandes’ spot-kick and Youri Tielemans‘ first United goal dragged the hosts level before another two-goal lead was imposed less than ten minutes later.

And if that was not enough, Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu found the back of the net in injury time to help them take a point back to their digs in 18th.



SunSport’s Manchester United reporter Katherine Walsh talked through the three big points from the messy fixture.

FAN PROTESTS

Each Manchester United game just cranks up the heat on the club’s under-fire hierarchy.



New signs, chants, banners, failed walkout plans and tennis balls thrown on to the pitch.

Yesterday, there was a new sign on show that read, “We don’t want a new stadium, we want new owners”.

That was unfurled in the Stretford End, where Red Devils fans still sang boss Michael Carrick’s song.

SunSport was also sent pictures of “F*** the Glazers” spread across gold and green balloons — the colours of the original Newton Heath club.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Several balloons made their way over to the directors’ box in the Sir Bobby Charlton Stand, where director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada tried to ignore the hate.

Frustrated fans made their feelings clear with anti-Glazer hatred aimed at the missing American family, who are seemingly preoccupied with their Tampa Bay NFL team.

And minority co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe — who has his eyes set on a new ‘Wembley of the North’ to replace Old Trafford by 2035 — also faced flak.

How about fixing the issues on the pitch to avoid relegation?



The demonstrations reflected the growing unrest surrounding the club’s direction, with supporters demanding accountability and a clear plan to save the Red Devils from the dreaded drop.

For many supporters, a change in fortunes will not be enough.

LEAKY DEFENCE

United’s entire backline is a total shambles and the club now needs open-heart surgery to fix it.

The Red Devils have shipped 30 goals in all competitions this season — only Lens with 31 have a worse record across Europe’s top five leagues. It is a ­defensive crisis.



Their frontline showed admirable fight to haul them back into the contest against Aston Villa, but it was like trying to win a boxing match with both hands tied behind your back.

Whatever Carrick’s side produce going forward, their defenders look capable of throwing it all away.

They have now conceded 15 goals in their last five games — including a 4-1 humiliation in Como — with a trip to Liverpool now looming after the international break.

A defensive rebuild is promised for summer 2027 and I would struggle to find many who deserve to survive next season.



Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez are all out of contract, while Diogo Dalot has reached the point of no return amid a Joshua Zirkzee-style humiliation.

There were huge, mocking cheers when the Portuguese full-back was replaced by Patrick Dorgu on 66 ­minutes — the Old Trafford reaction was reminiscent of the savage reception handed out to Zirkzee when he was hooked against Newcastle back in 2024.

Dalot was all at sea for Villa’s opener before gifting them a daft penalty shortly after the break.

Yet making him the fall guy misses the bigger picture. Changes are needed across the back, who are without a clean sheet in the league this season.



LACK OF LEADERS

Carrick’s struggling side play off moments, which is unsustainable in the Prem.

It is the hallmark of a side desperately short of structure, leadership and control.

It also explains why the fallen giants have found themselves in the relegation places.

Their attack has stepped up, with Matheus Cunha almost a one-man band, trying to inject the energy and urgency required.

And who would have predicted Danish wideman Dorgu becoming the unlikely saviour?



His goal and assist helped rescue a point and handed Carrick an eight-point haul from ten games.

Bruno Fernandes looked furious at the final whistle despite the comeback, which told its own story.

Even Cunha and Amad Diallo had the audacity to gesture towards the crowd for more noise, despite the wreck unfolding in front of them.

Old Trafford has shown it can roar when given something to believe in — and the players feed off that energy.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But it should not be the supporters’ job to drag the team over the line.

United need to give their fans something to shout about — not keep demanding they help bail them out.



It was Villa who threw this one away.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace ready to sack Pierre Sage after woeful start to season with two immediate frontrunners to replace him
Sports.content:
Next

CRYSTAL PALACE are ready to SACK manager Pierre Sage after just 16 games in charge.

The Frenchman’s future is hanging by a thread following today’s 3-1 defeat to Liverpool at Selhurst Park.



The latest humiliation left the Eagles rock bottom of the Premier League table after a disastrous start to the campaign.

Palace are set to part company with Sage, 47, just five months after appointing him as manager.



And BBC Sport reports that former Tottenham boss Thomas Frank has emerged as a strong contender to replace him, with Sean Dyche another option being considered.

Frank has been out of work since being dismissed by Spurs in February, having previously earned widespread praise for establishing Brentford as a Premier League club.

Meanwhile, Dyche is also available following his departure from Nottingham Forest earlier this year and boasts plenty of experience battling relegation.

Sage arrived at Selhurst Park in June to replace Oliver Glasner, who had guided Palace to historic FA Cup and Europa Conference League triumphs.

But the former Lens boss has endured a nightmare opening to life in English football, with Palace winning just twice in their opening ten league matches.

Sunday’s defeat was their fourth consecutive Premier League loss, while their leaky defence has conceded a staggering 24 goals – the worst record in the division.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Liverpool piled on the misery through goals from Alexis Mac Allister, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak.

Eddie Nketiah grabbed a late consolation from the penalty spot.

The result left Palace bottom of the top flight for the first time after a complete round of fixtures since December 2017.

Palace chairman Steve Parish will now face a huge decision over Sage’s future during the international break.

Sports.title: ‘This just can’t go on’ – Gary Neville fears Man Utd ‘causing themselves emotional damage’ with post-match antics
Sports.content:
Next

GARY NEVILLE revealed his brutal worries concerning Michael Carrick’s Manchester United after their 4-4 thriller with Aston Villa.

The Red Devils trailed the Villans by two goals after just four minutes in their box office clash.



Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans dragged the hosts level, only for a quickfire Villa double after half-time to have them 4-2 down once more.

While two goals from United in injury time meant that both sides took away a point apiece, Neville is concerned about the “emotional damage” they are causing themselves.



After the final whistle blew, Carrick & Co. sauntered around the pitch, clapping the home fans – but the former Prem skipper is not convinced.

The 51-year-old said: “You have got to admire their persistence. They kept going.

“Their defensive errors were shocking.

“I played for Manchester United 602 times. I always appreciated the fans after the game.”

Neville admitted that the post-match “lap of honour”, particularly after the 3-0 Bournemouth result too, was “painful to watch”.

He said: “It’s almost like they’re causing themselves emotional damage.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“This just can’t go on, can it? It’s absolutely desperate.

“Michael will be proud of them.

“The fans are singing his name because they love him, but this is a really sorry situation.”



Before the game, the clash was viewed as a make or break for Carrick, but the draw just might be enough for him to survive the international break.

During the Villa game, Diogo Dalot was booed off by the United fans, but the boss insisted that he’s “giving everything” he’s got.

Carrick said: “We’re all frustrated, we’re all disappointed, and the players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that.

“Diogo, he gives absolutely everything. He’s played in different positions, he’s played left back, he’s played really well at times.

“He gives a penalty away today, he knows that. Maybe he can do a little bit better, all right, that’s part of it, he’s made a mistake, but he cares an awful lot and he’s giving everything.



“So I like what he brings to the team, I like what he brings to the group, I like what he brings to the whole environment and the culture that we’ve got.

“Picking a team and who plays the next game, that’s a whole different decision, but it’s a whole different game that we’ve got to look forward to now.”

United still only have one Premier League win to their name this season from a 5-2 home victory over Ipswich on August 30.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

They now lie 18th in the rankings, knowing that when they return, Liverpool will be waiting.

Following the Anfield fixture, United will travel to Sporting in the Champions League, where they currently sit in the middle of the play-off qualifiers spots after four games.

Sports.title: ‘Got to be careful’ – Michael Carrick warns Man Utd fans over their reaction to Diogo Dalot substitution
Sports.content:
Next

MICHAEL CARRICK has warned Manchester United supporters to “be careful” with how they treat players after Diogo Dalot was booed during the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

Dalot’s 66th-minute substitution with United 4-2 down was wildly cheered by supporters and the right back was then loudly booed as he headed towards the touchline.



The 27-year-old was embraced by substitute Joshua Zirkzee, who received similar treatment when he was hooked in the first half of United’s 2-0 defeat to Newcastle in December 2024.

Dalot started at left back and was culpable for Alysson’s opening goal before he conceded a 47th-minute penalty by tripping the Brazilian at 2-2.



United supporters booed Dalot as he skulked off the pitch after the 3-0 drubbing by Bournemouth last month and he has effectively become the matchgoers’ main scapegoat.

Dalot joined United from Porto in 2018 and is under contract until 2028, with the option of an additional year.

The Portuguese made his 260th United appearance against Villa and he is the squad’s longest servant with Luke Shaw sidelined through injury.

Dalot’s replacement, Patrick Dorgu, nodded in United’s 96th-minute equaliser.

“We’ve got to be careful with that, I think,” Carrick said of the reaction to Dalot’s substitution.

“I understand the frustration, I understand the disappointment of the supporters, so I get it.

“We’re all frustrated, we’re all disappointed, and the players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that.

“Diogo, he gives absolutely everything. He’s played in different positions, he’s played left back, he’s played really well at times.

“He gives a penalty away today, he knows that. Maybe he can do a little bit better, all right, that’s part of it, he’s made a mistake, but he cares an awful lot and he’s giving everything.

“So I like what he brings to the team, I like what he brings to the group, I like what he brings to the whole environment and the culture that we’ve got.

Carrick also confirmed that Harry Maguire was forced off at half-time after suffering a back spasm.

Maguire was replaced by Ayden Heaven, who was booked.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick in tense exchange with Sky Sports reporter as he’s asked whether he would resign as Man Utd manager
Sports.content:
Next

MICHAEL CARRICK will not quit as Manchester United manager despite one win from ten Premier League games.

Although United scored in the 92nd and 96th minute to salvage a remarkable 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford, they are 18th.

With United certain to be in the bottom three for a fortnight during the international break, it will be the longest the club has spent in the relegation zone since October 1986.



The United hierarchy resisted sacking Carrick in the wake of the 3-0 drubbing by Bournemouth a fortnight ago and United have since lost at Chelsea, beaten Roma and drawn with Villa.



Carrick is due to oversee some training sessions at the club’s Carrington training complex this week but his future remains mired in uncertainty.

The 45-year-old gave little away in his post-match debriefs and had a prickly exchange with Sky Sports pitchside reporter Patrick Davison when the topic of Carrick’s future surfaced.

When asked if he could walk away, Carrick stressed: “It’s not going to happen, no.”



Carrick then disputed whether he would hold discussions with chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

At his post-match press conference, Carrick added: “I’m quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in, and it’s got to win games.

“Yeah, 100%, yeah [I’ve seen enough to turn things around]. I think there’s more than enough.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“Goals change games and you’ve got to deal with it, and it’s part of something we have to improve on drastically, but there’s more than enough.



“We’re just making it too difficult for ourselves at the moment in certain times.”

Carrick all but acknowledged that the international break had come at a convenient time for United, who have won three games from 15 this term.

United’s next Premier League fixture is at Liverpool on November 22 before they had to Lisbon to face Sporting in the Champions League.

By the time United kick off at Anfield, they could be bottom. “It’s been a right mixed week, or two or three really, if you’re looking at the events,” Carrick said. “But I’m pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there.

“Obviously some of the boys will be flying off around the world and different things, and the group will be split for 10 days or so.



“But as a normal international week is, you know, we’ll have some training, we’ll have one or two days off, not too much, but we’ll train and we’ll get ready for the next game.”

Sports.title: Man Utd wonderkid Jaydan Kamason accidentally wipes out linesman as u21s clash marred by red card drama
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED youngster Jaydan Kamason accidentally clattered the linesman during a youth match.

The 19-year-old was playing for United‘s Under-21 side against Burnley on Sunday when the unfortunate incident happened.



The full-back had received a cross-field pass from a team-mate in the 31st minute but mis-controlled the ball with his head.

He was forced to chase after the ball to stop it from going out for a Burnley throw-in.



Kamason did keep it in play, but ended up wiping out the poor man standing next to the touchline.

The wonderkid had slid towards the ground and took the linesman with him.



Kamason immediately stood up and tried to help the official to his feet and even handed him his flag.

The linesman initially looked like he had picked up an injury as he tried out his left leg.

But he was fine to continue after consulting with a fellow official on the touchline.

It was only the first moment of drama in the game as United went on to draw the game and finish with ten players.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

United were 1-0 up at the time of the linesman incident after Benedito Mantato’s early opener.

Kamason was one of United’s best players and should have had an assist when his cross found Jim Thwaites, but he could only fire against the bar.

Burnley then equalised through Zach Johnson after unleashing a rocket into the top corner.

But United’s game unravelled when defender Daniel Armer was given a straight red card for lunging in on an opponent.

Kamason did have a chance to win the game after striking at goal after a mazy run, but was thwarted by keeper Lewis Forshaw.

Sports.title: Fans furious at missed Morgan Rogers incident in Chelsea defeat to Sunderland and ask ‘why did VAR not review this’
Sports.content:
Next

FANS fumed that Morgan Rogers should have been sent off against Sunderland after footage emerged of the Chelsea star appearing to knee an opponent.

And Rogers, 24, has a contentious history with the Black Cats star involved in the incident.



The Blues lost 1-0 to a Sunderland side who began the day bottom of the Premier League table.

Things could have gotten even worse for Xabi Alonso and Co, had Rogers been penalised for a controversial moment.



During a break in play, the England international walked back into position.

In footage that has since circulated on social media, Rogers can be seen appearing to knee Trai Hume in the head.



It is not clear whether Rogers meant to do so.

Hume, 24, immediately held the back of his head – while team-mate Thomas Meunier came over to defend his colleague.

The match VAR opted against taking any action following the incident.

Commentator Don Hutchison then claimed of Rogers: “He knows exactly [what he’s doing]. When you’re walking across there as a player, you’ve only got one intention if you’re going to knee someone in the head.”

Many fans were also left seething with the incident.

One fumed on X: “That was a straight red card”.

And a second asked: “why did VAR not review this?”

A third alleged: “Morgan Rogers knows exactly what he is doing here on Trai Hume”.

Another added: “what’s the point in VAR?”



Rogers was involved in a contentious incident with Hume last season while playing for Aston Villa.

During a match in September 2025, Rogers was sent flying by Hume as Villa took on Sunderland at the Stadium of Light.

The Black Cats subsequently posted a clip of the crunching challenge to Instagram, with the caption: “Still got the ball”.

Rogers hit back on his Instagram Story, writing: “Great message to send out… dangerous tackles getting highlight reels”.

Sports.title: 'Not many sports teams have done it' - Wolff 'proud' of Mercedes turnaround
Sports.content:
Toto Wolff says he's "proud" of Mercedes' turnaround to win the 2026 Formula 1 Constructors' Championship and feels very few sports teams have bounced back so quickly.

Mercedes won their ninth constructors' title on Sunday at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, five years after their last championship, which was their eighth in a row at the time.

Regulation changes in 2022 ended Mercedes' dominance as they struggled to get on top of the so-called ground effect cars, but they have won the first season of the new 2026 cars, and also wrapped up the Drivers' Championship earlier this month with Kimi Antonelli.

"The thing is when you are in these difficult moments, like we all are sometimes in our lives, it's not that easy to keep going," said Wolff.

"Looking back in retrospect, you're saying, 'we needed these tough moments in order to grow as people or to grow as an organisation'. But when you're down, that is quite difficult to feel.

"I think those last four years were very difficult between getting it wrong, then kind of understanding why it was wrong and then realising no we didn't understand. That was a bit back and forth.

"But we will be looking back in 10 or 20 years. When you look at the statistics, it wasn't that we were complete losers over those four years, because we finished second, (second), third, fourth [in the championship], we won races, won many races. So it wasn't that bad at all when you look at the sheer numbers, but it felt not good."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Toto Wolff reacts to Mercedes winning the Constructors' Championship in Brazil

As Wolff points out, Mercedes still won races between 2022 and 2025, with George Russell and Lewis Hamilton winning seven Grands Prix between them.

"The resilience of the team, the people that held together in those tough times, is a factor, I think," continued Wolff.

"It feels really good sealing those two titles. Not many sports teams have done that after consecutive run of championships, then a difficult spell and then coming back, so I'm really proud that we are part of this very small group of teams that have done that in all sports."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Sao Paulo Grand Prix

Wolff: Mercedes has 2,500 superstars

Mercedes move level with Williams on nine constructors' titles - only McLaren (10) and Ferrari (16) have more in Formula 1 history.

Wolff says his pride comes from the hard work in Mercedes' UK factories in Brackley and Brixworth to produce the best car, on average, this season.

"Sometimes the drivers, or myself, we are so visible because we are in in front of the TV cameras, but there's so many people that are part of this," he told Sky Sports F1.

"I always say there are not two superstars, the drivers, but there are 2,500 superstars, all of them delivering a great job, being all of us contributing to such a championship."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli reacts to Mercedes claiming their ninth world constructors championship

Mercedes were unable to finish with either of their drivers on the podium in Brazil as Lando Norris dominated in mixed conditions, while Antonelli and Russell both spun.

Russell finished in fourth, just ahead of Antonelli who says everyone at Mercedes "deserves" this year's success.

"They have done an incredible year and it's an amazing group of people, who push every day to do their best and give us the best opportunity to fight for wins and championships," the Italian told Sky Sports F1.

"This year they have done an incredible job and that's why they deserve this championship and we will enjoy it together."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell says Mercedes would've liked to win the Constructors' Championship title in style after both cars finished fourth and fifth respectively

Russell added: "We achieved what we came here to do and won the Constructors' Championship. We would have liked to have done it in a bit more style, but it's an incredible achievement for everyone in the team.

"We've had four difficult years and the whole organisation put so much work into getting us back into this position. When I joined Mercedes in 2022, we hoped we'd be fighting for championships regularly, so to have gone through that journey and now get back to the top is something we should all be incredibly proud of."

Sports.title: Hamilton says he overrode Ferrari pit call due to 'lack of information'
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says a lack of information led to him overriding Ferrari's call for him to come into the pits as rain fell during the closing stages of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

Hamilton was running in eighth at Interlagos when heavy rain began to fall with 10 laps to go. While the leaders had already passed the pit entry by the time the rain intensified, Mercedes brought in George Russell from fifth.

Ferrari instructed Hamilton to come in, but he decided to do the opposite to the car just in front of him at the time, Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson. Hamilton's team-mate Charles Leclerc, running just behind him, came into the pits.

The seven-time world champion spun on the next lap in the treacherous conditions, before pitting at the end of it to follow his rivals onto intermediates.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

While there was little at stake, as Hamilton ultimately finished ninth rather than claiming what could have been seventh if he had got past Lawson, it was the latest example of imperfect execution from the British driver and his Italia team.

Speaking to Sky Italy after the race, Hamilton said: "The last bit of information I got was that the rain was going to stay the same, and in those conditions my grip was feeling pretty good.

"And I was like, 'ah, I'm catching.' And I was coming out the last corner, just before the pit lane they asked me to box, and I was right behind Lawson.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following a disappointing race, Lewis Hamilton reflects on 'tough' Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

"He went in, and I ended up staying (out). They didn't say it's raining more in the first half of the lap. If I'd have known that I would have come in.

"As soon as I got to Turn 1, I realised it was wet. So, it just lacked a little bit of information there.

"And ultimately, that's on me. Sorry for the team, for that. I gave it everything. We just didn't have the pace today unfortunately."

'A really tough day for the whole team'

Hamilton had come into the weekend off the back of a major controversy with his team-mate in Mexico last weekend, as he was angered by a first-lap clash between the pair that he felt cost him victory and the team a one-two.

While Hamilton revealed on Saturday that the pair had "squashed" their issues, the precious nature of their winning opportunity in Mexico City was highlighted by their struggles in Brazil.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari Team Principal Fred Vasseur answers questions about Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc after a public spat between the two,

Both Hamilton and Leclerc were compromised by grid penalties that saw them start from 20th and 14th, respectively, but neither appeared to have the pace to match McLaren's race winner Lando Norris or Red Bull's Max Verstappen in second.

Hamilton told Sky Sports F1: "Really tough day and weekend for the whole team. They have done a really great job.

"All the mechanics did such a great job switching out the engine and making sure the car was as good as it could be."

Hamilton had a great start as he climbed to ninth on the first lap, and successfully pulled off being the first driver to switch from intermediates to slicks as the track dried early in the race, but didn't have the pace to take advantage of either moment.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli passes Lando Norris for the lead in the opening lap at Sao Paulo GP.

He added: "We struggled in the dry but I had a great start. Unfortunately, the rear tyres just ballooned and overheated and I struggled.

"After that, I was pushing to go onto the slicks, which I eventually got on, I think I was one of the earlier ones [to switch to that tyre].

"I was feeling pretty good. It was very tricky in those conditions. We ended up having an extra stop, which ultimately, I had a lot of ground to cover there."

Sports.title: Norris wins wet Sao Paulo GP as Mercedes seal constructors' title
Sports.content:
McLaren's Lando Norris recovered from a poor start to claim a dominant victory in a wet Sao Paulo Grand Prix that saw Mercedes seal the 2026 Formula 1 Constructors' Championship.

Max Verstappen produced a signature stunning drive in the wet to come from 21st on the grid to finish second, with his team-mate Isack Hadjar completing a double-podium for Red Bull.

Newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli had looked on course for victory after taking the lead at the start but ultimately had to settle for fifth behind his team-mate George Russell, which was more than enough for Mercedes to establish an unassailable lead over Ferrari in the constructors' standings with three rounds to spare.

A ninth constructors' title for Mercedes, their first since claiming eight in a row from 2014-2021, brings the Silver Arrows level with Williams in third on the sport's all-time list of winners.

"It's amazing," Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said. "We have taken a few years to be back at the top spot. Not many teams have been able to come back from such a situation and it just shows the great work, the great people we have in our organisation and it's great to be among them."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes party on the podium after sealing their ninth Constructors' Championship title.

Norris lost the lead to Antonelli at the start as the pole-sitter dropped to third on the opening lap, but a early-race switch to slick tyres as the track dried swung the race.

Antonelli had led by six seconds before the stops but delayed pitting by a lap and then struggled with his tyre temperatures, spinning off to give the lead back to Norris before also being overtaken by both Red Bulls.

The rain returned in the closing stages to force the entire field back onto intermediate tyres, but Norris handled the conditions masterfully to take the chequered flag just short of 15 seconds clear of Verstappen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli loses the lead by going off track twice to slip to third.

"It was a very tough race, very very tough," Norris said. "I didn't have the best of launches off the line. A lot of challenges today with the conditions and going onto slicks in the wet is always tough, especially when you are pushing for the lead and trying to catch up a little bit.

"The main thing today was I kept it cool and didn't make any mistakes and had the pace when I needed to. Nice to be back on the top step and what a place to do it as well."

Sao Paulo GP Result: Top 10 1) Lando Norris, McLaren



2) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



3) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



4) George Russell, Mercedes



5) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



6) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



7) Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls



8) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari*



9) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



10) Nico Hulkenberg, Audi



*Leclerc demoted a position by five-second penalty

Norris' team-mate Oscar Piastri claimed sixth, which meant McLaren matched Red Bull's haul of 33 points from the race and stayed 17 points behind them in the battle for third in the constructors' standings.

Charles Leclerc finished seventh after passing Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson during a final-lap scrap, but their positions were reversed as the Ferrari driver was given a five-second penalty for causing a collision between the pair during the overtake.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc and Liam Lawson touch on lap 70 as they battle for seventh!

Lewis Hamilton surged from 20th on the grid up to ninth on the first lap, but was ultimately unable to improve on that position after struggling for pace amid a couple of tyre gambles as the conditions changed.

Nico Hulkenberg took the final point in 10th for Audi, holding onto the position despite having to serve a penalty late in the race for forcing Alpine's Franco Colapinto off track in an earlier battle.

Rafael Camara was last of the cars to take the chequered flag in 20th for Haas as he made his grand prix debut at his home race following the team's fall out with Esteban Ocon at last weekend's race in Mexico City.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris shatters champagne bottle after attempting his trademark podium celebration after winning Sao Paulo GP.

Norris stages recovery to return to winning ways

Having been the only team to bring a significant upgrade to Brazil at this late stage of the season, McLaren arrived in Sao Paulo hopeful of taking a step forward.

Norris had taken full advantage of the team's earlier upgrades to win back-to-back races either side of F1's summer break, but after being unlucky to miss out a third victory in Madrid, the Woking squad's pace has faded.

The Brit was adamant that the wet conditions qualifying took place in on Saturday were more crucial than the upgrades in enabling him to take pole, and he got his wish as the rain returned on Sunday.

However, the start was far from ideal as a poor getaway saw him fall behind both Antonelli and Lawson, who was starting from third after being promoted by grid penalties for several others.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli passes Lando Norris for the lead in the opening lap at Sao Paulo GP.

It wasn't until lap six that Norris got his tyres working well enough to pass Lawson, but he was still losing time to Antonelli, who at one point extended his lead beyond eight seconds.

As the track dried, Norris began to close the gap, before Hamilton became the first driver to switch from intermediates to soft slick tyres at the end of lap 14.

Reacting to Hamilton's strong pace, Norris pitted on lap 16, while leader Antonelli opted to stay out.

That proved to be a mistake from Mercedes as when Antonelli pitted a lap later, he came out only a second ahead of Norris, with the McLaren driver's tyres fired up and working much better than the leaders.

Just a week on from becoming F1's youngest ever world champion, the 20-year-old sounded distressed over team radio as he expressed concern that his car wasn't working properly.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris wins the Sao Paulo GP ahead of Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar.

That soon told as he spun off at Turn 1, allowing Norris to ease into the lead, and soon allowing the Red Bulls to follow through.

Norris never looked like relinquishing the lead from that moment, showing consistently strong pace to extend his lead before calmly managing the switch back to intermediates with 10 laps to go.

Verstappen is renowned for his pace in the wet, but Norris was more than a match in the final stages, maintaining and then extending his lead to join the Dutchman and Russell on three race wins for the season.

Verstappen the star of 'reverse grid' race

Unlike some of its junior categories, F1 has not introduced a reverse grid race, where cars start in the opposite order that they have qualified.

However, there was something of a 'reverse' feel to Sunday's grid with several of the drivers at the top of the championship serving penalties for exceeding their engine part allowance for the season.

Hamilton and Verstappen were starting from 20th and 21st respectively, with Russell seventh and Leclerc 14th.

Hamilton made an incredible start to jump to ninth on the first lap, while Verstappen wasn't far behind, slotting into 10th behind the Ferrari by lap three.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Karun Chandhok looks at how Max Verstappen went from 21st to 2nd at Interlagos.

A mistake from Hamilton allowed Verstappen past, and from that point on their races went in vastly different directions.

While Hamilton struggled for pace and had to give back one of the positions he'd gained illegally on the first lap from Haas' Oliver Bearman, Verstappen continued to surge forward.

The four-time world champion was soon up to fifth, and was gifted another place as Russell spun in the pit lane on his way back out to the track having switched to slick tyres.

Antonelli's struggles gave him another place, before Red Bull ordered Hadjar to allow his team-mate past on lap 38 as Verstappen closed in.

While there was no victory this time around, Verstappen made it eight podiums in a row and 10 in his last 11 races, a run of form that is likely to see the 29-year-old go into the winter as the favourite for next year's title.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen says that despite his progression from P21 to P2 at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, his car was 'not working'.

"It was a challenging race," Verstappen said. "The first few laps were, of course, very important and I overtook a lot of cars. Actually, that first stint on the stints was very, very strong.

"Unfortunately, after that, I don't know if we picked up some kind of damage, because the car felt like the complete opposite I've felt the whole weekend with some really weird balance.

"Once I got into P2 I couldn't really make any inroads. So, we have to understand what went wrong there but, I mean, starting in P21 and being on the podium in second is a very good result."

Other candidates that Palace are interested in include Frank Lampard, Sean Dyche, Vitor Pereira, Kim Hellberg, Vitor Matos and Tony Popovic.
