No decision has been taken at Palace yet, but Sage is likely to lose his position following a seventh league defeat of the season.

Frank is amongst a list of names that Palace considered in the summer. The former Brentford boss is expected to be among the frontrunners if as expected the club decide to make a managerial change.

Frank had great success at Brentford during his seven-year spell between 2018 and 2025, getting the Bees into the Premier League and then establishing them as a top-flight club, reaching a ninth-place finish in 2023.

He then moved to Tottenham last season to replace Ange Postecolgou as head coach, but was sacked after less than eight months in charge with the club in 16th place, five points above the relegation zone.

Image: Frank's time at Tottenham was littered with setbacks

Spurs only sealed survival from relegation on the final day of last season, after Igor Tudor and Roberto De Zerbi replaced Frank as head coach.

Frank failed to win over the Tottenham faithful, with his short tenure littered with setbacks, including drinking from a coffee cup which carried the badge of rivals Arsenal.

Carragher expects Palace to sack Sage

Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher speaking after Palace's 3-1 loss to Liverpool:

"I think that would have been one of the best Crystal Palace performances this season. Liverpool won 3-1 away from home but their goalkeeper was their best player. That tells you how well Palace did.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Crystal Palace’s match against Liverpool in the Premier League.

"But I don't think you can hang your hat on the performance, especially with a new guy into the Premier League. He's really struggled so far.

"I don't think you can take the risk as an owner when you think of the finances involved. Palace - 14 seasons in the Premier League, we don't expect them to be [bottom]. They're an established Premier League club.

"I think the decision will be made, unfortunately for Pierre Sage. I think Palace will have a new manager the next time they play in the Premier League"

Sage: 'We haven't had our rewards'

Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage to Sky Sports after the loss to Liverpool:

"I always say the same thing about what we deserve and what we have.

"We start really well, we create a lot of chances but without scoring and taking this goal [against] after a set-piece with the consequence of transition, it's really difficult against Liverpool because they have a lot of speed and are really efficient in transition.

"That's why we suffered more in the second half. We tried to make it 1-1 but we left too much space and they took it.

"Football is about efficiency. If we create these chances, it's a good step. But the next step is to score. If not, it's as [if] you did nothing.

"I'm really frustrated, especially for the fans and the players, because I think we're able to do better."

Sports.title: Man Utd in relegation zone but boss Carrick 'expects' to stay on
Sports.content:
Under-pressure Manchester United boss Michael Carrick "expects" to stay on despite his side sitting in the relegation zone after Sunday's dramatic 4-4 home draw against Aston Villa.

Man Utd scored twice in stoppage time to rescue an unlikely point against Villa, but the draw leaves Carrick's side third-bottom and a point from safety.

Man Utd's 18th-place position is their lowest after 10 top-flight games since 1986/87, when they were 20th.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Manchester United and Aston Villa

The draw against Villa extends Man Utd's winless run in the league to eight games - a club record in the Premier League era - raising further doubts over Carrick's position heading into the two-week November international break.

When questioned on his future by Sky Sports' Patrick Davison, Carrick engaged in a tetchy back-and-forth, insisting he would remain in charge.

PD: "What do you expect to happen over the next few weeks? If you thought walking away was the best thing, you'd probably do it."

MC: "It's not going to happen, no."

PD: "What do you expect to happen? Clearly there's going to be conversation?

MC: "Is there?"

PD: "You would assume so, right?

MC: "Would you?"

PD: "What do you think, Michael?"

MC: "You're telling me what you think, aren't you?"

PD: "I'm asking you what you think? What do you expect to happen?"

MC: "We understand the situation; we haven't won enough games. But I expect to move forward and keep working on things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good in the game today, tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Man Utd fans show their love for Michael Carrick at full-time after the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa

Then, speaking in his post-match press conference, Carrick expressed confidence his side could still turn things around this season.

"One hundred per cent," he said. "I think there's more than enough. Goals change games and we've got to deal with it and it's something we have to improve on drastically. But there's more than enough, we're just making it too difficult for ourselves at the moment in certain times…

"I'm quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in. We've just got to win games."

"Football is about moments, football is about what happens in both boxes in the end," Carrick added.

"Take (away) the moments and the totally avoidable goals we've given away, I actually thought we played pretty well, we were the better team for the most part and I'm disappointed we haven't won the game."

Neville: 'Ownership don't have a clue what to do' on Carrick

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Gary Neville, speaking on NBC, delivered a scathing assessment of Manchester United's leadership

Sky Sports' Gary Neville on NBC:

"You can keep changing the manager and thinking that's going to be the answer. But this has been proven now over eight managers in 12 years - that's not the answer.

"Michael could leave, Michael might stay, we don't know. The ownership don't have a clue what to do.

"It's rinse and repeat. (Ruben) Amorim, (Erik) Ten Hag, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Carrick, Jose Mourinho, Louis van Gaal, David Moyes, Ralf Rangnick - some of them are world-class managers who have had success; there are a lot of promising young managers there, ex-players who know the club as well.

"None of it has worked because if you recruit badly, if you've got a poor performance department, a poor recruitment department, you've not got leadership that is strong right through the spine of the football club, you will fail.

"Every organisation in the world will fail if you've not got an aligned leadership from top to bottom - your board and your ownership right the way through to the person who is stood on the pitch trying to play football.

"There are real issues within that football club; you've got people doing those jobs who have never done those jobs before in senior positions."

Keane: 'Politician' Carrick 'better get moving' on improvements

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ex-Man Utd players Roy Keane and Ashley Young discuss whether top players would still consider joining the club

Sky Sports' Roy Keane:

"It's obviously difficult for the manager. Under pressure, no doubt. He talks a lot but doesn't say much. I don't know if that's a tactic. Like a politician.

"He keeps saying we need to tighten up and there's things we need to work on, but they better get moving on that.

"It's the worst start in how many years; all these stats aren't very good. If you keep giving up goals and chances, it's just going to continue.

"What are we expecting to change over the next few weeks and months? What are they working on? They need to do a lot better than that.

"I admire people who are maybe casual. I wish I was casual like that! I see Carrick, and he's like, 'We just have to tighten up'. I'm going, 'Tighten up? You should be banging heads!'

"We're all different, but put it this way, they're going to Liverpool in a few weeks. How many chances are Liverpool going to get? I don't think this is a top Liverpool team, but do you believe United are going to roll their sleeves up and get a clean sheet? Dig in deep? Be hard to beat? Start quick? Well, good luck with that one.

"I don't see that as an honest dressing room. The really top players put demands on each other. They all seem to be tiptoeing around each other.

"They are certainly lacking leaders in the dressing room."

Sports.title: Villa boss Emery explains why he went down tunnel before full-time
Sports.content:
A prickly Unai Emery claimed he headed down the Old Trafford tunnel after Manchester United's late equaliser against his Aston Villa side because he thought the match was about to end.

Villa threw away two separate two-goal leads to draw 4-4 with United in a Super Sunday thriller - but the 97th-minute equaliser from Michael Carrick's side, scored by Patrick Dorgu, brought about a strange reaction from Emery.

The Villa manager was seen walking down the tunnel before the full-time whistle, with the match continuing for another two minutes before it ended.

Image: Unai Emery went down the Old Trafford tunnel before the full-time whistle

Villa have complained about the legitimacy of United's fourth goal - with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens accused of impeding with Villa counterpart Zion Suzuki as he competed with Dorgu for the corner.

Asked if Emery walking down the tunnel was due to the emotional about the goal standing "No emotion. They scored in minute 96 and there were six minutes added. I [thought] the match was finishing."

When asked if he felt the goal being awarded was unfair, Emery replied: "No, no. Not unfair. Please.

"They scored the goal in minute 96. You were making the question [about why] I left before. Because the minute 96 and 30 seconds, was when we started the kick-off."

Full transcript of Emery's prickly interview

Sky reporter Patrick Davison: Does today happen because you're a new team or young side? It is an experience they have to learn from?

Unai Emery: "I don't know."

PD: Does history play a part, we spoke before the match that Aston Villa don't have a good record here.

UE: "We are in our way and we might be positive, even with this defeat [draw]. We have to be moving on with the process we have."

PD: We saw you left...

UE: "More, more, more questions?"

PD: Last one Unai, we saw you left before the end while VAR were...

UE: "They scored in minute 96!"

PD: Just emotion?

UE: "No emotion. They scored in minute 96 and there were six minutes added. I think the match was finishing."

PD: You brought something up that I wasn't expecting. Did you think the goal was unfair?

UE: "No, no. Not unfair. Please."

PD: Ok, I'm listening.

UE: "They scored the goal in minute 96. You were making the question [about why] I left before. Because the minute 96 and 30 seconds, was when we started the kick-off.

"My English is so poor, but it's clear or not?"

PD: No, you've explained it well.

UE: "Ok. Thank you, thank you very much. More questions?"

PD: No all done.

UE: "No? Thank you very much. Have a good Sunday."

Villa chief complains about equaliser standing

Villa's director of football operations Damian Vidagany took to social media to show his dismay at United's last-gasp equaliser against his team being allowed to stand.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Roy Keane and Ashley Young analyse whether Senne Lammens impeded Zion Suzuki in the build-up to Manchester Utd's late equaliser against Aston Villa.

United goalkeeper Lammens - who went up for the corner - made contact with Suzuki whilst not looking at the ball, which left Villa furious. VAR checked and cleared Lammens' involvement in the goal.

Sky Sports' Roy Keane says "football is a contact sport" which means the goal should be allowed to stand.

However, Vidagany posted on X: "To put in context this convenient narrative of 'contact sport' we've been told by referees during the summer that this season to go to unbalance or push the GK on purpose on the six-yard box was not going to be allowed anymore.

"Lammens did not even look at the ball, went straight to do a contact with the hip over Zion.

"Having said that we played good match and we must do better than last six minutes. We will do and we will improve.

"But the rules are the rules and must be respected. That is a fact."

Is Emery angry with his players?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Manchester United and Aston Villa.

Emery admitted his anger at seeing Villa throw away their significant advantages at Old Trafford - but revealed his anger was not directed at his players.

"Angry, of course," he said in his press conference. "To accept to lose in the last minutes two goals, it is difficult.

"I am angry for the situation, not with the players. We lost the opportunity to have two points more."

Asked how United were allowed to come back into the game, Emery replied: "They did the same here against Roma with the supporters pushing, they were playing with heart.

"The last moments when we were close to finishing the match, with [Patrick] Dorgu left side, we couldn't defend him good.

"The last corner we were focusing on the adaptation, protecting them to try to avoid the block. Zion [Suzuki] is going to improve, adapting to the Premier League, but during the process we conceded one more.

"But Zion is very fantastic how he is performing."

The tech-infused golf league sees LPGA Tour stars feature in a unique team format, following on from the success of the men's competition, with all players mic'd up and every match being played at SoFi Center - a purpose-built indoor venue in Florida.

Five teams feature in the inaugural season, each having a five-team roster, with Atlanta Drive GC, Boston Common Golf, Los Angeles Golf Club, Motor City Golf Club and New York Golf Club all involved.

Teams play 15 holes of golf each match, divided into two sessions, with nine holes of triples - three against three playing alternate shots - and six holes of head-to-head singles golf.

Sports.title: Borthwick and Itoje reject reports of England squad rift - 'Not accurate'
Sports.content:
England head coach Steve Borthwick and captain Maro Itoje have rejected claims made in a newspaper article this week of a squad rift, saying it "does not represent the environment" they recognise.

Speaking to media following Sunday's dominant 45-22 Nations Championship victory over Australia at Allianz Stadium Twickenham, Borthwick addressed the article for the first time since its publication on Friday.

Within it, The Times reported that some England players lost faith in Borthwick during a summer campaign which included a 45-21 defeat to world champions South Africa and a nervy win over Argentina.

It is alleged players objected to Borthwick's treatment of them, that he was involved in a training ground bust-up with Ellis Genge and that they wanted RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney - who this week unequivocally backed the head coach - to listen to their gripes.

Speaking to Sky Sports on Friday, Jamie George said England's players were "hurt" by the report, calling the timing of the article "shocking."

On Sunday, Borthwick said: "It's not an environment I recognise. It's not an accurate reflection.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Steve Borthwick praises 'excellent' Henry Pollock after a standout performance on the wing for England against Australia.

"What I will say is that in the last couple of days, a number of my predecessors have reached out and contacted me, and they certainly did.

"They're always supportive, and I won't name who they are, but a number of them reached out to me and the basic gist of it is: 'Been there, got the t-shirt, focus on the rugby', and that's it.

"As England head coach you get that t-shirt, and what you do is focus on the rugby and that's what I've done this week, that's what the players have done, that's what every member of the staff around the players has done.

"That's what we've done this week."

Itoje: We have full support in Borthwick

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie George told Sky Sports England's players were hurt by the 'shocking' report of a rift with Borthwick

Sat next to Borthwick at Sunday's post-match press conference, England skipper Itoje gave a passionate defence of his head coach.

"From a player's point of view, we have full support in Steve," he said.

"I've had the privilege of Steve being my coach since 2016, with a little gap when he was in his Leicester years. That's not the man I recognise. The article doesn't represent the environment I recognise, and I think if you speak to players over his coaching career they will say a different story.

"Particularly, often you think about players from other countries. If you speak to some of those guys from the 2017 Lions tour [to New Zealand], they'll tell you about the impact Steve had on them.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Henry Pollock spoke on his change in position during the Rugby Union game between England and Australia.

"Those guys aren't English I'm talking about, I'm talking about the Irish guys, I'm talking about the Welsh guys who he had the pleasure of coaching and having an influence on.

"Just from a player's point of view, as always there's things that we want to get right, there's things that we try and put on the field, sometimes for whatever reason it doesn't quite click. I think often too much criticism is attached to the coach.

"Whereas, no matter how well Steve coaches us, we as players are the ones on the field. We as players are the ones who have to perform and put it right.

"There's been times where we haven't quite done that which has put a bit of pressure on him. I'm delighted that today we were able to get the win. He's a world-class coach and we're lucky to have him."

What's next?

For England, they next face Japan in their second Nations Championship Test of the autumn at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham on Saturday November 14 (4.40pm kick-off).

Sports.title: Dorgu rescues point for Manchester United in eight-goal thriller against Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Does this late, late comeback draw keep Michael Carrick in his job? He urged United to back up their breathless Roma comeback victory on Tuesday by building momentum and they did, kind of, by avoiding defeat.

Patrick Dorgu’s 96th-minute equaliser went off his head and in. Senne Lammens, up for the corner, knocked into his opposite number, Zion Suzuki, but no foul was given – to Unai Emery’s disquiet, Aston Villa’s manager pointing to this afterwards. This made it 4-4 to follow Joshua Zirkzee’s added-time finish as Villa were somehow pulled back by Carrick’s chaotic unit.

Chris Kavanagh soon blew for time but not before further bedlam as the referee sent off what appeared to be a member of Villa’s technical staff.

Before all of this Lammens (twice), Diogo Dalot and Leny Yoro were ­culpable for Villa’s goals. What can any manager do if a trio of players shoot the team in both feet with the schoolboy defending that allowed Alysson to score a barely credible 59 seconds in, and Nicolas Jackson to double the lead after four minutes?

Both these goals were ­Lammens’s fault. Then, after a rousing Roma‑esque first-half comeback to make it 2-2 via Bruno Fernandes and Youri ­Tielemans, Dalot’s chop on ­Alysson two minutes into the second period conceded the season’s clearest ­penalty, which John McGinn dispatched. Further farce followed via Yoro’s own what-are-you-doing moment: a ­flying header towards his own net that led to Leon Goretzka’s fourth goal for Emery’s team.

The bottom line is that United have still won three games all season, from 15, and only one of these in the league, on 30 August, when Ipswich were beaten 5-2.

Carrick may well cling on because Jason Wilcox has been reluctant to fire the head coach so far. Yet United enter the international break in a ­bewildering 18th place, so who knows? Carrick cuffed away a post‑match question that asked if he might walk away – for the good of the club. “I’m not,” was his curt reply.

For two minutes and 46 seconds his team were actually bottom of the table earlier in the day, when Sunderland went 1-0 up against Chelsea and before Liverpool took the lead at Crystal Palace.

The toxicity towards the United owners was summed up in the message, held up in letters and displayed in the Stretford End, to the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe: “Your funeral not ours, sell up”.

Villa’s lightning start was uber-professional from them and dismally amateurish from United: the ball arrived with Alysson and his shot went through Lammens’s legs.

United’s No 1 was in the dock again when Alysson’s effort went to ­the Belgian’s left and he pushed it out to Jackson, who smashed in for 2-0.

The joke beforehand was that even United could not lose by the 10‑goal margin needed to end the day in 20th place. The joke now was that United were in “hold my beer” territory.

Could they get a grip and retrieve a two-goal deficit, as they did ­versus Roma? Matheus Cunha, who scored twice against the Italian side, made a ­barnstorming charge into the right of Villa’s area that caused Boubacar Kamara to upend him. Kavanagh awarded the penalty and so ­Fernandes, as he did versus Roma, had the chance from the spot to pull a first goal back.

A hop-and-skip later it was game on again, Suzuki guessing the wrong way. This was 16 minutes in and the confusing rabble that is Carrick’s United took over as Villa were then pummelled until half-time.

View image in fullscreen Leon Goretzka bundles home Aston Villa’s fourth goal from close range. Photograph: Darren Staples/AFP/Getty Images

United were all they had not been in the calamitous opening four ­minutes: slick, fast, and in charge in a 20-minute passage of pressure that was finally broken when Villa escaped their half, Pau Torres heading McGinn’s free-kick over.

United continued on. Their energy impressed and it said they still believed – in rescuing the match, and Carrick. Hard evidence arrived with Tielemans’s equaliser as Villa folded precisely as United had. Noussair Mazraoui’s cross came to the Belgian and he beat Suzuki. So, at the interval, the contest was all square after a breakneck opening half.

Quick Guide How do I 

What might the second period ­conjure? The answer: Dalot’s ­feeble trip on Alysson, as Carrick was a ­picture of despair. McGinn converted, to Lammens’s right, and it was 3-2 to Villa.

They stretched their advantage further due to more ­slapstick play from United. McGinn floated in a free-kick from the right, Yoro’s header forced ­Lammens to tip the ball on to the frame of the goal, and it rebounded and ­Goretzka ­bundled in.

Carrick had not found a place for Shea Lacey despite his impact as a substitute against Roma but on 65 minutes the head coach did, the youngster joined by Dorgu and Mason Mount in a triple change.

Tielemans, Amad Diallo and Dalot came off and the Portuguese seemed to be jeered: if so a rare occurrence here for United to boo one of their own. Then came Zirkzee and Dorgu’s goals that grabbed a point for United.

“Sacked in the morning” had been the Villa support’s taunt of Carrick. We wait to see if this is prescient. It is a 50‑50 shot, maybe.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace poised to sack Pierre Sage and target Frank after Liverpool defeat
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace are poised to sack Pierre Sage after Sunday’s defeat by Liverpool left them bottom of the Premier League for the first time since December 2017, with Thomas Frank emerging as the main candidate to succeed him.

The Frenchman, appointed in mid-June to replace Oliver Glasner, has been under mounting pressure since a 5-0 defeat by Brighton last month. There have been few signs of improvement as Palace have slumped to four successive league defeats.

Sage has guided Palace to only two wins from their 10 Premier League games this season and they have the league’s worst defensive record, with 24 goals conceded so far. Although there were promising moments during the 3-1 defeat by Liverpool at Selhurst Park on Sunday, their habit of conceding goals from set pieces has not been rectified and it is understood the patience of the club’s hierarchy has worn thin despite Sage only being at the helm for 16 matches.

He is expected to become the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season on Monday. Palace are already believed to have started the process of bringing in his replacement. Frank, who was dismissed by Tottenham in February, spoke to Palace in the summer and is said to be keen for a new challenge after a successful spell at Brentford.

The former Nottingham Forest manager Sean Dyche also has his backers at Palace and would be seen as a safe pair of hands given his vast experience in the Premier League. Vítor Pereira, another former Forest manager, could be an alternative.

Sage signed a three-year contract in south London after leaving Lens, where he won the Coupe de France and qualified for the Champions League in his final season. Palace have lost their two main central defenders this year, Marc Guéhi moving to Manchester City in January and Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea in the summer. Two loan players – Axel Disasi and the teenager Honest Ahanor – were signed as replacements. Palace did not land one of Sage’s top targets, Malick Fofana.

Sage denied after the Liverpool game that his dream job had turned into a “nightmare” but suggested that Palace’s squad needed investment in January. “We have to adjust some positions during the winter transfer window to give more solutions,” he said.

Sports.title: Le Fée’s penalty stuns Chelsea and breathes life into defiant Sunderland
Sports.content:
A lot can change in five‑and‑a‑half months, but as an early winter chill descended on Wearside last week – both meteorologically and ­metaphorically – Sunderland were determined that some things should remain the same. Just as they had beaten Chelsea on the final day of last season to ensure European qualification for the first time in 53 years, they did so again on Sunday to lift themselves off the bottom of the Premier League.

The Sunderland performance was certainly familiar to their head coach, Régis Le Bris – “the identity, the intensity, the togetherness, the way we managed the game” – on the way to three crucial points.

Ultimately a patched-up defence, ­without the injured Dan Ballard and the banned Omar Alderete, kept ­Chelsea at enough distance to allow Robin Roefs a tranquil ­afternoon amid the tumult. Chelsea may be ­developing into a ­chaotic must‑watch under Xabi Alonso but they were ­subdued here and have fallen out of the top four. “We didn’t produce enough to deserve to win,” Alonso said. “We lacked a bit of patience and creativity.”

Margins were paper-thin in a game decided by two first-half penalty calls, the first not awarded to Chelsea after Luke O’Nien’s clumsy challenge on Cole Palmer, deemed after video assistant referee consideration to be fractionally outside the area, and the second given to the hosts by Jarred Gillett after Levi Colwill brought down the ebullient Brian Brobbey; the defender argued, not without justification, that the Dutch striker had a handful of his shirt too but the award stood.

Alonso, as ever, made no excuses, ­focusing not on the officiating and more on how he was “not happy with how we defended that situation”. Enzo Le Fée had been equally unequi­vocal just beyond the half‑hour, sending Mike Penders the wrong way and dispatching into the goalkeeper’s bottom-right corner for the game’s only goal.

Europe may be a blessing for Sunderland but the full-time mood had been bleak after the latest alarming performance in the home defeat against Dinamo Zagreb on Thursday. It had felt like a season watershed and only the captain, Granit Xhaka, Thomas Meunier and Roefs survived the cull here. That the talismanic Xhaka, the subject of strong summer interest from his former coach Alonso, had his afternoon truncated by injury after less than three ­minutes, felt like yet more of the ill fortune dogging Sunderland.

View image in fullscreen Sunderland’s Reinildo Mandava attempts to wrestle the ball away from Morgan Rogers. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Richard Sellers/Apl/Sportsphoto

There was no feeling sorry for themselves, though. With this the start of a challenging quartet of fixtures leading into the Tyne‑Wear derby next month, it felt like this match had to be attacked to prevent an early-season hiccup turning into a full mid‑season tangle with relegation trouble. And Chelsea were greeted with determination and ­aggression, with Xhaka’s withdrawal not ­blowing that plan off course. Two zesty ­incisions by Chemsdine Talbi in the opening quarter-hour, in his first ­Premier League start this season, caused Alonso’s men flutters, the first leading to a blocked Trai Hume shot and the second presenting Brobbey with a clear opening that he would have expected to convert.

The passion was there, the precision maybe less so. O’Nien’s challenge on Palmer elicited a penalty appeal that did not end up being costly after the VAR check and Morgan Rogers headed wide from a Marco Palestra cross, but Chelsea could not capitalise on any potential home nerves. If anyone was prone to belated Halloween frights it was the Blues, particularly at the hands of Brobbey, who led the line with enormous presence. He took on and beat the last man Wesley Fofana before steering his shot just too high, past Penders’ near post, and then won the penalty that led to Le Fée’s winner. “He is stoppable,” Alonso said, “but only when you defend better than we did.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Such was Chelsea’s bluntness in the first 45 that the coach opted for not just a substitution but a reshuffle at the break, with Estêvão replacing the injured Colwill, beefing up the attack with Moisés Caicedo slotting into the defence. Sunderland continued to fight tooth and nail in a game that threatened occasionally to bubble over. Meunier was booked for a late tackle on Caicedo and shortly afterwards Brobbey was cautioned for wrestling Roméo Lavia to the ground, a continuation of an ongoing feud between the pair. When he was substituted, spent, for the ­enduringly ­popular Wilson Isidor halfway through the second half Chelsea must have breathed a sigh of relief.

Estêvão made one burst through the middle on to a Rogers pass but Reinildo Mandava stepped across to snuff out the opportunity. Yet even with little possession Sunderland looked sharper. A ball broke for Isidor after Chelsea failed to clear Le Fée’s through ball, Penders saving and the rebound not breaking for the Frenchman before Pep Chavarría cleared.

As the last 10 minutes approached Alonso sent on Geovany Quenda for Chavarría, and the young winger finally conjured a goal attempt worthy of the description, fizzing a shot just wide of Roefs’s far post via deflection. Talbi, finishing as he started, pinged one just wide from distance on the break as the home side still looked more likely, even with a third of possession. Sunderland had rewarded their crowd’s vociferous faith.

Sports.title: Diego Gómez hits another stunner as Brighton beat 10-man Brentford to go second
Sports.content:
Who can stop Brighton’s ­ascension in English and European football? They are setting standards, ­practices ­leaving almost everybody else ­trailing in their wake. A ­second‑place position in the ­Premier League would once have read like a glitch in a ­Football ­Manager ­session. Not in November 2026, where they appear the only team capable of throwing down any sort of challenge to Arsenal.

Under low winter sun, Brentford, an opposition to which Brighton are often, if lazily, compared, were ­swatted aside. If Keith Andrews’s team, and their fans at the Amex ­Stadium, could level blame at a couple of ­refereeing decisions, they received little chance of rescuing anything. Brighton squeezed them, toyed with them.

If Pascal Gross, scorer of a perfectly hit penalty, attempted to dampen expectations of a title challenge, his manager, Fabian Hürzeler, allowed fans to dream. “They should always be excited, it’s our job to make them excited,” he said.

A successful return to the Amex Stadium following five Brighton away trips, more than 5,000 miles on the road including victories at ­Manchester City and Getafe over the past two outings. Brentford returned to a stadium where they have never won in the Premier League. Normal service was duly resumed, any Brighton negatives coming in a failure to add to their first-half goals.

An up-and-under straight from the kick-off was a rare Brentford foray into the Brighton box. Bart Verburggen catching it on the full prefaced an easy afternoon for the Brighton goalkeeper. There are many further dimensions to ­Hürzeler’s team. Last week Paul Scholes, an unlikely ­progressive, declared himself an admirer of a “level of ­coaching” he suggested is ­unsurpassed in ­English football. “The one thing that is non‑negotiable is to always put the team first,” Hürzeler said.

View image in fullscreen Brighton were already 1-0 down when the VAR upgraded Igor Thiago’s yellow card to a red. Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters

Diego Gómez’s opener was not as spectacular as the halfway-line goal of the season against Crystal Palace but a beauty nonetheless. Caressing the ball first with his left and then with his right, he laid up a thrash past Caoimhín Kelleher. Its trajectory was unerring, unstoppable. Hürzeler revealed: “Yesterday, he changed to shooting with [his] left foot … I couldn’t see him scoring with his left foot. I asked him after where this quality came from.”

The path to a commanding win opened up. Igor Thiago did not last many ­minutes beyond his failed attempt to lob ­Verburggen. Scuffling in midfield with Chema Andrés, his shove was first ruled a yellow by the referee, Michael Oliver. In stepped the video assistant referee, Stuart Attwell: “violent conduct” and “with force” was the verdict from Stockley Park.

Afterwards, Andrews was ­visibly unhappy: “We’ve lost two games and both when down to 10 men. So we need to analyse ourselves first. In both scenarios we can do better. In both scenarios the opposition player has been the one to provoke the situation.”

Infact, both Yehor Yarmolyuk and Vitaly Janelt were dismissed against Liverpool, and if Andrews rues such lapses of discipline he was more unhappy at the initial decision’s video-assisted overturn: “The game is in a state now of a place I don’t particularly like.”

Straying beyond the confines of his technical area in a manner likely to add him to Mikel Arteta’s “massive storage of images” of such breaches, Andrews asked his team to dig deep but Brighton’s dominance of possession became near-total.

Luka Vuskovic, ­serving ­previously as a deep-lying playmaker, won the penalty. Keane Lewis-Potter’s ­panicked response to a physical 18-yard box mismatch was to snatch at the ­Croatian’s shirt. Gross’s penalty was struck as truly as Gómez’s goal. “We need to be cuter,” Andrews said. “I take real pride in the way we defend set pieces and we need to do better because that wasn’t good.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Pascal Gross’ penalty was unsaveable. Photograph: Alex Ferrelly/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock

Andrews’s half-time ­adjustments, bringing on Yarmolyuk and Nathan Collins, was an attempt to protect Brentford’s goal difference. Brighton continued to pile on pressure, their ­possession share reaching beyond 75%. A set piece became Brentford’s sole route back, though Mathias Jensen’s diagonal into ­Verbruggen’s hands would not have passed muster in rugby’s Nations Championship.

Ironic cheers from the away end came when Brentford won a corner, and then another – rare excitement at Brighton’s defenders being asked to do something other than build an attack. The visitors’ fighting spirit at least sustained, though threatened to spill over. When Kevin Schade shoved ­Vuskovic to the ground by the touchline, another red card was a possibility, only for Oliver and Attwell to rule a yellow as sufficient this time.

Brighton’s push for honours and further horizons will require more than spectacular goals. “You see the Premier League, the margins, you look at the results – we are not ­getting carried away yet,” Gross said. “Every game we have to suffer a lot.”

Hürzeler, like Andrews constantly straying beyond the confines of his technical area, does not countenance any let-ups. When Brighton meet the unstinting demands of their coach, so many are left in their wing mirrors.

Sports.title: Russo on target again as double fires under-pressure Arsenal to vital WSL win at Liverpool
Sports.content:
If a good striker can always get their team out of a hole, Alessia Russo is doing her best to drag Arsenal out of a deep chasm of uncertainty. Her two goals gave the ­under‑pressure Arsenal head coach, Renée Slegers, some brief respite with a much-needed, albeit still rather unconvincing victory.

Russo’s double took her impressive recent tally to seven goals in her past four appearances. Her goals were priceless for an Arsenal team who arrived on Merseyside with just one win in their previous seven Women’s Super League games. They will be relieved to have won after Liverpool posed plenty of problems and the hosts were unhappy about a ­disallowed goal.

Arsenal began the match brightly, with Lisa Baum’s effort deflecting on to the bar and Olivia Smith firing over from a tight angle. They were rewarded when a good move down their right led to Emily Fox’s cross being angled into the net by Russo’s incisive first-time finish.

Liverpool were level six minutes later, though, and from a defensive point of view it was a familiarly exasperating story for Arsenal, who have conceded from simple long balls through the middle ­several times this season.

They exerted very little pressure as Liverpool found Natalia Ramos in space and her direct ball picked out Beata Olsson up front, with the Arsenal centre-backs Steph Catley and Leah Williamson positioned so far apart that they were almost in different time zones, ­playing Olsson onside. Liverpool’s central striker did enough to keep the ball away from Williamson and lash her strike into the bottom corner.

A curling Ramos free-kick was tipped on to the bar by the Arsenal goalkeeper Misa Rodríguez, before the game’s most contentious moment left Liverpool feeling ­understandably aggrieved. Jenna Clark tucked the ball into the net at the far post after ­Arsenal failed to clear a corner, but the assistant referee disallowed the goal for offside against Vivien ­Endemann, despite the delivery towards the player having been ­inadvertently played off an Arsenal foot rather than being a deliberate forward pass from the home side, who looked baffled.

That seemed to wake Arsenal from their slumber, however, and ­Caitlin Foord went close before Russo restored Arsenal’s lead in the final minute of the first half, as her downward header from Baum’s cross was too precise for Khiara Keating to reach. Slegers praised Russo, as she said: “She’s in top form. The two goals are such clean finishes. She picks up really good positions in the box.”

After a very watchable first half for neutrals, the second half was comparatively less entertaining but still tense as Liverpool fought to try to force an equaliser. They almost found it in the 89th minute but Gareth Taylor had his head in his hands in disbelief after Cornelia Kapocs volleyed wide from a glorious, unmarked position in front of goal. Arsenal clung on.

Liverpool are now winless in five league games but their defender Grace Fisk, who signed a new contract on Saturday, said: “There were so many positives. We made them very uncomfortable for large parts of the game. It’s just the bits in both boxes right now that are letting us down.” ­Taylor, Liverpool’s head coach, agreed: “­Performance‑wise, I couldn’t ask for any more from the girls.”

Slegers, who next has a ­daunting trip to face the European champions Barcelona, said: “The way we defended at the end of the game, for our lives, with so much passion and pride for the shirt, that ball wasn’t going to go in.”

Sports.title: Barcelona move clear at the top after Fermín López’s double stuns Atlético Madrid
Sports.content:
They had been in a battle, they had been behind and they had been on edge, but Barcelona found a way through, holding on to their place at the top of the table and holding the doubts at bay for another day. A fortnight in which they were defeated by Pris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, in which they might have wondered if something was not quite right, ended with a 2-1 win at Atlético Madrid. This was a proper test, first place awaiting the winner, and in the end that was Hansi Flick’s side.

At a noisy, intense Metropolitano, against an even more intense Atlético, they went behind to a Giuliano Simeone goal and for a while in a frantic first half it looked like there may be no way back. But they found it, two goals from Fermín López either side of half-time leading them to the kind of victory that brings a reward beyond just the points. It had been a long night, but they had made it.

Atlético flew into this, fuelled by the noise. They did more inside three minutes than in 90 against Bayern Munich in midweek. A superb clearance from Pau Cubarsí kept them at bay in the first minute. Álex Baena curled wide in the second. And they forced a corner in the third. Barcelona were overwhelmed and exposed, unable to settle, and Diego Simeone’s side could sense it.

They could see it too, all that space behind the visitors’ defence for them to run into, and soon Koke released Julián Alvarez. He had a long way to run and a long time to think. Was this the moment for the man who wanted to join Barcelona in the summer but was forced to stay redemption and forgiveness laid before him? As he dashed into the area he opted to go round Joan García but the goalkeeper stretched and just about reached out a finger to force him even wider. Forced to turn back by the time Alvarez was facing the goal again, sufficient Barcelona players had recovered to clear.

Not for long. From the corner Marc Pubill thudded a header against the bar and although Barcelona did the same at the other end when Lamine Yamal and Pedri combined for the latter to shoot, Atlético soon had the lead. It started with a superb cross-field ball to open up the right wing again where Marcos Llorente and Lee Kang-in worked the space for the Korean to guide a pass to Alvarez on the other side. The Argentinian immediately returned it across the face of the box where Giuliano Simeone, head back, breathing hard, was running in at top speed, which is the speed he always runs at. From seven yards, without breaking his frantic stride, he scored.

The Metropolitano erupted. This was no more than Atlético deserved and so they kept on coming back for more and more. Every time they changed the direction of play, space yawned before them. Baena was going at Barcelona on the left, Alejandro Grimaldo joining him. Lee did the same on the right, Llorente with him. Pablo Barrios was taking a grip in the middle. As for Giuliano Simeone, he was everywhere, screeching about the pitch like a cartoon whirlwind, arms and legs occasionally visible sticking out of a thunderous dust cloud. Alvarez moved smartly through the chaos and chances came.

Alvarez might have added a goal to his assist, his shot escaping under Garcia and almost over the line. He also set up a wonderful opportunity for David Hancko, alone in front of goal, but his touch slipped just wide. Then Lee’s shot was stopped by García.

View image in fullscreen Giuliano Simeone fires Atlético Madrid into a first-half lead. Photograph: Susana Vera/Reuters

Barcelona could be grateful the lead was only one still. Would be, in fact. They were almost level on half an hour, when Lamine Yamal, almost the only outlet, slipped in – the angle was tight and from close range he hit the side-netting – and on 45, they were level. The momentum still felt like it was against them, the vulnerability still there when Atlético leapt out, but they began to get a grip of the ball, edging their way into the game, and equalising it too. Pedri ran at the defence, neat footwork taking him through a tight space to find Fermín. There was fortune in the deflection off Pubill but the finish was superb.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Half-time came as a reset; with the storm seen out and Frenkie De Jong introduced Barcelona began the second half better. Pushing Atlético back, the press better applied now, the ball was moved with more precision and more comfort too. Twice Lamine Yamal let fly. Twice Pubill had to intercept.

And yet the best opportunity in those opening minutes fell to Alvarez on 55 minutes. Running through, he lifted his shot over García and over the bar. Baena was played in by Alvarez too but, as if shocked to find the ball landing at his feet all alone by the far post, he hesitated and his attempt at scooping the ball up to Alexander Sørloth didn’t come off.

The game was opening up, tiredness affording a little more time and space. And when Fermín made yet another sharp, darting run, Lamine Yamal played a clever, perfectly weight pass into the area for him to cut the shot past Jan Oblak for his second of the night, his eighth of the season. It wasn’t over, the feeling that the olés from the Barcelona fans were premature and a little foolish, tempting fate, reinforced when Pubill ran through and found Alvarez, whose deflected shot looped over. For Barcelona, the priority now was control; they had been in a fight but they were still standing at the end.

Sports.title: Scottish roundup: flying Falkirk hit five to shatter Hearts’ long unbeaten home run
Sports.content:
Falkirk obliterated Hearts’ 18-month unbeaten home record in the Scottish Premiership with a stunning 5-2 win at Tynecastle on Sunday as they leapfrogged their hosts into third place.

Wouter Vrancken’s beleaguered side, missing 11 players through injury, were in disarray as Falkirk romped into a five-goal lead early in the second half through Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell’s double. Hearts hit back through Sabri Guendouz, on as a substitute, and a Cláudio Braga penalty, but Falkirk were well worthy of making it five top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1995.

Vrancken said: “This is an embarrassment, the first half for sure. It’s crazy, crazy, and everybody – me, staff, players – have to take responsibility in those things. This is ridiculous.”

It was a first league defeat at Tynecastle for Hearts since April 2025 and they have won just two of their past 11 matches. Falkirk move into third, a point above Hearts, although they have played a game more.

Liam Scales provided a looping finish to secure a 1-0 home victory for Celtic against Kilmarnock later on Sunday. The Irish defender hooked a Camilo Durán cross into the top corner in the 26th minute to restore Celtic’s four-point lead at the top of the table.

Celtic – and Kasper Høgh in particular – otherwise had a frustrating day in front of goal, with Benjamin Nygren missing a second-half penalty. Høgh had an early goal disallowed as his barren run without scoring hit 16 games since a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on his second appearance.

The Celtic manager, Martin O’Neill, said: “I thought Kasper was off the mark for about 35 seconds. I think he would maybe have scored the next chance if the first had counted, but he worked really hard for us.”

Rangers banished their recent away day blues with a solid 2-0 win at St Mirren on Saturday.

Draws against Dundee and Hearts in their past two Scottish Premiership games away from Ibrox had blemished their title challenge, but Derek McInnes’s side were determined to leave Paisley without a mark on them.

The in-form striker Ryan Naderi scored with a soft penalty after 18 minutes before the returning captain, Dan Neil, added a second just after the hour with a deflected strike to extend Rangers’ unbeaten run in all competitions to 12 games.

The Aberdeen manager, Stephen Robinson, insists he will face the challenge head on as his side go into the international break in real trouble at the wrong end of the table.

Hibernian started the evening three points behind Robinson’s side, but a dominant second-half performance in a 4-0 victory at Pittodrie allowed the Edinburgh club to overtake their hosts in 10th place on goal difference.

View image in fullscreen Hibernian players applaud their fans at full time. Photograph: Peter Summers/Shutterstock

The hosts showed promise early in the game and the Hibs keeper Raphael Sallinger saved well from Jack Milne, who also hit the bar for Aberdeen before Jamie McGrath’s 25-yard strike found the target. Aberdeen went all-out in search of an equaliser, but quickly fell 2-0 behind to Callum Wright, sparking calls for Robinson’s head from the home support. Further strikes from Thibault Klidjé and Nicky Cadden completed the rout.

Robinson said: “It’s really, really disappointing, there’s no hiding away from it. It was an unacceptable performance and an unacceptable result. We haven’t taken our chances – Hibs had five or six chances and took four of them – [and] that’s always the difference in football. We got the result we deserved.

“It’s a difficult situation, difficult for myself, the players and the club. I will keep fighting until told otherwise. We have to be better than that, that’s not acceptable. We have to get players who want to fight and try to get us out of this situation.”

Jim Goodwin, the home manager, hit out at the decision to award the penalty that cost Dundee United dear in a 1-1 draw against Motherwell at Tannadice.

The referee, Ryan Lee, had initially given a free-kick for offside in the early stages of the game. However, he was then advised by the VAR, Andrew Dallas, to have another look at an incident where Tawanda Maswanhise had gone down in the United box under a challenge by the home captain, Dylan Tait. After checking the pitchside monitor, the referee pointed to the spot with the Motherwell captain, Lukas Fadinger, tucking the penalty away.

The hosts ultimately salvaged a point thanks to Jesse Randall’s goal but Goodwin insisted his side should have had all three. “It’s a poor decision for me,” he said. “I know it’s going to be subjective and people will have their own opinions on it, but I don’t know what Dylan Tait is meant to do.”

Unsurprisingly, the Motherwell manager, Alfred Johansson, disagreed with Goodwin’s assessment, saying: “He’s on the ball and gets down from a tackle, and it’s a penalty.”

Simo Valakari was thrilled to give St Johnstone supporters a 2-1 victory against Dundee to celebrate after recent Perth struggles against their Tayside rivals.

Josh Campbell headed the home side in front after five minutes. Joe Westley, on as a substitute, replied early in the second half after a mix-up between the keeper Ross Sinclair and Cheick Diabate. Kai Fotheringham, on his first Premiership start for St Johnstone, scored a deflected winner on 72 minutes.

Sports.title: FA Cup roundup: Seventh-tier Wimborne shock Crawley to reach second round
Sports.content:
Seventh-tier Wimborne heaped more misery on Crawley as the bottom side in the Football League lost 2-0 in the biggest upset of the FA Cup first round.

The Dorset part-timers took the lead after only nine minutes when the property surveyor Yang Seung-woo curled a superb strike from just inside the penalty area into the top corner.

Crawley came close to equalising when Kai Jennings flashed a low shot narrowly wide before Jonny Russell headed tamely into the arms of the home goalkeeper Cam Plain.

Crawley’s interim manager, Kevin Blackwell, made a triple change at half-time and Charlie Barker fired inches wide for the team 57 places above their hosts in the pyramid. The Southern Premier League South side got a huge slice of luck to seal victory 11 minutes from time. Jackson King’s shot hit Cameron Munn to send the ball squirming beyond the former Arsenal goalkeeper Vito Mannone.

Will Sutton scored a dramatic extra-time winner for Oldham as Dave Challinor’s first game in charge of Sheffield Wednesday ended in an upset. The homegrown central defender was up for a free-kick which the Owls failed to clear, with Sutton left completely free to nod home from six yards and secure a 2-1 win.

Calum Kavanagh put Oldham ahead in the 66th minute with a fierce drive after Mike Fondop headed on Noah Chilvers’ right-wing cross. Wednesday equalised 10 minutes later through the former Oldham forward Davis Keillor-Dunn.

The match ignited further in the 84th minute following a touchline fracas involving a large number of players. The Oldham manager, Micky Mellon, was sent off and Sheffield Wednesday’s Callum Slattery was booked. After Sutton’s winning goal, Oldham defended resolutely to close out the game.

Stafford Rangers were denied a historic win after losing 3-2 on penalties to Grimsby after they drew 3-3 after extra time. Two goals from firefighter Darrhyl Mason and one from the Aston Villa youth coach Jack Birch got the eighth-tier side – 89 places below League Two Grimsby – to a shootout.

Mason and Birch had put Rangers 2-0 ahead in front of a crowd of 3,130 at the Stan Robinson Stadium as they chased the second round for the first time since 2007. But set-piece headers inside three minutes from Harvey Rodgers and Maldini Kacurri sent the tie into extra time, where Mason and Géza Turi traded goals.

View image in fullscreen Stafford Rangers’ Luca Navarro (right) appears dejected after missing the deciding penalty. Photograph: Gary Oakley/PA

The home debutant Luca Navarro had to score to send the tie into sudden death but saw his spot-kick saved by Harvey Cartwright to end Rangers’ nine-match Cup marathon.

Lewis Fiorini’s extra-time penalty sent Stockport, who are second in League One, into the second round after they came from two goals down with 10 men to win 3-2 against Cray Wanderers.

Despite being 112 places below their opponents in the pyramid, it was the Isthmian Premier side Cray who took the lead after 21 minutes when Sammie MacLeod found the bottom corner.

Stockport were then reduced to 10 men in the 31st minute as goalkeeper Luca Ashby-Hammond was sent off for a dangerous challenge on John Ufuah. Alex Hernández bent a brilliant strike into the top corner from the resulting free-kick.

Depleted Stockport pulled one back in the 81st minute when Kyle Wootton tscored with a header. And the Hatters then sent the tie into extra time when Mikael Mandron was in the right place to nod home Jack Diamond’s cross. The decisive moment came in the 101st minute when Cray goalkeeper JJ Briggs clattered into Mandron to give away a penalty, which was dispatched by Fiorini.

Charlie Savage scored against his father’s team as Reading eased into the second round with a 5-0 rout of Peterborough at the Weston Homes Stadium on Saturday.

This all-League One tie turned out to be one of the most one-sided of the day, with the Peterborough manager, Robbie Savage, watching on in disbelief as his side were pulled apart.

Reading went ahead after 26 minutes as slick passing led to Andy Rinomhota playing in Daniel Kyerewaa, who found the bottom corner via a deflection. Reading doubled their lead in the 34th minute when a cross from Haydon Roberts was met by a diving header from top scorer Jack Marriott.

It was in effect game over in first-half stoppage time as Savage deepened his father’s misery when he took possession after the ball ran off Marriott, his deflected effort finding the top corner.

Jamie Reid added a fourth for the visitors in the 72nd minute when Paudie O’Connor nodded Savage’s free-kick into his path for him to lift over the Peterborough goalkeeper Alex Bass. Reading struck yet again four minutes later when Liam Fraser’s pass put Reid clean through to score his second.

Non-league Kidderminster breezed into the second round with a convincing 3-0 victory over League One Doncaster.

The National League club opened the scoring after 22 minutes when Maz Kouhyar pulled the ball back to Lewis Walker, and he fired home at the second attempt after his initial shot had hit the upright.

View image in fullscreen David Davis celebrates a goal in Kidderminster’s FA Cup upset victory. Photograph: Matty Paddock

The Harriers striker continued to cause problems, putting an effort over the bar and another just wide, but in the 36th minute he turned provider, charging upfield before teeing up Kouhyar and the on-loan Notts County midfielder slotted home. Kouhyar was again involved in the third goal, having a shot that Josh Clarke could only parry and David Davis turned in the rebound.

The Kidderminster manager, Paul Wotton, said: “We started well, scored the goal and got the crowd up. It was just a really good day. They are a League One team at the end of the day, no matter what the scoreline suggests. They are two leagues higher than us, so they are going to have moments in the game, but we stood up to it.”

League Two Exeter pulled off an upset with a 2-1 win away to League One leaders Huddersfield. Exeter took the lead after 12 minutes, thanks to a perfectly delivered cross from the left from Luca Woodhouse, with centre-back Jack Taylor stealing in at the far post to finish it off.

Huddersfield looked a different team in the second half and found an equaliser within eight minutes of the restart as Ibane Bowat headed home Cameron Humphreys’ corner at the back post.

Charlie Cummins grabbed the winner nine minutes from time at the end of a well-worked move up the right, culminating in Reece Cole’s cutback and a good finish.

View image in fullscreen Exeter’s Charlie Cummins celebrates after his late winner against Huddersfield. Photograph: Steve Taylor/PPAUK/Shutterstock

Altrincham were denied another famous FA Cup upset as they conceded an 84-minute equaliser against Notts County before bowing out in a penalty shootout.

County took the lead through Jacob Bedeau in the 28th minute but Altrincham responded well with Lucas Weaver grabbing an equaliser six minutes before half-time. Lewis Banks gave the hosts the lead just before the hour but Callum Roberts dashed Altrincham’s hopes of another cup scalp, having beaten 17 Football League sides in the competition, scoring with a first-time strike to force extra-time.

With neither side able to make a breakthrough in extra-time the game went to penalties and Aidan Barlow, Sam Taylor and Eddy Jones all missed from the spot for Altrincham as County triumphed 3-2.

Blackpool survived a scare at Hornchurch, needing to rely on a 118th-minute winner from Josh Bowler to secure a 2-1 comeback victory at the Hornchurch Stadium.

Fleetwood’s hopes of following up their memorable Carabao Cup upset against Premier League champions Arsenal with a long FA Cup run are over after a 2-1 home defeat by fellow League Two side Rochdale. Baba Adeeko’s goal in extra time at Highbury sent the visitors through.

Chesterfield withstood a second-half comeback from Yeovil Town to secure their place in the second round with a 4-3 victory. Yeovil recovered from 3-1 down to level at 3-3 before Joel Randall struck the winner for the Spireites a minute from time.

Late Mansfield goals from Rhys Oates and Jordan Bowery ended the plucky Cup resistance of National League North Macclesfield. Nathan Moriah-Welsh gave Mansfield a first-half lead but the Silkmen were still in the tie under Oates made it 2-0 in the 72nd minute. Bowery added a third three minutes into added time to wrap up victory for the Stags.

League One Plymouth eased through thanks to three goals in a late 11-minute spell in a 4-0 win against Southern League Premier Central battlers Alvechurch. Will Evans finally broke the deadlock after 50 minutes, winning the ball from Jessy Bavanganga before driving a low angled shot into the far corner. Further goals from Evans, Michael Baidoo and Ronan Curtis saw the Pilgrims through.

View image in fullscreen Michael Baidoo makes it 3-0 to Plymouth as they overcome Alvechurch. Photograph: Dave Rowntree/PPAUK/Shutterstock

League One strugglers Barnsley booked their spot in the second round with a 7-2 win over Aldershot at Oakwell, with Cameron McGeehan grabbing a hat-trick.

Leyton Orient held off Harborough 5-1 to progress into the second round while League Two high-flyers Crewe beat Wimbledon 2-1.

Nick Powell and Adam Phillips scored twice as Bradford thrashed National League North side Marine 7-0, while a late goal from Joel Randall helped Cheltenham close out a dramatic 4-3 win over National League Yeovil.

Last season’s quarter-finalists Port Vale booked their place in the second round with a 4-2 victory over National League strugglers Scunthorpe United at Vale Park. MK Dons avoided an upset as they ground out a 2-1 win over League Two Swindon.

Southern League Premier Central team Worcester’s hopes of an upset were ended in a 1-0 defeat at League Two Colchester while Jack Bates scored twice in the first half as Dover progressed with a 2-0 win over Wealdstone.

Ollie Pearce scored after 10 seconds as York sealed a 4-0 win over Northampton. The City captain also scored a second before Alex Hunt and Josh Stones completed the rout.

Jordan Thewlis’s stoppage-time penalty gave seventh-tier Guiseley a 1-0 win over Sutton at Nethermoor Park as Carlisle beat League Two leaders Salford 1-0. Ryan Graydon missed a penalty for the visitors before David Ajiboye’s goal just before the break proved enough to send the Cumbrians through.

Eighth-tier AFC Rushden & Diamonds slipped to a 4-0 defeat at Burton. Will Collar and Borges Rodrigues scored for the Brewers in the first half, with Charlie Webster and Zac Scutt adding two more late on.

Nathan Odokonyero scored twice as National League South Salisbury saw off seventh-tier Sholing 6-0 to take their place in round two for the first time since reforming in 2015.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso must look at HIMSELF, not the officials, as another questionable line-up sees Chelsea fold at Sunderland - and Cole Palmer wastes his chance to respond to Thomas Tuchel snub, writes KIERAN GILL
Sports.content:
When searching for why Chelsea were beaten by the side who were sitting bottom of the Premier League, the temptation from Xabi Alonso might be to describe this defeat as a tale of two penalties. First, Chelsea were denied one when Cole Palmer was sandwiched by Luke O'Nien and Jules Ahoka as he entered the Sunderland area, with the officials concluding the contact occurred outside of the box. Then, Sunderland were awarded one when Brian Brobbey was brought down by Levi Colwill. The striker had hold of the defender at the same time, and arguably clipped his own heel upon second viewing, but Enzo Le Fee gladly accepted the opportunity to score the game's only goal. However, it would be wrong to blame this deserved defeat on those two decisions alone. Referee Jarred Gillett and VAR Nick Hopton were weak but not the reason that Chelsea lost. This was actually a tale of two strikers. Sunderland had one in the brilliant bully that is Brobbey, whereas Chelsea had nobody after Alonso yet again decided against starting Danny Welbeck. In the three Premier League games played since Joao Pedro's injury – against Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United and now Sunderland – Alonso has gone with Morgan Rogers as a false nine once and Pedro Neto twice. Welbeck was on the bench in all of those matches. Sunderland handed Chelsea a brutal reality check as they climbed off the foot of the table The visitors fell victim to two questionable penalty calls at the Stadium of Light We are not saying the 35-year-old is the answer to all of Alonso's problems, but he is an actual No9 who scored 13 times in the Premier League for Brighton last season. Neto was hardly going to have a high success rate when wrestling with centre backs for the long balls which were coming from Colwill and Co. It is a question that needs asking, therefore, especially after another loss. Why did Chelsea sign Welbeck if not to play when Joao Pedro is injured? Welbeck came on in the 62nd minute here, but by then, a familiar feeling was washing over Chelsea. They lost 2-1 here at the very end of last season. Malo Gusto scored an own goal, Wesley Fofana was red carded, and Chelsea, managed by Calum McFarlane in the interim, failed to qualify for any form of European football. They smacked of an utterly unserious side then, and resembled it here, too. Chelsea had a week to prepare for this Premier League clash while Sunderland were playing – and losing – to Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League. Regis Le Bris' side had not won in the league since August. Yet they were the sharper of the two teams here. It hardly helped Alonso that Chelsea's attackers never appeared at it individually. Cole Palmer had a stinker. This was supposed to be an opportunity to show why Thomas Tuchel made a mistake in not naming him in his latest England squad. If anything, he helped make sure those accusations cannot be levelled at Tuchel over this break. Xabi Alonso tinkered with his line-up and it failed to pay off in a second defeat in three games Cole Palmer had a stinker in a woeful response to Thomas Tuchel's England snub Rogers' performance was best summed up by the time he simply sprinted out of play with the ball to gift Sunderland a goal-kick. He and Palmer resembled no-shows. MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS Sunderland (4-2-3-1): Roefs 6; Hume 7, Mukiele 7, O'Nien 6, Mandava 7; Xhaka 6 (Ahoka 4, 6), Sadiki 7; Meunier 6, Talbi 6 (Rigg 88), Le Fee 6 (Angulo 88); Brobbey 8 (Isidor 67, 6) Subs (not used): Ellborg, Danso, Methalie, Fofana, Tutierov Scorers: Le Fee (36 pen) Booked: Ahoka, Meunier, Brobbey, O'Nien, Angulo Manager: Regis Le Bris 7 Chelsea (4-3-3): Penders 6; Palestra 5 (Gusto 62, 5), Fofana 5, Colwill 4 (Estevao 45, 6), Chavarria 5 (Quenda 79); Caicedo 6, Lavia 6, Henderson 6 (Emegha 87); Palmer 4, Neto 5 (Welbeck 62, 5), Rogers 4 Subs (not used): Sharman-Lowe, Barco, Anselmino, Nicoll-Jazuli Booked: Colwill, Neto, Caicedo, Fofana Manager: Xabi Alonso 4 Referee: Jarred Gillett 4 Neto looked like a lost little boy trying to lead Chelsea's line in the absence of Joao Pedro. The half-time statistics said Chelsea had sent more open-play crosses into Sunderland's box in the opening 45 minutes than in their entire games v Fulham, Everton, Tottenham, Manchester United, Bournemouth and Brighton. Except, they had no striker for Alonso's full backs Marco Palestra or Pep Chavarria to try to find. Just 5ft 8in Neto and the odd other box-crasher. Trailing 1-0 at half-time here, Alonso made a singular substitution. It was to introduce Estevao for Colwill, who had been tormented by Brobbey. Le Bris was asked in his post-match press conference if there is another player like his striker in the Premier League. He thought long and hard before answering: 'What do you think? I don't think so. His physicality, his intensity, it's impressive, that's for sure. The build-up is so important to have a target man.' Alonso chipped in on Brobbey: 'He is not unstoppable. He is stoppable but only when you defend better than we did.' On his own attack, he added: 'We didn't produce enough to deserve to win.' Sunderland's tactic of hoofing the ball up to Brobbey worked wonders. He scared the daylights out of Chelsea's centre backs. When Fofana first arrived at the Stadium of Light, a Chelsea fan shouted at him as he got off the bus. 'Fofana, please be on the bench,' he said. Fofana may have been wishing he was a substitute as well whenever he was wrestling with Brobbey. It was the long-ball approach which led to Sunderland winning their penalty. They smashed it towards the top of the pitch and Brobbey bullied Colwill. Sunderland won their spot-kick and, in truth, deserved the lead for the sheer energy they brought to this match. Alonso is ten Premier League games into his Chelsea career. The honeymoon period is over. Sunderland lost their captain Granit Xhaka to an injury after two minutes here. Chelsea had named a line-up featuring three midfielders. But they never showed any signs of control, and for that, Alonso should be looking at himself and his own side rather than the refereeing team.

Sports.title: Prickly Unai Emery fires back at 'more questions' from Sky Sports reporter in awkward interview after storming down Old Trafford tunnel before full time
Sports.content:
Aston Villa boss Unai Emery was in a prickly mood as he bit back at Sky Sports reporter Patrick Davison in a fiery end to his post-match interview at Old Trafford on Sunday. Emery had just seen his Villa side twice throw away a two-goal lead against Manchester United – with Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu scoring in stoppage time to secure a remarkable 4-4 draw. The Villa boss was spotted storming down the touchline before the full-time whistle and after Dorgu's dramatic 97th-minute equaliser – with play continuing for another two minutes. And the Villa boss, already exasperated at being asked 'more questions,' did not take kindly to being asked if he was emotional about the late equaliser or if he felt it was unfair. When asked if his walking off was an emotional reaction, he responded: 'No emotion. They scored in minute 96 and there were six minutes added. I [thought] the match was finishing.' And then when asked whether the award of the goal was unfair, he replied: 'No, no. Not unfair. Please. Unai Emery was in a prickly mood towards the end of his post match interview with Sky Sports Emery had just stormed down the tunnel at Old Trafford after Aston Villa threw away a 4-2 lead in stoppage time Emery took exception to being asked 'more questions' by Sky reporter Patrick Davison 'They scored the goal in minute 96. You were making the question [about why] I left before. Because the minute 96 and 30 seconds, was when we started the kick-off.' Emery ended the interview making light of his 'poor' English, and then sarcastically asking if there were 'more questions' before an ironic 'Have a good Sunday' as he walked out of the interview. Villa's director of football operations Damian Vidagany complained on social media about the legitimacy of United's last-gasp equaliser. He accused United goalkeeper Senne Lammens – who went up for the corner – of impeding his Villa counterpart Zion Suzuki as he looked to punch the ball clear. After Roy Keane said 'football is a contact sport,' he posted on X: 'To put in context this convenient narrative of "contact sport" we've been told by referees during the summer that this season to go to unbalance or push the GK on purpose on the six-yard box was not going to be allowed anymore. 'Lammens did not even look at the ball, went straight to do a contact with the hip over Zion. 'Having said that we played good match and we must do better than last six minutes. We will do and we will improve. 'But the rules are the rules and must be respected. That is a fact.' Michael Carrick was involved in a spiky interview with Sky Sports about his Man United future Sky Sports' Davison's brush with Emery came just minutes after a spiky interview with beleaguered United boss Michael Carrick. When the future of his own position was put to him by Davison, Carrick took exception to the question. 'What do you expect to happen over the next few weeks? You've been asked time and again about your future? I know you have said that you walking away was the best for the club, you'd probably do it,' Davison asked Carrick. 'It's not going to happen, no,' Carrick replied. With United chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox in the stands, Davison pushed further asking: 'What do you expect to happen? Clearly there's going to be conversation?' This prompted Carrick to quizzically state: 'Is there?' as the pair engaged in a back-and-forth on the subject. Eventually Carrick replied: 'You know the situation, we haven't won enough games. But I expect to move forward with things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good from today tighten up a few mistakes and win some football matches.' United's start of one win in 10 games is still their worst since Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago this week. They conceded twice at the start of each half against Villa, and have now let in 30 goals in all competitions – the joint highest in Europe's top five leagues.
