Sports.title: Canelo Payday Would Reward Sheeraz’s Janibek Duck
Sports.content:
Hamzah Sheeraz might pull off the slickest business move in boxing by tossing his WBO belt in the trash. Dan Canobbio called out the absurdity of the whole setup: Sheeraz walks away from a dangerous night against Janibek Alimkhanuly, and his reward could be the richest payday in the sport against Canelo Alvarez.

Canobbio revealed the reason behind the split. It was never about old testing drama with Janibek. It came down to cash, exposing the massive gap between heavily subsidized guarantees and what the open market actually pays for a real fight.

“He didn’t like the money. He went to purse bid and he saw his true value out there, not the inflated purses that he’s been getting from Turki,” Canobbio said to Ariel Helwani. “I’m not fighting Janibek, who’s very good, for what he considers low money. So he vacates the belt.”

The purse bid told the whole story. Janibek is a stylistic nightmare with zero commercial juice, and nobody stepped up with silly money to save Sheeraz from the risk.

From a pure survival standpoint, Sheeraz made the smart business play. Getting beaten by Janibek kills his career progress and ends his Canelo lottery ticket before he ever touches the check. Getting beaten by Canelo still pays him millions and puts him on the biggest stage in the game. Both bouts bring real danger, but only one leaves him set for life.

The WBO belt stopped being an asset and turned into a snare. Titles are supposed to give a fighter leverage. The moment this one forced a low-dollar dogfight, Sheeraz dumped it to keep the fast lane to Canelo open.

Canelo certainly does not care about Sheeraz’s vacated strap. Sheeraz brings the height, reach, and punching power to cut a flashy promo video, while Canelo brings the buying public. When the backers want the pairing, the sanctioning bodies lose all their juice the second the fighter surrenders the belt.

The ugly part is what this does to the sport. Surrendering a title is supposed to carry a penalty. Instead, Sheeraz gets an upgrade. Every contender watching gets the exact same signal: taking on a terrifying mandatory is for suckers when ducking the assignment lets you jump straight to the cash cow.

Canobbio still likes the matchup because Sheeraz has size and punch, but that angle needs a cold reality check. Height has never bothered Canelo. Callum Smith brought the exact same size, only to spend twelve rounds getting his arms tenderized and his body battered along the ropes.

Towering over Canelo means nothing if you cannot stop him from walking through the front door. Destroying Edgar Berlanga did not prove Sheeraz can control distance against an elite counterpuncher, and taking the bigger payday certainly does not mean he picked an easy night.

This move does Canelo no favors either. For a superstar who built his reputation chasing undisputed status, taking on a fighter who just ditched his hardware looks cheap, especially with active champions like Osleys Iglesias sitting right there.

The fight will sell, but putting it together next turns the sport on its head. It tells every fighter in the division that real tests are optional as long as the promoters want you in the main event anyway.

Sports.title: Elif Turhan vs. Alycia Baumgardner: Strategic Analysis
Sports.content:
Alycia “The Bomb” Baumgardner seeks to become a two-division world champion today as she challenges the undefeated IBF lightweight world champion, the “Golden Turkish Warrior” Elif Nur Turhan.

The match will be the toughest challenge of her career, testing her chin and technical boxing abilities. Baumgardner faces a strong power puncher with six 1st-round knockouts and an overall knockout rate of 57.14 percent. In women’s boxing, a knockout ratio of 50 percent or higher is considered exceptional.

What makes Turhan so dangerous is her unconventional style where she throws punches from awkward angles under relentless pressure. In the IBF championship match against Beatriz Ferreira, she demonstrated her power and tenacity by overpowering Ferreira dropping her multiple times en route to a fifth-round technical knockout victory.

Ferreira mistakenly believed she could stay in the pocket and exchange with the Golden Turkish Warrior and paid the price. Since then, opponents have learned not to stand in front of Turhan (14-0, 8 KOs) by giving her the opportunity to land clean punches. Her last two opponents Taylah Gentzen and Gabriela Tellez found success by being mobile and becoming moving targets. The lateral movement frustrated Elif as she struggled to cut the ring off and land cleanly, missing several shots badly from distance against both.

However, when they were in range, she found limited success by connecting from awkward angles. Both her fights against Gentzen and Tellez went the distance and in the eyes of some were controversial decision victories.

Baumgardner (18-1, 7 KOs) likes to come forward and exchange with her opponents and takes a lot of punishment as a result. She is vulnerable to counters, and against Turhan it may very well be her downfall. Defensively, she’s been taking more and more damage with every fight. In her last three fights, her opponents’ total landed punches have gone up with per fight:

Jennifer Miranda outlanded Baumgardner in total punches, 79 to 78; Leilan Boudain was able to land 98 total punches against her; and Bo Mi Re Shin landed the most ever against Alycia at 151. Baumgardner is not known for her defensive prowess, but against Turhan she cannot be so careless.

It may pose difficulty for her to tighten up defensively when she is so offensively oriented. Baumgardner’s opponents do have success against her in landing their power shots, doing so at a high rate of 27.3 percent. If Turhan is given the opportunity to land the same rate of power shots, she will win the fight (Compubox).

This is Alycia’s toughest fight because she’s being forced to change her fighting style. She must be technically and defensively sound. She is the smaller fighter in terms of weight and will find herself on the back foot, evading Elif’s offensive attack. She must be defensively disciplined for 30 minutes and avoid getting caught with a big shot.

Baumgardner won’t be able to stay in the pocket and exchange as she’s done in her previous matches. Her best method of victory for this match will be to outpoint the Golden Turkish Warrior by limiting exchanges, boxing at distance, and landing calculated and timed punches. Given her past defensive history, it may be too difficult to be so technical from one fight to the next. For Turhan, she must cut the ring effectively, utilize her jab, and try to be more precise with her punches.

She has knockout power that will give Baumgardner problems, and if she’s able to utilize calculated pressure, she can be more controlled and more difficult to telegraph. The shots will be there for her; she should just be more offensively strategic by dictating the exchanges. If she can be more tactical, she can create the openings needed to end it early.

Sports.title: Tony Yoka’s Five-Win Rebuild Has Taken Him Nowhere
Sports.content:
Tony Yoka has put together five consecutive wins, yet his heavyweight rebuild is chewing through critical years without showing that he has resolved the flaws exposed in his three career defeats. Saturday’s 59-55 points win over Kostiantyn Dovbyshchenko in Manchester kept the streak alive, but against opposition well below the standard required of a serious contender.

Six rounds against a durable Ukrainian journeyman on the Buatsi–Hutchinson undercard told us nothing new about the 2016 Olympic gold medalist Yoka. Over the past three years, the former Olympic champion has merely padded out his record while keeping his true ceiling carefully hidden from view.

Yoka controlled the range behind his jab and timed the Ukrainian with rear-hand uppercuts on the way in. What he failed to do was capitalize on that control. His corner repeatedly called for more spite, but Yoka settled for single shots instead of putting together sustained flurries.

Dovbyshchenko has never been stopped, so a decision win is not an embarrassment on paper. The red flag was Yoka’s refusal to turn up the heat on a fighter offering minimal return fire. That hesitation points to an uncomfortable reality: this run has not restored his confidence, it has simply matched him with opposition he can outpoint without evolving.

Yoka still left the ring with a bloody nose and a cut above his eye. Those marks are not catastrophic, but they highlight the danger of letting an aggressive target march forward unpunished. Against punchers with real stopping power, landing early leads means nothing if he cannot survive the inside exchanges that follow.

Scrapped bouts with Lawrence Okolie and Murat Gassiev account for the layoff, and taking Saturday’s contest on a few hours’ notice showed professionalism. Neither factor alters the urgency of his situation.

At 34, padding the record with routine six-round assignments brings zero value. A sink-or-swim test against someone like Frazer Clarke would finally answer whether Yoka can stand firm when an opponent walks straight through his jab.

Queensberry can keep finding him rounds. Finding a win that restores his credibility is the real challenge, and after five tune-ups, that test is long overdue.

Sports.title: Denzel Bentley Riding Fast Track To The Exit Door At Zuffa
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley is acting like he just hit the jackpot with Zuffa, but scraping past Shane Mosley Jr. should bring him right back down to earth. At 31, Bentley does not have a massive fan base to protect him when things go wrong. If he thinks a busy media schedule guarantees loyalty, he is in for a rude awakening.

Bentley bragged that he received more publicity in two weeks with Zuffa than during his entire run with Queensberry. That is basic promotional launch hype, not a lifetime commitment. Every promoter rolls out the red carpet for a fresh signing. The real test is what happens to that promotional push the minute you take an L.

“I just felt undervalued there. Over here, I feel really valued. I feel like they want to push me and move me forward,” Bentley said after the fight. “I’ve had more press in the last two weeks than I’ve had my whole career at Queensberry. And that’s not a dig at no one. They have their priorities, and that’s who they want to move, and I didn’t think I was a priority over there. So I went where I was appreciated, and I feel appreciated here.”

Most of that early noise came from the controversy of Bentley ditching his promoter and getting stripped of his WBO belt. It gave writers an easy angle before he even laced up gloves. Once that headline gets stale, hype will not carry him.

Frank Warren gave Bentley plenty of patience. Bentley took losses against Felix Cash, Janibek Alimkhanuly, and Nathan Heaney. Queensberry did not toss him in the trash. They kept finding him dates, kept him active, and rebuilt him.

After the Heaney loss, Bentley ran through Danny Dignum, Derrick Osaze, Brad Pauls, and Endry Saavedra. That was a tidy domestic recovery run that fixed his ranking without matching him against the division’s monsters. Bentley might have wanted more spotlight, but Warren kept his career alive.

The mandatory defense against Yoenli Hernandez was supposed to prove whether Bentley had actually improved. Instead of facing the dangerous Cuban, Bentley opted for Mosley, lost his belt, and threw away his best bargaining chip. Now he is calling out Carlos Adames and Aaron McKenna with empty hands. Without a belt, you do not dictate terms to anybody.

Saturday night hardly helped his stock. Bentley dropped Mosley in the second round, got greedy looking for a quick knockout, and let Mosley drag him into deep water. Bentley admitted he ignored his corner because he thought the stoppage was right there.

Bentley claimed he did not gas out, which actually makes it worse. It means once Mosley shook off the knockdown and turned up the heat, Bentley simply lacked the ring generalship to stay in control. That kind of tactical drift gets you knocked out against punchers like Adames or Janibek.

A cash cow can afford an ugly night because ticket sales keep promoters hooked. Bentley does not have that luxury.

Zuffa comes from the UFC mindset where rosters get trimmed fast. If Bentley loses, they are far more likely to cut him loose than spend two years quietly rebuilding him at small domestic venues. Warren gave Bentley second and third chances. Bentley has yet to find out whether Zuffa has any interest in picking up the pieces when he gets beat.

For academics, it is publish or perish; under the Zuffa banner, it is produce or hit the pavement.

Bentley is walking around grinning about media scrums and spotlight time, completely blind to the fact that every camera pointed at him right now is a record entry. Dana White and company do not run a charity. The UFC promotional machine operates on an aggressive ROI formula: you either deliver explosive highlight-reel finishes that generate viral clips, or you pack the house with rabid, ticket-buying fans.

Bentley brings neither to the table. He is not a powerful one-punch artist who guarantees fireworks, and he certainly does not move tickets in the United States.

When you fight under a traditional boxing boss like Frank Warren, you can afford an ugly night or a bad loss because the promotional structure includes patience, domestic dates, and long rebuilding cycles. In the Zuffa ecosystem, fighters are viewed as content inventory. The second an import with zero domestic drawing power fails to deliver explosive content or drops a decision, there’s little reason to keep them on board.

Bentley was brought in to provide fresh content, look slick, and give their brand a boost. Struggling to pull away from an ordinary fighter like Shane Mosley Jr. was the absolute worst way to introduce himself. He thinks he landed a promotion that genuinely values him as an athlete, but in reality, he signed up for a high-turnover business that will hand him his pink slip the very second he stops producing.

Sports.title: Hutchinson Targets Bivol-Smith Winner After Beating Buatsi
Sports.content:
Willy Hutchinson grabbed the vacant WBC light heavyweight title off Joshua Buatsi and went straight to calling out whoever wins between Dmitry Bivol and Callum Smith. Going for all the belts sounds great on the microphone, but the loose, free-wheeling style that worked against Buatsi will get him picked apart against either of those two.

Against Buatsi, Hutchinson relied on speed bursts, weird angles, and flipping between orthodox and southpaw to completely baffle a rigid, predictable opponent. Try that against Bivol, though, and it turns into a disaster. You cannot switch stances right in front of a technician like Bivol without squaring your feet up and losing balance. The second Hutchinson gives away his stance, Bivol will drill him down the middle with a straight right.

“We’ll go for undisputed, isn’t it? I want to beat the best, be the best, beat the best. And I’m one of the best now. Got one of the belts,” Hutchinson said after the fight.

Hutchinson likes the idea of the Bivol vs. Smith winner, but his biggest bad habit will be an open invitation for Bivol. Whenever Hutchinson throws his lead left hook, he leaves his chin in the air and pauses to admire his handiwork. Bivol thrives on that exact mistake. He takes a clean step back, makes the shot miss, and snaps back with a check-hook or a 1-2 before his opponent can even tuck their chin. Hutchinson cannot showboat his way out of trouble against a guy who controls the ring that well.

Smith presents a totally different kind of danger. Hutchinson loves throwing wide, flashy flurries, but Smith is deadliest when backed up to the ropes, waiting to uncork a short inside left hook. Trading hooks at mid-range with Smith is asking to get caught. To beat Smith, Hutchinson would have to abandon the circus act, use a stiff jab to keep range, target Smith’s tall body, and make Smith come forward so that counter hook stays locked away.

Then there is the Ben Whittaker option. Hutchinson shrugged and said he would take the fight, but it makes zero sense for his career right now.

Whittaker hates fighting on his back foot, and Hutchinson has the hand speed and awkward angles to give him nightmares. Still, both guys rely on athletic reflexes instead of solid defense. Taking on Whittaker is pure risk. If Hutchinson slips up, he blows his new WBC belt on a domestic scrap and waves goodbye to massive unification paydays in Saudi Arabia.

It ultimately comes down to boxing politics. If mandatory defenses or rematch clauses hold up the Bivol vs. Smith winner, Hutchinson will have to decide whether to stay busy with a simple defense or risk it all in a domestic clash.

Hutchinson finally has the belt he wanted. Keeping it means figuring out that the wild, erratic showmanship that worked on domestic rivals will get him dismantled against the elite at 175.

Sports.title: The Hold And Hit Trap That Wrecked Chris Billam-Smith
Sports.content:
Cheavon Clarke stopped Chris Billam Smith in the seventh round at London’s Copper Box Arena, crediting former heavyweight champion Wladimir Klitschko for the tactical blueprint that unraveled the former cruiserweight belt holder.

Asked about grabbing on to mess up Billam Smith’s timing, Clarke gave full credit to Klitschko’s old tactics.

“I learned that one from Klitschko. So, shout out Klitschko. That was a Klitschko special right there,” Clarke stated at the post-fight press conference.

The maneuver served as far more than basic stalling. Inside the ring, holding functions as an offensive exit strategy. A fighter stepping back after launching an attack enters counterpunching range. Smothering the reply by stepping forward eliminates that hazard, outsourcing the retreat to the referee.

That approach neutralized Billam Smith, who relies on sustained pocket combinations to do damage. Getting inside accomplished nothing when every entry resulted in wrapped arms. Each intervention by the referee forced Billam Smith to reset, handing Clarke another opportunity to score before initiating the next clinch.

Beyond killing the return fire, Clarke used his upper torso to press his full weight downward across Billam Smith’s neck. Forcing a fighter to carry dead weight round after round burns out their legs. By the middle rounds, Billam Smith was flat-footed, lacking the spring in his lower body required to absorb contact or dip away from incoming punches.

Clarke pushed the referee’s patience to the limit, later admitting he was warned about losing a point. A verbal warning means nothing to the fighter trapped in a headlock, though. Billam Smith needed to solve the problem himself instead of waiting on the official.

All that holding set the trap for the seventh round knockout. Clarke spent six rounds getting Billam Smith used to being grabbed after every punch. When Clarke stepped in during the seventh, Billam Smith dropped his hands to brace for another clinch. Clarke did not grab him this time. He ripped hard shots straight through the open guard, dropping Billam Smith twice before the referee stopped it at 1:24.

For the rematch, Billam Smith has to stop the clinch before Clarke gets both arms around him. He needs to fight for inside control, keeping one hand free to dig hard hooks into Clarke’s ribs. Timing an uppercut right when Clarke ducks forward would also make him think twice about diving in to grab. Once Clarke has both arms locked, trying to wrestle him off just burns energy without landing punches.

Billam Smith wants an immediate rematch, but running it back without fixing that flaw will lead to the exact same result. He has to hit Clarke on the way in before Clarke grabs him and forces the referee to step in.

Sports.title: Abraham Perez Drops Yankiel Rivera, Wins Unanimous Decision
Sports.content:
Abraham “Hammer” Perez scored a second-round knockdown and defeated Yankiel “El Doctorito” Rivera by unanimous decision over 12 rounds Saturday at Kiva Auditorium in Albuquerque, New Mexico.

Perez (16-0, 7 KOs) retained his IBF Intercontinental flyweight title by scores of 118-109, 118-109 and 120-107. Rivera (8-2-1, 4 KOs), a southpaw who represented Puerto Rico at the 2021 Olympics, had stretches of success, but the judges favored the hometown champion by wide margins.

A right hand to the nose dropped Rivera in the closing seconds of the second round. Referee Tony Weeks administered the count, and Rivera continued with blood coming from his nose.

Rivera fought his way back into the contest, opening a cut over Perez’s left eyebrow with a right hook in the final minute of the fourth. He then outlanded Perez in the fifth and sixth rounds before Perez rocked him with a right to the chin near the end of the seventh.

Perez landed a three-punch combination late in the ninth, while Rivera answered with a competitive tenth and outworked him in the eleventh. Both fighters had their moments during an active final round, although the scorecards showed Perez had built an insurmountable lead.

The DAZN card was promoted by Legacy Promotions, King’s Promotions and Salita Promotions.

IBF minimumweight champion Pedro Taduran (21-4-1, 14 KOs) retained his title with a unanimous decision over Brandon Moreno (16-1, 5 KOs). The judges returned widely differing scores of 120-106, 115-113 and 115-113 after 12 rounds.

In the light heavyweight co-feature, unbeaten southpaw Atif Oberlton (18-0, 14 KOs) defeated Dean Nicholson (23-2, 19 KOs) by split decision in a scrappy 10-round contest. Two judges scored it 98-92 for Oberlton, while the third favored Nicholson 96-94.

The taller Oberlton used his jab to establish an early advantage. Nicholson struggled to get inside and developed swelling around his left eye after catching an elbow in the seventh round.

Nicholson continued having difficulty closing the distance in the eighth and ninth, but found some success with looping right hands in the final round. Oberlton said afterward that he had injured his left arm.

Heavyweight Pryce Taylor (14-0, 8 KOs) claimed the NABF title with a split-decision victory over Tsotne Rogava (13-2, 8 KOs). Two judges scored the 10-round bout 96-94 for Taylor, while the third had Rogava ahead 97-93.

Rogava’s jab gave him the better of the opening three rounds before Taylor increased his work rate through the middle rounds. Both men slowed in the ninth, but Taylor produced a strong finish, staggering Rogava with a left hook midway through the tenth.

Albuquerque’s Jose Luis Sanchez (15-7-2, 4 KOs) defeated Josh Torres (31-8-2, 17 KOs) by unanimous decision over 10 rounds. Sanchez won by scores of 98-92, 99-91, and 99-91.

Unbeaten heavyweight southpaw Sardius Simmons (11-0, 6 KOs) earned an eight-round unanimous decision over Cesar Navarro (15-5, 13 KOs). The judges scored it 78-74, 77-75, and 77-75.

Navarro started aggressively, pinning Simmons in a corner during the opening round. Simmons worked his way into the fight and outlanded Navarro through much of the middle rounds. Navarro rallied in the seventh, but Simmons finished with a competitive eighth to secure the decision.

In a four-round super middleweight bout, debutant Parminder Pannu (1-0) defeated Peter Balderas Jr. (2-4, 2 KOs) on referee David Rios’ scorecard, 40-36.

Sports.title: Dana White’s Shakur Split Weakens His American Boxing Plan
Sports.content:
Dana White dismissed talk that Conor Benn’s reported purse triggered Zuffa Boxing’s sudden split with Shakur Stevenson. Yet the real damage is far more practical: Zuffa lost its premier American headliner before ever using him to anchor a broadcast or sell the rest of its roster to domestic fight fans.

During Saturday’s post-fight press conference in London, White revealed that he initiated the separation during a phone conversation with Stevenson’s team.

“We were on a call one day, and I said, ‘Maybe it’s better if we all just go our separate ways.’ And everybody agreed,” White said. “That just didn’t work out. You win some, you lose some.”

When asked if Stevenson pushed for parity after seeing Benn’s reported $15 million payday for the Regis Prograis bout, White shut it down immediately.

“That’s completely not true. Completely not true,” White said.

Asked what Stevenson actually demanded, White clamped down on specifics.

“That’s between us. That’s business behind the scenes. If you want to ask Shakur that question, ask him that. I’m not going to talk about it,” White said. “We all decided to go our own ways, and everybody’s happy with the decision.”

White’s comments shoot down the rumor mill while keeping the financial mechanics under wraps. Without figures on the table, it remains impossible to tell whether Stevenson overplayed his hand or if Zuffa attempted to impose an MMA-style pay structure that elite boxing champions routinely reject.

The structural fallout for Zuffa is unmistakable. In modern boxing promotion, an expensive main event star operates as an engine for the entire evening. Fans tune in for the proven name, creating a massive captive audience for developmental talent on the undercard. Without Stevenson delivering eyeballs, Zuffa cannot expose its lesser-known prospects to large-scale viewership. The company must now shoulder the expense of building interest in raw talent from scratch.

Stevenson also presented an awkward commercial equation for White’s promotional philosophy. White sells high-octane violence and ruthless aggression. Stevenson delivers surgical, defensive brilliance that purists appreciate but casual fans rarely rush to purchase. If Stevenson sought superstar guarantees without bringing explosive mass appeal, the balance sheet became an uphill battle.

Replacing that caliber of stateside talent presents an immediate hurdle. Reporters pressed White on established American draws like David Benavidez, Jaron Ennis, and Jesse Rodriguez, pointing out that nearly every top-tier domestic fighter is locked into commitments with rival outfits.

“We’re like eight or nine months into this thing. We’ll see how it all plays out,” White said.

Patience works in matchmaking, but broadcast partners look for immediate, dependable fixtures on the calendar. Television executives commit serious capital to showcase proven stars, not to finance protracted rebuilding phases. Walking away from Stevenson avoids an untenable contract, but it strips Zuffa of its flagship American asset before the company staged its first major domestic show.

Ghana News.title: Seven dead and more than 100 injured after trains collide in Egypt
Ghana News.content:
At least seven people have died in a train crash near the Egyptian city At least seven people have died in a train crash near the Egyptian city of Giza, with more than 100 injured.

The country's railway authority said two trains travelling south from Giza and Cairo collided, causing several carriages to derail and fall down an embankment.

Images from the scene showed people looking inside overturned carriages for injured passengers as a massive emergency response was launched.

Egyptian President Abdul Fattah al-Sisi said he had ordered state authorities to "investigate the circumstances of the accident, and hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent".

The public prosecutor's office warned the death toll could rise.

Getty Images Men search a train carriage after it derailed in Egypt. One can be seen clambering inside what appears to be a passenger car that has been torn open.Getty Images

Uninjured passengers and bystanders searched derailed carriages for injured people

The government said hospitals in the area had been put "on heightened alert" as they dealt with a massive influx of patients.

Egypt's health minister Dr Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said people were being treated for broken bones and head injuries.

The Egyptian Red Crescent said it was providing aid and psychological support to victims and their families at the scene.

The driver of one of the trains was among those who died in the crash, the ministry confirmed.

The first train was travelling from Giza to Fayoum, south of Cairo, when it crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to Aswan, which was stationary on the tracks.

Images from the scene showed some carriages had overturned, with the body of at least one appearing to have split in two.

Getty Images People look on after train carriages derailed following a crash in EgyptGetty Images

Trains between Giza and the Upper Egypt region were suspended as cranes were dispatched to remove the wrecked trains. The railway authority has not said how long it expects this to take.

The collision occurred in the area between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Al-Ayyat, close to where Egypt's deadliest train tragedy occurred in February 2002, when a fire engulfed a passenger train travelling from Cairo to Luxor.

In that incident, more than 370 people were officially reported killed, although some estimates put the toll considerably higher.

Two further crashes in the area in 2009 killed dozens more.

On Sunday, calls in Egypt urged the transport minister to resign over the latest deadly rail disaster.

Foreign leaders and dignitaries have shared condolences and support for the victims.

Saudi Arabia's ministry of foreign affairs expressed "solidarity" with Egypt and wished those hurt a speedy recovery.

Turkey's ambassador to Egypt wrote on X that he extended "heartfelt condolences and sincere sympathy" to the victims, their families, and the Egyptian people. Giza, with more than 100 injured.

Ghana News.title: South Africa’s ANC records worst-ever results in local elections
Ghana News.content:
Voters cast their ballots at a polling station during South Africa's local government elections in Johannesburg

South Africa's ANC has recorded its worst-ever showing in local elections since Nelson Mandela led the country out of apartheid and into democracy more than 30 years ago, a result the party has called "catastrophic".

While it won the most votes of any party, the African National Congress took 30.76% of the overall vote, one-third down from the 46% it gained in 2021, and far from the 64.82% it had 20 years ago.

The story of its decline is also clear in the provinces and cities. The party won a majority in just one of the country's nine provinces, Limpopo. In 2021 it won six. It also won the most votes in just two of the eight cities, compared with six at the last local elections.

The Democratic Alliance (DA) came second overall with 24.64%, retaining majority control of the city of Cape Town. Former president Jacob Zuma's MK party came third overall with 9.76%, unseating the ANC as winner in the city of Durban, while the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF), led by Julius Malema, once seen as a serious challenge to the ANC, came fourth with 6.22%.

"This has been a very catastrophic outcome for the ANC," said secretary-general Fikile Mbalula on Saturday. "We knew this disaster was coming; we're staring at it. As we got into elections, the cost of living of our people was too high. The middle class have turned on the ANC in big numbers."

Entering the count centre tonight, South Africa's president and leader of the ANC Cyril Ramaphosa said: "We accept the will of the people however concerning it might be; we accept that this is how the people of South Africa in our towns, in our cities, in our metros have spoken - and this is their verdict; we accept it with humility. It is a decline that is concerning; that is how I characterise it."

It's a continuing decline for the ANC, which lost majority rule in the national elections in 2024 for the first time in its history. It then had to form a coalition government with a raft of other parties in what is now known as the GNU, or government of national unity.

While the Democratic Alliance made significant gains in the cities in these local elections, its overall vote share rose marginally from 21.83% in 2021, and was below the 26.9% it gained in 2016.

Voter turnout was 52.29%, an increase from 45.9% in 2021, when elections were held during the Covid pandemic.

"This election is delivering a devastating message to the ANC", said political analyst Susan Booysen. "It's an ANC in decline at local municipal level, at the metropolitan level, and when the results are reflected provincially and nationally, we see severe declines in ANC levels of support all around."

The decline in support is largely due to poor service delivery and infrastructure across the country, from water and power to sanitation. "These are huge problems," says Booysen, "and have really been affecting the lives of ordinary people, in the suburbs, in the townships, and in very dramatic ways."

The big picture looks even more bleak for the ANC. The party will elect a new leader next year as Cyril Ramaphosa comes to the end of his term. He is due to remain president until the next national elections in 2029, but few candidates are lined up to succeed him in either role.

"It is sort of the end of the liberation movement era in South Africa," said political analyst William Gumede, "and the dominance of the liberation movement since the end of apartheid. So the ANC is going to be a party that by 2029 could be the second biggest rather than the biggest party. It may actually spiral into a long period of just total infighting. This is a new era for South Africa's politics and also the ANC."

The elections also saw a significant shift in voting patterns, with the DA, traditionally known as the "white party" for attracting a largely white vote, gaining more black votes. "We're moving towards a post-racial voting pattern in South Africa," added Gumede.

South Africa now faces days of local coalition-building, with the three metropolitan municipalities in Gauteng, the country's powerhouse province, under particular scrutiny. The ANC may even be shut out of the cities of Johannesburg and Pretoria.

"We are now in a coalition country," said Gumede. "Essentially, what the voters are saying is, "Well, the ANC has dominated the last three decades; they didn't use their power to change society for the good, so we don't want the dominant parties anymore, whether at national level, provincial level, or rather now at a local level. We actually want coalitions. We want people to work together."

Parties now have 14 days from the moment results were announced to negotiate coalitions.

Ghana News.title: Top House Democrat ‘a hard yes’ on impeaching Hegseth
Ghana News.content:
Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth

The frontrunner to lead the US House of Representatives after Democrats take control of Congress in January has said he is "a hard yes" for impeaching Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth.

New York congressman Hakeem Jeffries told ABC's programme This Week that Hegseth had "abused his power, undermined our national security, and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran".

Outgoing Republican congressman Thomas Massie, a foe of President Donald Trump, has said he plans to introduce a resolution to impeach Hegseth as early as Monday.

In a statement to the BBC, the Pentagon said it had followed the law and that Hegseth would not be deterred by "phony investigations".

Congress returns to session this week after the Democrats' midterm elections landslide victory.

Massie's resolution contains eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth, including accusing him of violating the War Powers Resolution of 1973 for America's role in the war with Iran.

"I'm a hard yes on the Hegseth resolution," Jeffries told ABC on Sunday.

"Pete Hegseth has got to go," he continued.

'It won't work'

Jeffries - who is favourite to be the next House Speaker, the most powerful member in the lower chamber of Congress - has vowed that the newly empowered Democrats will serve as a check and balance on the Trump administration.

But he said after the midterms results that House Democrats were not currently focused on impeaching President Trump, who was impeached twice during his first term.

Last week, Hegseth released a nearly six-minute video urging Congress to approve the Pentagon's latest military budget request before the Republican-controlled legislature's final days end.

In the clip, he addressed talks of Massie's impeachment effort, calling the threat "sham articles".

"You see, their policies don't work. So, their obsession with political theatre disguised as power drives them to try to destroy their opponents," Hegseth said.

"It's all about the politics of personal destruction. Didn't work against President Trump and it won't work with me."

With more races still to be called, Democrats hold a 254-seat House majority, well beyond the 218 threshold needed to pass articles of impeachment.

But they will fall well short of the two-thirds Senate majority required to remove an official from office.

Ghana News.title: King Charles leads solemn Remembrance Sunday service at Cenotaph
Ghana News.content:
King Charles III led the nation in a solemn two-minute silence on Remembrance Sunday in London to honour veterans who had died in conflict.

On a stone-grey autumn morning, he laid a wreath at the Cenotaph in Whitehall before a march-past by 10,000 armed forces veterans.

That included a shrinking number of World War Two veterans, with 12 taking part this year, including 103-year-old Annie Duplock, who described it as a "very emotional day".

Meanwhile, the number of former prime ministers reached a record high, with nine lined up to lay wreaths, while Andy Burnham attended for the first time as the current occupant of No 10 Downing Street.

For the first time, Reform UK leader Nigel Farage had enough MPs in Parliament to qualify to lay a wreath alongside other major party leaders.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham laid a wreath at the Cenotaph

Queen Camilla and Catherine, Princess of Wales, watched the event from the balcony of the Foreign and Commonwealth Office

The Prince of Wales and the Princess Royal were among the royals in attendance, along with military chiefs, senior politicians, diplomats, and faith leaders, watched by large crowds squeezed behind railings along Whitehall.

Queen Camilla and the Princess of Wales watched from a balcony above the Cenotaph in the Foreign Office.

Among the flags on the roof of that Whitehall building was the Ukrainian blue and yellow. It went up when Russia invaded and four years later it is now visibly frayed - a reminder of the length of that war and of current threats.

At 11:00 GMT, as Big Ben's first strike echoed from the nearby Houses of Parliament, the two-minute silence filled the usually frenetic streets before the playing of the Last Post.

The King closed his eyes, and the crowds in Whitehall paused in thought, a rare moment of calm in the capital.

Veterans arrived at Whitehall ahead of the service

The poignant parade past the Cenotaph included representatives of about 340 different military and civilian groups, from the Royal Naval Association and the Royal Marines Association to Transport for London and the Royal National Lifeboat Institute.

Alongside them marched flotillas of disability scooters and families helping veterans in wheelchairs.

Those who took part in WW2 are now increasingly frail - and there were 12 participants in the march-past compared to 20 last year. The oldest participant this year was aged 105.

"In everlasting remembrance" the King wrote on the wreath he laid at the Cenotaph

Annie Duplock had joined the Land Army at the age of 16

Taking part for the first time was 103-year-old Annie Duplock, who had been part of the Land Army that had helped feed the country at war.

She had joined the Land Army in 1940 as a 16-year-old, having lied about her age, and worked on a farm in Leicestershire.

"I feel very honoured to be taking part in the parade and to represent the Land Girls. I'm very excited, although a little apprehensive as I don't quite know what to expect," she said.

"I think it will be a very emotional day, bringing back memories of all those who didn't return home. It will be lovely to be there and remember them."

(Top left to bottom right) former Prime Ministers Rishi Sunak, Liz Truss, Boris Johnson, Theresa May, Lord Cameron, Gordon Brown, Sir Tony Blair and Sir John Major

Archbishop of Canterbury Dame Sarah Mullally led those gathered at the Cenotaph in prayer

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the annual event was a time to "reflect on the selflessness and courage it takes to commit your life to protecting others".

He earlier announced that he wanted to tackle the problem of homelessness among ex-service personnel to "ensure that any veteran sleeping rough is offered appropriate accommodation before Christmas".

Mark Atkinson, the director general of the Royal British Legion, said: "As we come together on Remembrance Sunday, we pay tribute to all those who have served and sacrificed, from generations past to those still serving today."

Remembrance events took place across the country as thousands gathered to pay their respects to those who died in past conflicts.

First Minister of Scotland John Swinney placed a wreath at the Stone of Remembrance outside the City Chambers during an event in Edinburgh.

Veterans, military personnel and cadets also marched through the centres of British cities such as Manchester, Birmingham and Leeds.

A silent poppy drop was held as part of the Festival of Remembrance at Durham Cathedral while wreaths were laid at Canterbury Cathedral.

Separately, the Duke of Sussex was seen attending a Remembrance service in the market town of Brackley in Northamptonshire.

For more than a century, the national Remembrance event has been held around the Cenotaph.

The monument was built as a focal point for honouring those who had fought and died in World War One, including those who had no grave, and as a place to mourn for those families who might not be able to visit war cemeteries overseas.

The word "cenotaph" means "empty tomb" in Greek and it was designed by the architect Sir Edwin Lutyens in a simple, austere style, with no sense of triumphalism and with almost no decoration.

The monument had been originally built in 1919 as a temporary, plaster and wood structure. But it proved so popular with the public that it was replaced in 1920 with a permanent version, in the same design but in stone.

It was opened at 11:00 on 11 November 1920 by King George V. His great-grandson, Charles, was there again, on an overcast morning 106 years later, to continue paying respect.

Ghana News.title: White House vows to keep up immigration crackdown after midterms defeat
Ghana News.content:
US President Donald Trump's administration has vowed not to change course on its mass deportation plans after last week's midterm elections defeat.

"This administration will not slow down its efforts to arrest and deport criminal illegal aliens who terrorise our communities," the White House said in a statement to the BBC.

Trump's promotion on Friday of immigration hawk Stephen Miller to White House chief of staff had signalled no climbdown from the administration on border security.

Exit polls indicate immigration was the third most important issue for midterm voters, after the economy and the state of democracy.

In historically conservative states like Texas, a swing of Latino voters towards Democrats helped seal the party's landslide congressional majorities.

But multiple US officials sources told the BBC's US partner CBS that the administration had put the midterm losses down to concerns about the economy, affordability and the war with Iran, rather than its immigration crackdown.

The White House maintained on Sunday there would be no change of direction.

"There has never been a President stronger on immigration enforcement than President Trump," said White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) also said it would forge ahead.

"ICE is NOT backing away or slowing down," a DHS spokesperson told CBS.

"Under the leadership of President Trump and Secretary Mullin, DHS will continue to enforce our nation's laws and remove criminal illegal aliens from our streets."

Following Tuesday's results, Vice-President JD Vance had appeared receptive to adjusting their immigration strategy.

"I'm open to the idea that we should change enforcement - by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labour, for instance," Vance wrote in a lengthy online post reflecting on the results.

But the White House's posture appears to have hardened after Trump promoted Stephen Miller to chief of staff on Friday.

Miller is widely seen as the architect of the administration's hardline immigration policy during the first and second Trump presidencies.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) sources told CBS that in recent weeks officials have been instructed to aim for about 2,700 arrests of illegal immigrants per day, an increase from an earlier 2,000 daily arrest target.

Enforcement sweeps this year spurred anti-ICE demonstrations in cities including Chicago, Minneapolis and Los Angeles.

In Minneapolis, two US protesters, Renee Good and Alex Pretti, were fatally shot by immigration agents.

Ghana News.title: Nvidia launches investigation into CEO’s affair with suspected Chinese spy
Ghana News.content:
US tech giant Nvidia has opened an independent investigation following reports that its CEO, Jensen Huang, had a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.

The company, one of the world's most valuable, said its board had no reason to believe its secrets or national security were compromised, adding that the CEO was committed to continuing to lead the company.

Separately, Jensen Huang admitted to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children.

US intelligence officials believed that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report.

Jensen Huang said he took "full responsibility" for what he did, adding that he had fallen short of his responsibilities to Nvidia's employees, board and shareholders.

Nvidia is one of the world's largest companies and is seen as central to making the hardware for emerging AI technologies.

Its CEO said: "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

His statement continued: "Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, Nvidia's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully.

"I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American."

A separate statement issued by Nvidia's board of directors said it would begin an investigation in "light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort".

It continued: "The Board prioritises US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders.

"While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information."

Alice Huang, who is of no relation to Jensen Huang, is linked to Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed.

The company told the New York Times last month its current leadership took the allegations seriously and had appointed external legal advisers to conduct an internal investigation.

Nvidia is a central player in AI infrastructure, providing chips to leading AI model developers including OpenAI and Meta.

The microchip manufacturer is worth some $4.5 trillion, making it one of the most valuable companies ever.

China previously rejected allegations of an espionage operation targeting Nvidia's chief, calling the claims "groundless speculation".

US intelligence agencies monitored Alice Huang and concluded she was acting on behalf of the Chinese government, according to unnamed sources cited by The New York Times.

Surveillance reportedly revealed communications between Alice Huang and an American citizen, who was subsequently identified as Jensen Huang through a process known as "unmasking".

It remains unclear what information Alice Huang – who is also known as Huang Le – allegedly passed to Beijing, how valuable it was, or when she is believed to have begun gathering intelligence.

Alice Huang did not respond to the paper's request for comment.

Last week, members of Congress wrote to Jensen Huang, asking him to appear before them in the light of the reported relationship.

Three House Republican committee leaders asked the CEO to appear later in the month, to talk about Nvidia's "security protocols against foreign adversary espionage" given his reported relation Alice Huang.

"Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's [China's] access to sensitive US technology and information.

"The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge US technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress," the letter said.

Nvidia's AI chips have been a major focus of the rivalry between the US and China, and Washington has previously imposed controls on where its advanced products can be sold.

The H200, Nvidia's second most advanced semiconductor, had previously been restricted by Washington over concerns that it would give China's technology industry an edge over the US.

In January, the Trump administration said it would allow the company to sell its H200 chips to Chinese customers under certain conditions.

Ghana News.title: England await Guehi scan results after injury concern
Ghana News.content:
Manchester City defender Marc Guehi will undergo a scan for a hip complaint on Sunday to determine whether he can report for England duty this week.

The 26-year-old was substituted at half-time in City's loss to Nottingham Forest on Saturday, and manager Enzo Maresca said afterwards the centre-back requested to come off because of the injury.

Maresca did not specify Guehi's issue, but it is understood he has been troubled by the hip problem in recent weeks.

The fact he requested to be substituted has raised doubts about whether he will be available for England's UEFA Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain.

Guehi will undergo tests, although England's medical staff will likely want to assess the player before making a final decision.

Thomas Tuchel will hope the defender is cleared to play, with the former Crystal Palace captain a mainstay of his team since he took over as England head coach in January 2025.

Guehi started in all but one of England's World Cup games and in all four of the team's Nations League fixtures in September and October.

England face Croatia at Wembley on Thursday, 12 November, before travelling to Madrid to face World Cup winners Spain on Saturday, 15 November.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
