World.title: Lens’ nightmare week worsens with late Marseille defeat
World.content:
PARIS: RC Lens’ nightmare week continued ‌as they conceded a late goal to lose 2-1 at home to Olympique de Marseille in Ligue 1 on Sunday after a humiliating 9-1 thrashing ​in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Lens fell behind in the second minute when Amine Gouiri scored for Marseille, following a defensive error, but Florian Thauvin pulled them level in the 20th.

They appeared on course to earn a point until Keyliane Abdallah struck with eight minutes remaining, the 20-year-old following up after Gouiri’s initial effort was blocked, to condemn the hosts to a ‌third successive defeat ‌in all competitions.

The defeat left Lens ​11th ‌in ⁠Ligue 1 ​and ⁠extended a miserable run that began when Olivier Giroud scored a late winner for Lille in last weekend’s derby.

Wednesday’s Champions League defeat to Como equalled the heaviest in the competition’s history and marked another low for last season’s Ligue 1 runners-up, whose fortunes have declined sharply since Pierre Sage left to take charge of Crystal ⁠Palace.

His replacement Dino Toppmoeller lasted only a matter ‌of weeks and Yannick Cahuzac’s position ‌is now also under scrutiny.

Marseille, meanwhile, have ​climbed to fourth after overcoming ‌their sluggish start to the campaign. They have won five ‌successive Ligue 1 matches and also beat Bayer Leverkusen in the Europa League on Thursday.

Earlier, Belgian defender Nathan Ngoy scored Lille’s winner in a 2-1 victory at Rennes that lifted them to second.

Lille have 21 points, ‌two behind leaders Paris St. Germain and one ahead of third-placed Paris FC. Marseille are fourth ⁠on 18 ⁠points, above Olympique Lyonnais, who lost 2-0 at Brest on Sunday.

Nice continued their resurgence with a 2-0 win at Angers, their fourth victory in five league matches. Sofiane Diop opened the scoring in the second minute before Jonathan Clauss sealed the points in the 78th.

The result lifted Nice to sixth, while Monaco slipped to seventh after conceding a 90th-minute equalizer in a 1-1 draw at promoted Le Mans.

Monaco, beaten 3-1 by Paris FC last weekend, have gone five league matches without a win.

Substitute Erwan ​Colas equalized from a corner ​to earn Le Mans a valuable point and lift them to 15th, outside the relegation zone.

World.title: Nvidia announces probe into CEO Huang amid reports China spied on him
World.content:
NEW YORK: Chip giant Nvidia’s board announced Sunday it opened a probe into Chief Executive and co-founder Jensen Huang after he acknowledged an affair with a woman US officials say was working for Chinese intelligence.

Late last month, The New York Times reported that US intelligence officials concluded that the woman, a Chinese executive linked to a Singapore-based data center company called Megaspeed, had been funnelling information to Beijing.

The executive, Alice Huang — also known as Huang Le, and no relation to 63-year-old Taiwanese-born Jensen Huang — developed a close relationship with the Nvidia boss, the Times said.

In a message to company employees released Sunday, Huang acknowledged having an affair and apologized to both his family and company staff.

“I was unfaithful to my wife,” he said. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Asked about the report Sunday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he couldn’t comment, saying it was an “internal corporate matter.”

Jensen Huang is a key figure in the artificial intelligence revolution and close to President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly spoken out against regulating the industry so as not to let China gain the upper hand in the AI race.

The Times said Huang’s relationship with the other Huang could have given her insights into Trump’s thinking around AI. The issue of AI is likely to arise during Trump’s planned talks with President Xi Jinping later this month at a summit in China.

Nvidia said in a statement it opened an independent probe “in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” It did not name a country.

The statement added: “While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information.”

The Chinese government has dismissed the Times report as “groundless speculation.”

‘Black eye moment’

China is in a race for tech dominance with the United States, which restricts the export to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips.

Nvidia, a global leader in producing chips used to train and run AI models, is one of the world’s most valuable companies.

Megaspeed was under scrutiny for possibly steering Nvidia AI chips to China, the Times report said, citing unnamed sources briefed on the matter.

Trump was briefed on the intelligence findings about Huang’s relationship with the businesswoman roughly a year ago and chose not to act on the information, the Times report said.

Technology analyst Dan Ives, with the investment bank Yorkville Ives, said word of the probe is “a black eye moment” for Jensen Huang.

Ives predicted it will at the very least spark multiple congressional inquiries and “create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons.”

In the near-term Huang is expected to keep his job but risks being removed as Nvidia’s CEO depending on the board’s probe, Ives said in a statement.

“This will add risk to the stock as he is so important to the Nvidia story and strategy globally,” he said. “This will also increase major scrutiny regarding selling chips to China, which remains a key battleground issue in DC.”

World.title: Lopez double earns Liga leaders Barca win at Atletico
World.content:
MADRID: Fermin Lopez struck twice to help Barcelona come from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 on Sunday and move three points clear at the top of La Liga.

The Spanish champions lead second place Real Madrid, who beat Valencia 3-0 on Saturday, by three points with Atletico third and a further two points off the pace.

Giuliano Simeone fired Atletico ahead in a high-octane start, before Lopez pulled Barca level shortly before the interval at the Metropolitano stadium.

The 23-year-old Spain international netted the winner after 66 minutes when Lamine Yamal slipped him in, helping Barca triumph despite not being at their best.

Last season Atletico defeated Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals and also in the Copa del Rey, but the Catalans earned some measure of revenge here.

“Coming off last season, when they beat us... we knew what they were going to offer — a very difficult game,” Lopez told Movistar.

“It got tricky for us in the first half with their goal, but I think we knew how to come back and we had a great match.”

After criticism following defeats by Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid in recent weeks, Flick’s side proved they can handle themselves in big matches.

“We have the quality to win these matches... I totally believe in the team,” Flick told reporters.

“In the second half especially we did a great job today, it’s not easy to win here.”

Atletico coach Diego Simeone said his team performed well despite the result.

“I have nothing to complain about, we played the match we wanted to play,” he told reporters.

“I’m leaving here knowing that we are a work in progress, that we still have things to improve, and that obviously we have players who still need to keep growing.”

Barca mount comeback

The match started at a fast pace and both teams hit the woodwork in the opening stages.

Alvarez, who tried and failed to force a move from Atletico to Barca in the summer, rounded goalkeeper Joan Garcia but could not finish off the chance as the defense blocked his route to goal.

From the resulting corner Atletico defender Marc Pubill headed against the crossbar with Garcia beaten.

At the other end Pedri crashed a strike against the woodwork after being fed by Barca’s teenage star Lamine Yamal.

Atletico took the lead in the 10th minute, slicing Barca’s defense open. Alvarez crossed for Giuliano Simeone to turn home from close range.

Alvarez was denied by Garcia as Atletico looked for a second and Barca struggled to click into their top gears.

Despite their struggles they went in level at the break, with a goal out of nowhere.

Lopez’s path to the box was blocked but the ball bounced loose to the midfielder and he quickly smashed a strike past Jan Oblak.

Early in the second half Alvarez lobbed a good chance over the crossbar when running in on goal.

“He’s a great player, we love him... we need the best version of Julian Alvarez, without him we won’t get to where we want to be,” said Diego Simeone.

The forward came to rue the miss when Barcelona took the lead.

Yamal played a clever pass through Atletico’s defense and Lopez kept his cool to beat Oblak. It was his seventh league goal in 11 top flight appearances this season.

Barcelona kept Atletico at bay well in the final stages to take three points home from the capital before the international break.

Atletico captain Koke said his team would not let the defeat, their first in La Liga since September 5, upset them too much.

“I think the team had a really great first half. We had chances to kill off the game and we didn’t take them,” said Koke.

Earlier on fourth-place Real Betis earned a 2-0 win at Elche, while Real Sociedad, fifth, defeated Rayo Vallecano 1-0.

Villarreal beat Getafe 2-0 to move eighth and Celta Vigo and Levante shared a goalless draw.

World.title: Can Israel’s opposition end the Netanyahu era without agreeing on Palestine?
World.content:
BEIRUT: Gadi Eisenkot may be closer than any Israeli opposition figure in years to ending Benjamin Netanyahu’s grip on power, but replacing Israel’s longest-serving prime minister could prove easier than governing the country that Netanyahu leaves behind.

President Isaac Herzog announced on Saturday that the former military chief would be given the first opportunity to form a government after parties representing 67 members of the 120-seat Knesset recommended him for the job. Netanyahu received 46 recommendations, while the seven-member United Torah Judaism endorsed neither candidate.

On paper Eisenkot has a majority; in practice he commands only 48 seats.

His Yashar party won 21 in the Oct. 27 election, Naftali Bennett’s B’Yachad secured 12, Yair Golan’s Democrats took eight and Avigdor Lieberman’s Yisrael Beiteinu won seven. Netanyahu’s outgoing bloc holds 53, leaving the Arab-led Joint List, with 11 seats, and Ra’am, with eight, in the position of kingmakers.

The arithmetic looks simple; however, the political arithmetic is anything but.

Eisenkot can reach power by accepting Arab-party support, recruiting ultra-Orthodox factions, entering a unity government with Likud or persuading lawmakers to abandon Netanyahu. Each route would force someone in his camp to cross a line drawn during the campaign.

Reacting to the Oct. 27 election results, Meir Javedanfar, an Israeli commentator on Middle East conflicts, said: “History will remember that it was the Jewish PM of Israel, Benjamin Netanyahu, who tried to ruin Israel’s democracy, and it was the Arab citizens of Israel who saved it.”

Opposition leaders agree that Netanyahu has polarized Israeli society, weakened public institutions and avoided accountability for the Oct. 7, 2023, security failure. They can support a state inquiry, protections for the judiciary, repairs to the civil service and measures addressing the cost of living.

Palestine is where their shared program ends.

The parties disagree over who should govern Gaza, whether Israel should retain permanent military control there, whether settlements should expand and whether Palestinians should ever have an independent state.

A former chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces and member of Netanyahu’s wartime Cabinet, Eisenkot is not a conventional peace candidate. He is associated with the “Dahiya doctrine,” which advocates overwhelming force against areas from which Israel says hostile groups operate.

His son Gal was killed while serving in Gaza in December 2023. The loss gave Eisenkot an intensely personal connection to the war and reinforced his standing among Israelis who consider military service the foundation of citizenship.

His disputes with Netanyahu have focused less on whether Israel should use force than on how force is used, toward what strategic objective, and under whose accountable leadership.

Yashar promises a new national security doctrine, stronger borders, a reinforced military and expanded regional partnerships. It also supports compulsory military or national service for all citizens. Its platform speaks of maintaining a Jewish majority but does not explicitly endorse a Palestinian state.

Bennett’s B’Yachad wants Israel to remain behind its current military line in Gaza until Hamas is fully disarmed. If Hamas refuses, Bennett says Israel should disarm it by force. He opposes direct Israeli civil administration of Gaza but supports indefinite freedom for the Israeli military to operate there.

Former Israeli prime minister Naftali Bennett speaks during a B'Yachad (Together) party as the party presents their candidates ahead of Israel's legislative elections in Tel Aviv on September 6, 2026. (AFP)

His security program promises a larger and more lethal army, immediate attacks against enemy rearmament, and a move from containment to “decisive victory.”

Golan’s Democrats occupy the other end of Eisenkot’s bloc. They support an eventual two-state solution, oppose annexation in the West Bank and favor rebuilding Gaza under an alternative Palestinian administration supported by Arab and international partners.

They would be expected to resist expanded settlements, mass Palestinian displacement or an open-ended Israeli occupation.

Yair Golan (C), leader of HaDemokratim (The Democrats) party, marches with protesters during an anti-government demonstration in Tel Aviv on October 24, 2026, ahead of Israel's legislative election. (AFP)

Lieberman offers a third vision. His plan calls for dismantling the Palestinian Authority, abandoning the Oslo framework, preventing the establishment of a Palestinian state and applying Israeli sovereignty to Area C of the West Bank.

For Gaza, he advocates destroying Hamas’ military and civilian institutions before transferring administration to an outside actor.

Eisenkot’s prospective coalition therefore includes one party advocating two states, another determined to prevent Palestinian statehood and a third promising decisive military victory without explaining the political order that would follow it.

This is the coalition he must hold together before considering the parties outside it.

Ra’am leader Mansour Abbas has indicated that his party is prepared to join or support an Eisenkot government. Ra’am made history in 2021 when it entered the Bennett-Lapid coalition, becoming the first independent Arab party to participate in an Israeli government.

Abbas supports Hamas’ disarmament, potentially meeting one of Eisenkot’s conditions. His party’s priorities include investment in Arab municipalities, action against organized crime and recognition of underserved Bedouin communities.

Leader of the Arab Israeli party Ra'am (United Arab List), Mansour Abbas speaks during an election campaign event, ahead of Israel's legislative elections, in the Arab town of Ka'abiyye-Tabbash-Hajajre in Israel's Northern District on September 26, 2026. (AFP)

The Joint List has offered outside support without entering the government. That arrangement would allow its lawmakers to help remove Netanyahu while opposing policies they reject in Gaza and the West Bank.

The list supports ending the occupation and establishing a Palestinian state in the West Bank, Gaza and East Jerusalem. Its lawmakers have condemned attacks on civilians but declined Eisenkot’s demand that they describe Hamas as a terrorist organization that must be destroyed.

“We are willing to extend our hand in support in legislation and decisions that serve our political project and program,” Yousef Jabareen, head of the Joint List, told AFP news agency recently. He added: “Our positions are based on human rights and are supported by international law and international conventions.”

Yousef Jabareen, leader of Israel’s Arab-led Joint List political alliance, (C) and other members cheer at the alliance’s campaign headquarters in the northern Israeli city of Nazareth on October 27, 2026. (AFP)

With Ra’am’s eight votes and the Joint List voting in favor or abstaining, Eisenkot could theoretically defeat Netanyahu’s 53-seat bloc.

But Lieberman refuses to join a government that includes or depends on Arab parties. Bennett is also far less open to Arab participation than he was in 2021, reflecting the rightward shift in Israeli public opinion since Oct. 7 and the wars that followed.

The question is whether the votes of Palestinian citizens of Israel are accepted as a legitimate foundation for political power.

Netanyahu has long portrayed governments dependent on Arab lawmakers as inherently dangerous. If Eisenkot accepts that argument, he could make it impossible for the opposition to govern even after parties representing a Knesset majority recommended him.

If he rejects it, he could lose the nationalist partners he needs.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. (AP File)

The alternative is an agreement with Shas and United Torah Judaism. Together, the ultra-Orthodox parties hold 13 seats — precisely the number required to turn Eisenkot’s 48 into a majority of 61.

Yashar, B’Yachad and Yisrael Beiteinu campaigned on military or national service for all. Their voters include reservists and families who believe they have carried an unfair share of Israel’s wars. The ultra-Orthodox parties insist on protecting exemptions for religious students.

Eisenkot could compromise and become prime minister, but only by retreating from one of his clearest campaign commitments.

A unity government with Likud would provide a comfortable majority but could be even more politically corrosive. An opposition created to end the Netanyahu era would find itself governing alongside Netanyahu or a party still unwilling to break with him.

A prolonged caretaker scenario is not impossible. According to Daniel Shapiro, a former US ambassador to Israel, “Netanyahu may prefer to lead his current government in a caretaker role, refuse any compromises necessary to bring in additional partners, resume the war in Iran during government formation period, and take his chances in about six months.”

Avigdor Lieberman, chairman of the Israeli opposition party Yisrael Beytnu, speaking during a committee meeting at the Knesset. (AFP/File)

Israel has already tested the proposition that ideological enemies can govern together if they agree to avoid the Palestinian question.

The Bennett-Lapid “change government” formed in 2021 with eight parties spanning the nationalist right, center and Zionist left, together with Ra’am. Its members concentrated on budgets, public services and ending Netanyahu’s rule, while shelving their differences over the occupation.

The arrangement collapsed after right-wing defections and a dispute over renewing emergency rules that apply Israeli civilian law to Jewish settlers in the West Bank. The lesson was not merely that a diverse coalition is fragile. It was that maintaining the occupation is itself a policy requiring constant legislation, funding and military decisions. There is no neutral status quo.

An Eisenkot government would face the same structural problem but in more dangerous regional conditions. It could postpone final-status negotiations, but not decisions on Gaza, settlements, settler violence, Palestinian governance or Israeli military operations.

A major attack could drag the coalition toward Bennett and Lieberman. A large Israeli offensive or annexation initiative could drive the Democrats and Arab parties away.

Eisenkot’s best hope may be a limited “repair government” with a fixed timetable and deliberately narrow mandate: investigate Oct. 7, restore state institutions, pass a budget, rebuild border communities and establish clearer national-security decision-making.

Israeli left-wing activists hold placards and chant slogans during a demonstration outside the home of Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, in Herzliya on October 29, 2026, calling for the formation of a government that includes Arab parties. On October 28, Israeli President Isaac Herzog expressed hope that a new round of elections could be avoided, as a fiercely contested vote failed to produce a clear winner—a situation that has forced Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the opposition to explore all available options, potentially making Israeli Arab parties the "kingmakers."

A coalition agreement could rule out both annexation and immediate recognition of Palestinian statehood, while supporting a regional mechanism for Gaza’s reconstruction and preventing Hamas from rearming.

Eisenkot has assembled a majority that agrees that Netanyahu should go. “Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy,” he said on X after the election results were announced.

However, he has not yet assembled one that agrees on what Israeli security is meant to achieve, what political rights Palestinians should possess or whether Arab citizens can determine who governs Israel.

That is why his coalition is possible and perhaps impossible at the same time. It may be strong enough to remove Netanyahu. Whether it can survive the first crucial decision that follows is another matter.

World.title: Night sky
World.content:
Discover the night sky through a guided stargazing experience with expert storytellers at the historic AlUla Fort. The one-hour sessions take place on Nov. 13-14. Admission is free with advance booking required.

Further details and reservations are available at experiencealula.com.

World.title: Merz says will name Aigner as Germany’s first woman president
World.content:
BERLIN: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Sunday he intended to appoint Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner as the country’s next president, in 2027, making her the first woman in the post.

He made his announcement at a dinner for leaders of his center-right CDU party, confirming information leaked last week by party sources.

Aigner, 61, belongs to the CSU, the Bavarian sister party of the CDU.

Aigner’s nomination by Merz virtually guarantees her election on January 30, as those voting are almost all drawn from Germany’s two parliamentary chambers.

Currently speaker of the southern state’s regional assembly, she would replace outgoing President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, a Social Democrat, in the largely ceremonial post.

Steinmeier, who took office in 2017, will reach the limit of two five-year terms in March 2027.

German political practice is that coalition parties agree on a common candidate for the job. The president is meant to be above party politics, representing the moral conscience of the country.

The current ruling coalition is made up of the CDU, the CSU and the Social Democrats of the SPD.

‘Perfect candidate’

The SPD has frequently voiced its support for Aigner as president.

During the chancellorship of Angela Merkel, she served as agriculture minister, winning the respect of politicians outside her own party.

Dietmar Woidke, one regional SPD leader, told the news website Politico that she would be the “perfect candidate” for the job.

“She knows German politics like the back of her hand,” he said. “She’s accessible. She likes people, knows how to listen and people listen to her,” he added.

Her appearances in traditional dress at Germany’s beer festivals have also helped raise her profile in Bavaria.

And her way of dealing with the far-right AfD party in the Bavarian regional parliament is admired for being both firm and courteous.

At a time of increased political polarization, and as the anti-migrant, pro-Russian AfD is registering a record 28 percent in opinion polls, her admirers see her as a potential calming influence.

Aigner was born in Bavaria to parents who ran an electricity company. She survived a brush with cancer in her youth, when a tumor had to be removed from her back.

After technical studies, she worked as an electronics technician with a helicopter builder before moving into local and then federal politics.

World.title: US launches task force to disrupt land transit routes into Iran
World.content:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump said Sunday that a new task force is in place to disrupt land routes into Iran that the US military says are used for shipments of weapons and illicit materials.

US Central Command on Saturday announced the formation of a 20-member team to expand on a US naval blockade of Iranian ports during the eight-month war.

“Task Force Iron Gate is in full force and effect in the Islamic Republic of Iran. Coupled with history’s greatest Naval Blockade, very little gets into, or out of, Iran!” the president posted on his Truth Social platform.

CENTCOM chief Admiral Brad Cooper said in Saturday’s statement that the force “will further constrain Iran’s ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military.”

The team of both civilian and military personnel based in Florida would coordinate with US government agencies on “preventing the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials, and illegal revenue streams across Iran’s land borders and the Caspian Sea,” the statement added.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said Washington’s latest bid “will fail” and will not bring about economic collapse in the Islamic republic.

“The United States will never be able to impose the economic blockade it is pursuing and proposing under various names and through different plans,” Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebi said, according to Fars news agency.

“The Americans will not achieve their objective of exerting extreme economic pressure to bring about the collapse and disintegration of Iran’s economy.”

Mohebi added that the United States would be “powerless to block” communication channels between Iran and neighboring countries.

CENTCOM said that the naval blockade on Iranian ports had “prevented Iran from exporting more than $25 billion in crude oil.”

In August, Washington announced what it called an “economic asphyxiation” campaign on Iran aimed at strangling its already battered economy.

Those measures were in response to Tehran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, a key conduit for global oil supplies, where Iranian forces have regularly targeted vessels that attempted to cross without authorization.

World.title: Trump says deportation policy was ‘too tough’: CBS interview
World.content:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said that his mass deportation of undocumented immigrants was “too tough,” according to an excerpt of an interview with CBS aired Sunday.

Asked about his deportation policy, Trump told CBS’ “60 Minutes“: “I think it was too tough...I think it might be too tough.”

The excerpt was published by CBS on X ahead of a broadcast of the interview on network TV later Sunday. It was recorded after the Republican Party’s heavy loss in midterm elections on Tuesday.

While Trump has won some domestic support for securing the US southern border, his administration’s aggressive push to deport millions of undocumented migrants has drawn widespread criticism.

However, Trump on Friday appointed the architect of that hard-line policy, Stephen Miller, as his chief of staff on Friday, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback after the Republican election loss.

Miller has been synonymous with scenes of masked immigration agents committing violence after he backed federal agents who shot and killed two Americans early this year.

World.title: Train collision in Egypt’s Giza kills 4, injures 88: health ministry
World.content:
Al Ayyat – Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital on Sunday, derailing several carriages, killing four and injuring dozens, according to the authorities.

Egypt’s railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to the city of Aswan.

The health ministry said an initial count put the toll from the crash at four passengers killed, with 88 others currently being treated for injuries in hospitals around the Giza area.

State-owned media had earlier reported 120 people were wounded, without clarifying the degree of injury.

President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said he was following the accident “with great concern”, and had directed authorities to conduct an urgent investigation to “hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent”.

Emergency crews used cranes to remove the wreckage, the authority said.

Several carriages lay on their side, AFP journalists at the scene reported. One end of a train had crumpled into a mangle of steel, while the end of the other — spliced open in the impact — had toppled off the tracks into an adjacent farm.

First responders and passersby helped lift one of the victims out of the wreckage in a black body bag, AFP images showed.

Authorities said they had launched an investigation into the cause of the crash, which occurred in Giza’s Al-Ayyat area, the site of Egypt’s worst-ever rail disaster.

In 2002, more than 370 people were killed when a fire swept through a train carrying holiday travellers south of Cairo.

In 2009, multiple train crashes in the area killed dozens.

Egypt’s 110 million people depend heavily on rail transport, but the network — one of the largest in Africa — has suffered repeated deadly accidents.

Over the past decade, Egypt has poured billions of dollars into updating its transport infrastructure, including new highways and high-speed rail lines, but has yet to overhaul much of its ageing rail network.

World.title: Iraq reportedly delivers US message to Iran during Tehran visit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – According to sources cited by Saudi-owned Al Hadath television, an Iraqi delegation headed to Tehran for an eight-hour diplomatic trip to convey a message from the United States to Iranian leaders.

The alleged visit coincides with rising tensions between Washington and Tehran, with Iraq increasingly aiming to position itself as a diplomatic middleman between the two nations.

The allegation was carried by Iran International and other Iranian media sites, and it linked the delegation’s travel to a recent phone call between US President Donald Trump and Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, as well as a visit to Baghdad by US Special Envoy Tom Barrack.

However, neither Iraqi nor Iranian officials have officially acknowledged the claimed mission.

The identity of the delegation members, the nature of the supposed American message, and Tehran’s reaction are unclear.

The accusations come after a November 6 phone call between Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein and his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi, during which Hussein suggested forming a committee of regional foreign ministers to visit Washington and Tehran in an attempt to defuse tensions.

Iraq’s diplomatic attempts take place amid a background of differences over Iran’s nuclear program, security in the Strait of Hormuz, and the actions of Iran-aligned armed organizations in Iraq.

Baghdad has tight political and economic ties with Tehran while simultaneously working with Washington on security issues, putting Iraq in a potentially advantageous position to facilitate indirect contact between the two administrations.

World.title: Turkey to gradually hand over military base to Iraq as Baghdad-Ankara ties strengthen
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Turkey will begin taking steps to gradually transfer control of the Bashiqa-Zilkan military base in northern Iraq to the Iraqi federal government, according to a joint announcement issued on Sunday, November 8.

According to the Office of Iraq’s Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, Baghdad and Ankara have also agreed to set up a joint security coordination committee to monitor efforts to restore full Iraqi government authority in Sinjar, Nineveh Governorate, and to end the presence of armed groups operating outside state control.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan struck an agreement in New York on September 23, leading to the announcement.

The two heads of state agreed to coordinate security measures in northern Iraq and plan for the eventual handover of the Turkish military station.

Turkey maintained a presence at the Bashiqa-Zilkan base near Mosul during the 2015 anti-ISIS battle.

However, the deployment sparked long-standing tensions, with Baghdad frequently objecting to Turkish forces operating on Iraqi soil without federal authority.

Turkey has also maintained military bases and carried out cross-border operations in northern Iraq against the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK), which Ankara deems a terrorist group.

Baghdad has condemned transgressions of Iraqi sovereignty while expanding cooperation with Turkey to combat the group’s operations.

In April 2024, Erdoğan visited Baghdad and signed agreements on security, commerce, energy, water management, and infrastructure development, leading to an improvement in relations between the two nations.

In August 2024, Iraq and Turkey inked a military and security cooperation pact to improve information sharing, counterterrorism coordination, and military training.

Beyond security, Baghdad and Ankara are pursuing big economic projects, such as the Development Road Project, which intends to link Iraq’s southern ports to Turkey and European markets via new transportation infrastructure.

The anticipated surrender of Bashiqa-Zilkan is another step toward settling a long-standing border conflict, while Turkey continues to retain military posts in northern Iraq.

World.title: Chelsea shocked by Sunderland, Liverpool cruise
World.content:
London – Chelsea suffered a shock 1-0 defeat at Premier League strugglers Sunderland, while Liverpool got back on track with a 3-1 win against lowly Crystal Palace on Sunday.

Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea arrived at the Stadium of Light hoping to bolster their bid to qualify for the Champions League via a top-four finish.

Instead, they departed red-faced after an embarrassing loss to third-bottom Sunderland, who celebrated a league victory for only the second time this season.

Fifth-placed Chelsea have already been beaten four times in 10 league matches under former Real Madrid boss Alonso.

Chelsea were rocked in the 36th minute when Enzo Le Fee converted a penalty after Brian Brobbey was up-ended by Levi Colwill.

Blues boss Xabi Alonso was furious that Chelsea were not given a foul on Cole Palmer in the build-up to the spot-kick.

Liverpool had been beaten by Arsenal in the Premier League and Fenerbahce in the Champions League before arriving in south London, sparking pointed questions about Andoni Iraola in the former Bournemouth manager’s first season in charge at Anfield.

But Alexis Mac Allister headed Liverpool in front at Selhurst Park from Dominik Szoboszlai’s cross after 40 minutes.

Florian Wirtz bagged Liverpool’s second with a composed finish from Bradley Barcola’s cross in the 54th minute.

It was Wirtz’s first league goal this season and only the second in all competitions for the inconsistent German playmaker this term.

Alexander Isak finished off Wirtz’s pass in the 89th minute to wrap up fourth-placed Liverpool’s much-needed victory after a two-game losing streak.

It was Liverpool’s fourth consecutive away league win this season.

Eddie Nketiah’s stoppage-time penalty after a foul by Milos Kerkez was no consolation for Palace.

Palace manager Pierre Sage — hired to replace Oliver Glasner in the close-season is on the brink of being sacked after his side slumped to the bottom of the table following their seventh defeat in 10 league matches.

– Seagulls flying high –

Brighton extended their superb start to the season, climbing to second place with a 2-0 win against Brentford at the Amex Stadium.

While Fabian Hurzeler’s side might not have the staying power to challenge Arsenal for the title, they have established themselves as contenders for a Champions League place.

Diego Gomez’s 25-yard rocket gave the Seagulls the lead in the 15th minute.

Brentford striker Igor Thiago was sent off for clattering Chema Andres in the face midway through the first half.

Pascal Gross doubled Brighton’s advantage with a 42nd minute penalty after Keane Lewis-Potter fouled Luka Vuskovic.

The Seagulls’ sixth win in their last seven league games lifted them above third-placed Manchester City and within five points of champions Arsenal, who beat Hull on Saturday.

Evanilson maintained his hot streak in Bournemouth’s 2-1 win at Ipswich.

The Cherries’ Brazilian forward struck with a clinical finish in the fifth minute, taking him to seven goals in his last eight games.

An own goal from Leif Davis in the 46th minute increased Bournemouth’s lead and Jack Clarke’s 73rd minute penalty wasn’t enough to rescue Ipswich.

In Sunday’s late game, Manchester United manager Michael Carrick cannot afford a defeat against Aston Villa at Old Trafford as he fights to save his job ahead of the international break.

United are without a victory in their last seven league games and have won just once in the top-flight this term.

They ended a miserable nine-match winless run in all competitions by coming from two goals down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday.

smg/ea

World.title: Spain’s Alcaraz wins Paris Masters for first time
World.content:
Paris – Carlos Alcaraz gained a measure of revenge on Ben Shelton on Sunday as the seven-time Grand Slam champion beat the American 7-6 (7/5), 7-5 to win the Paris Masters for the first time.

In defeating the man that ended his US Open title defence earlier this season, the 23-year-old Spaniard claimed the ninth 1000-level title of his career.

Unlike their five-set quarter-final epic in New York two months ago, the clash in Paris lasted just under two hours.

Ahead of the ATP Finals, which run November 15-22 in Turin, world number three Alcaraz now holds five tour-level titles this year — only the injured Jannik Sinner has more with six.

In Italy, he will be seeking a first coronation at the season-ender.

After winning two French Opens and now the Paris Masters, Alcaraz is undefeated in title matches in the city.

But not for the first time in the French capital, Alcaraz won the title by saving match points en route — this time against Taylor Fritz in the quarter-finals in scenes reminiscent of his iconic Roland Garros final win against Italian Sinner last year.

For world number four Shelton, it was a first defeat in a Masters final after winning his two previous appearances in showpiece matches at that level– both coming in the last two editions of the Canadian Open.

– ‘Ten out of ten’ –

Serving at 1-2 in the first set, Alcaraz flirted with danger as he offered up four break points, but dug in to secure the hold when Shelton misfired at the end of a seven-minute long game.

Shelton then found himself two break points down in the seventh game but responded with a perfect drop volley and blistering passing shot to bring up deuce, before holding and keeping his nose in front.

Although both players threatened on the other’s serve and drew repeated gasps from the crowd with some audacious shot-making, the opener nonetheless required a tie-break to separate them.

A Shelton error at 4-4 followed by a leaping backhand smash by Alcaraz brought up two set points.

The first came and went when Alcaraz thundered the ball into the top of the net cord and the expectant arena froze in time as it rose and fell in seeming slow motion, only to land on the Spaniard’s side of the court.

Alcaraz was not to be denied a second time, however, as Shelton overcooked a forehand on the next point to cede the opener.

At 2-2 in the second set, Shelton let out a bellow of frustration after missing a groundstroke at 15-30 on Alcaraz’s serve, but the American could smile at the end of the game as a double fault and missed forehand produced the first break of the match.

Alcaraz had said after booking his spot in the final that his reflexes would need to be “ten out of ten” when facing Shelton’s serve and they were just that three games later as he levelled the set at four-all.

A deft exchange of angled drop shots ended by an Alcaraz winner down the line brought the Spaniard’s finger to his ear and the crowd again to their feet as Shelton suddenly found himself serving to keep the final alive.

He did so at the first time of asking but when required to serve again to force a breaker, Shelton cracked as Alcaraz again pounced to seal the title with a flicked backhand winner.

World.title: Iraq accelerates completion of 1,640 MW Anbar power plant
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi has authorized authorities to repay overdue payments to the Chinese business that is building the Anbar Combined-Cycle Power Plant, a significant electrical project with a projected capacity of 1,640 megawatts.

The decision was issued at a meeting with business executives on Sunday, November 8, 2026, during which Al-Zaidi stressed the importance of maintaining construction quality and completing the project’s technical criteria.

SEPCOIII, a Chinese engineering and construction firm linked with state-owned PowerChina, is implementing the project.

The project, near Hit in Iraq’s western Anbar Governorate, is being built for the Iraqi Ministry of Electricity.

The facility will be powered by four gas turbines and two steam turbines, with combined-cycle technology used to create extra energy from heat generated during gas-fired power production.

Construction started in 2013 but was halted after the Islamic State group’s control of sections of Anbar.

Work restarted in late 2022, with the Chinese contractor taking over responsibility for finishing the project.

The plant is scheduled to receive natural gas from Anbar’s Akkas gas field.

The connecting pipeline must be completed, and stable fuel supplies are still required before the plant can be fully operational.

Once finished, the Anbar power plant is projected to improve energy supply across the province and add producing capacity to Iraq’s national grid.

World.title: Iraq’s Kurdish parties face government split as Baghdad’s influence grows
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Political disputes between the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), headed by Masoud Barzani, and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), led by Bafel Talabani, have prompted fears about the possibility of two opposing governments in Iraq’s Kurdistan.

The issue erupted when the KDP convened a parliamentary session in Erbil without the PUK’s participation.

Bafel Talabani, the head of the PUK, later announced his party’s resignation from the regional government, increasing the likelihood of a breakaway administration centered in Sulaymaniyah.

The KDP, headed by former Kurdistan Region President Masoud Barzani, is the region’s major political party, having primary bases in Erbil and Duhok.

The PUK, led by Bafel Talabani, the son of former Iraqi President Jalal Talabani, has its major stronghold in Sulaymaniyah.

Despite strong political conflicts, the two parties have traditionally shared power in the autonomous territory.

The widening split comes as Iraq’s federal government in Baghdad strengthens its control over disputed territory, notably Kirkuk and sections of Nineveh province, including Mosul.

Following the Kurdistan Region’s independence vote in 2017, Baghdad reasserted federal sovereignty over Kirkuk and numerous contested territories.

Mosul, however, remains under federal control, with Kurdish groups vying for political power in the surrounding districts.

A sustained schism between Barzani’s KDP and Talabani’s PUK might erode the Kurdistan Regional Government’s bargaining power with Baghdad over oil income, public-sector wages, budget transfers, and disputed territory.

The likelihood of rival Kurdish administrations has heightened fears about political fragmentation, possibly increasing Baghdad’s clout as the two parties battle to reach an agreement on a single regional government.

World.title: Erbil flash floods kill two, cause widespread damage
World.content:
Erbil (IraqiNews.com) – At least two people have died and widespread property damage has been reported after overnight flash floods struck Erbil, in Iraq’s Kurdistan Region, on Saturday, November 7.

Erbil’s governor acknowledged the deaths as rescue crews continued to react to floods in the city and neighboring regions. The casualties were believed to be a five-year-old youngster and a 24-year-old adult.

The flooding occurred when torrential rains inundated areas of the city, causing damage to houses, businesses, and infrastructure, with preliminary estimates indicating damage in the tens of millions of dollars.

According to Iraq’s Kurdistan Region Meteorological Department, Erbil received roughly 70 millimeters of rain in 24 hours.

For instance, Halabja got 80.6 millimeters over the same time with no corresponding destruction.

The disparity has sparked concerns about Erbil’s drainage infrastructure, urban planning, and preparation for inclement weather, especially given the city’s rapid urban development in recent years.

The catastrophe has also sparked political criticism, with media sources linked with opposing Kurdish political groups trading allegations about infrastructure management and government accountability.

Critics contend that recurring floods demonstrate the need for more investment in stormwater drainage infrastructure and better urban design to safeguard people and businesses.

Emergency response efforts continue as officials analyze the full scope of the devastation and aid impacted populations.

World.title: Watch: Diwali lights up Srinagar's Lal Chowk as tourists, locals celebrate at Ghanta Ghar
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Thousands of earthen lamps lit up Srinagar's iconic Lal Chowk on Sunday evening as tourists and local residents came together to celebrate Diwali around the city's historic clock tower, popularly known as Ghanta Ghar.

Dozens of tourists gathered at the clock tower and lit diyas, illuminating the area around the landmark.

Local Hindus and Muslims also joined the celebrations, with people lighting firecrackers.

Ankush Chatterjee, a tourist from Kolkata, said he was delighted to celebrate the festival in Kashmir. "We are delighted to celebrate this year's Diwali in Kashmir. The atmosphere here is radiant," he told PTI.

Diwali celebrations at Ghanta Ghar have become a regular sight in recent years, with tourists and residents gathering at Lal Chowk to mark the festival.

Elsewhere in the Valley, security personnel celebrated Diwali by lighting lamps at their camps and distributing sweets.

World.title: 'Why funding only for temples?' Congress's Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury on Bengal's Rs 1,000-crore plan

Speaking to reporters on the occasion of Kali Puja and Diwali, Chowdhury said the country did not belong to any one religion and that the government should adopt an inclusive approach.

"There are Gurdwaras and mosques, too; why is funding given only to temples? If resources are to be allocated, it must be done for everyone, for people of all religions. Our country does not belong to just one religion," he said.

He added that resources should be made available to people of all religions and urged the government not to create divisions among religious communities.



He also appealed to the government not to create divisions between communities and called for an approach that included everyone.

World.title: Watch: Sonia, Priyanka take a trip down memory lane, recall Diwali with Rajiv Gandhi
World.content:
Screengrab from the video posted by Sonia Gandhi on social media.

NEW DELHI: Veteran Congress leader Sonia Gandhi and her daughter, Priyanka Gandhi, revisited memories of Diwali celebrations with former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi.In a conversation shared on social media, Sonia Gandhi recalled her fondness for Diwali, describing the elaborate decorations, traditional rituals and festive gatherings that marked the celebrations."Oh, Diwali I loved. So, Diwali was always beautiful," she recalled in a video shared on her Instagram account.Recalling the traditional rituals, Sonia said a Ganesh idol was placed at the entrance of the house, where the first diya of the celebrations was lit. She added that the idol is now kept at her residence."At the entrance, there used to be a Ganesh Murti, which is now in my house. And so, we would do the first lighting of the diya in front of Ganesh Ji's Murti. And it was always decorated. In those days, we didn't have those little lights everywhere, but we had diyas everywhere - around the pond, all along the roof, veranda, and along the path, wherever there was a path. So, it was very pretty," she said.Priyanka Gandhi, the MP from Wayanad, also recalled how festivals were celebrated with great enthusiasm, with people from different walks of life gathering in the Gandhi family's garden.Sonia remembered how the family would sometimes get carried away with firecrackers, while Priyanka recalled how her father, Rajiv Gandhi, would take them to Chandni Chowk in Old Delhi to buy crackers."Papa used to take us to Chandni Chowk to buy crackers. We used to go to Old Delhi to buy crackers," Priyanka recalled.Sonia also remembered phuljhadis, or traditional sparklers, saying she enjoyed them, although she was less enthusiastic about some of the noisier fireworks.Beyond the lights and firecrackers, Sonia said the atmosphere during the festive season remained particularly memorable. Recalling the weather during those celebrations, she spoke about the clear blue skies that formed the backdrop to the festivities."Weather at that time was beautiful. Blue skies and all, which you hardly see now. Yeah, it was lovely," she said.Sonia also recalled that festivals were marked by Kashmiri cuisine and a traditional sweet rice preparation, a culinary tradition that continues in the family."And then, on festivals, we always used to have Kashmiri food and that sweet rice, like that, which we still make, by the way," she said.Sonia Gandhi has also documented several personal experiences and significant moments from her life in her memoir, titled *Belonging: A Journey of Love*. The book is scheduled to be launched on November 10.The memoir chronicles Sonia Gandhi's journey, from her childhood in post-war Italy and her romance that brought her to India to the personal losses that profoundly shaped her life and her relationship with her adopted country.In the book, the 79-year-old Congress veteran, who holds the distinction of being the party's longest-serving president, revisits her childhood in Italy, her relationship with Rajiv Gandhi during their time at Cambridge, and the assassinations of her mother-in-law, former prime minister Indira Gandhi, and her husband, Rajiv Gandhi.

World.title: 3 Nigerian nationals arrested in Delhi for staying without valid documents

NEW DELHI: Three Nigerian nationals were arrested by the Delhi Police for allegedly staying in India without valid documents and subsequently sent to a detention centre, news agency PTI reported citing officials on Sunday.

Following their arrest, they were produced before the foreigners regional registration office (FRRO) and later sent to Sewa Sadan detention centre in Lampur, officials said.

World.title: Nvidia investigating reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence
World.content:
Nvidia is opening an investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort,” the company's board of directors said Sunday (November 8, 2026).

The announcement came after Mr. Huang acknowledged to the board that he had been intimate with a business executive whom U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing, The New York Times reported.

Mr. Huang apologised in a message to the company, according to the Times. “I was unfaithful to my wife,” he said. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Nvidia's board said in a statement it has “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised,” but that its inquiry would examine all available information. Mr. Huang “fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it,” the board said.

Mr. Huang, 63, will remain CEO during the investigation.

The Times reported last month that U.S. intelligence agencies had discovered that Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, and determined that she was feeding information directly to Beijing. The two are not related, according to the Times.

Ms. Alice Huang was previously a television reporter in China before becoming a top executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, which has become one of Nvidia's biggest customers in Southeast Asia. Megaspeed bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the past two years, according to the Times.

World.title: Saudi Arabia turns to Syria for help as fighting with Houthis escalates
World.content:
Syria is preparing to send fighters to Saudi Arabia to deploy along its border and potentially help it fight Iranian-backed rebels in neighbouring Yemen, three officials with knowledge of the plans told The Associated Press.

Syrian military advisers have already deployed to Saudi Arabia, but no fighters have been sent to Yemen, according to a regional official and two Syrian officials, all of whom spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to comment publicly.

Officials in Saudi Arabia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Fighting escalated this summer in Yemen between the Houthi rebels and the government's Saudi-backed forces. The Houthis have also launched direct and deadly attacks on Saudi Arabia in what is the latest front in the regional conflict that began in February when the US and Israel attacked Iran.

Syria, which has a supply of battle-hardened fighters after a long civil war, has so far stayed on the sidelines.

Saudi Arabia has an array of U.S.-supplied fighter jets and missile defences but has been unable to defeat the Houthis in past rounds of conflict.

While Saudi Arabia’s other allies have been reluctant to commit ground forces to its fight with the Houthis, the Syrian government is beholden to it. The Saudis provided funds to Syrian rebels during that country's civil war and have promised much-needed financial assistance for Syria's postwar reconstruction.

Syrian fighters set to deploy to Saudi-Yemen border

A Syrian official said that an initial force of about 600 Syrian special forces fighters is expected to be deployed to Saudi Arabia in the coming week.

The official said that a Syrian delegation led by Khaled Khattab, commander of the 82nd Division, had recently made a two-week visit to Saudi Arabia. A second Syrian official said 36 Syrian military officials visited a command and operations room in Jeddah staffed by Saudi and Yemeni officials and received briefings on the different front lines and areas of operation.

A regional official with knowledge of the discussions said Syria had already deployed a “small number of advisers” to Saudi Arabia, where they helped train Yemeni forces inside the kingdom.

Syria may enter defence agreement with Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan

An unnamed diplomatic official in Syria dismissed reports that Syrian forces were headed to Yemen, the country's state-run news agency, SANA, reported on Saturday (November 7, 2026). The official said the agreement with Saudi Arabia focuses on training its military forces and building its capabilities.

Syrian officials have said publicly that the country is discussing the possibility of joining a joint defence agreement recently signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan.

The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, signed in August, commits the three countries to regard an attack against one as an attack on all three, and to deepen military cooperation in other ways.

The two Syrian officials said that a decision had already been made — but not publicly announced — for Syria to join the Mecca pact, while the regional official said talks were still ongoing.

One concern is that Syria might ask the other countries for their support against Israel, the regional official said. Following the ouster of Syria's former President Bashar Assad in December 2024, Israeli forces seized control of a UN-patrolled buffer zone in southern Syria and have occupied it since.

Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa says his government does not seek a conflict with Israel and has called for Israeli forces to withdraw.

Syria and Saudi Arabia announced last week that they had signed a military cooperation agreement, without providing details. During a visit to Riyadh by Mr. al-Sharaa, the Saudi government agreed to lend Syria more than $400 million for postwar reconstruction of homes and basic infrastructure.

Change in Syria's stance on the regional war

Syria has turned down proposals by U.S. President Donald Trump for its forces to intervene against the Iran-backed Hezbollah militant group in Lebanon. Mr. al-Sharaa has said his focus is on rebuilding Syria after its lengthy civil war and that he wants to avoid getting embroiled in new conflicts.

But Saudi Arabia has been key to its reintegration into the Arab world, which had largely shunned Syria under Assad's rule.

Syrian involvement in the fighting against the Houthis in Yemen could expose it to attacks by militias in neighbouring Iraq that are allied with the Houthis.

World.title: Trump and his Justice Department stand defiant as Democrats ready an investigative blitz
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump and his Department of Justice are taking a combative stance toward Democrats after their election victories in the midterms, signalling intense conflict to come as lawmakers prepare aggressive investigations into the executive branch next year.

Mr. Trump set the tone, declaring on social media that investigative requests already made by Democrats are “extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable.”

Attorney General Todd Blanche echoed the Republican president and said criminal investigations of Democrats are possible.

“They are not allowed to just go around threatening existing members of the administration, to go around threatening companies, and that's what President Trump is extremely worried about and he should be,” Mr. Blanche said as he and congressional Democrats appeared on the Sunday news shows to discuss the repercussions from last week's elections.

Rep. Robert Garcia, who is poised to chair the powerful House Oversight Committee in the next Congress, is preparing investigations into what he calls the “Trump crime family.” He said Democrats are not going to be intimidated.

“The days of us not fighting back are over,” said Mr. Garcia, D-Calif.

The early rhetoric sets up a showdown ahead that will likely define Mr. Trump's remaining two years in office and test the power of Congress to put a check on the White House. About seven in 10 voters nationally say Congress is not doing enough to provide checks and balances on the presidency, according to The AP Voter Poll, a survey of more than 1,00,000 midterm voters.

Democrats have made clear that impeachment is an option.

If there are people who have been "shortchanging the American people, screwing over the American people, or stealing from the American people, then they need to be held accountable in a manner consistent with Congress' role, constitutionally,” said Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York.

Some Democrats worried about overreach

But the investigative onslaught is also a source of tension for Democrats, with many warning that delivering on their central promise to voters — actions to lower the cost of living — must take precedence.

Some fear their resounding wins Tuesday that have given them healthy majorities in the House and Senate will prove fleeting if conflict with Mr. Trump defines the agenda.

Sen-elect Adam Hamilton, the first Democrat elected to the chamber from Kansas in 94 years, expressed scepticism about impeachment, saying his campaign was about trying to bring people together. He said he does not want the next two years to be spent “dividing our country further.”

“I'm not as interested in impeachment as setting up guardrails,” Mr. Hamilton said. Still, Mr. Hamilton said he understands that some investigations are necessary, and Democrats “have to look at what's happened in Washington.”

Sen. Bernie Sanders, a Vermont independent who caucuses with Democrats, said he wants to hold Mr. Trump accountable, but warned there was only so much time.

“We cannot spend all of our time investigating Trump," Mr. Sanders said. "We've got to stand up for working-class families, make a real difference in their lives.”

Jeffries casts doubt on working with Stephen Miller

Mr. Jeffries, who is on the cusp of becoming the nation's first Black House speaker, was asked on election night about the prospects of working with Mr. Trump. He said he would be ready to work with the other side of the aisle “whenever and wherever possible to deliver real results.”

Mr. Jeffries on Sunday (November 8, 2026) criticised Mr. Trump's choice of longtime adviser Stephen Miller to succeed Susie Wiles as his chief of staff, calling him an “awful choice” and cast doubt on the prospect of working with him.

“There's not going to be an opportunity, certainly, to work with Stephen Miller and what he represents. And we're committed to forcefully pushing back against the extremism that they may try to continue to unleash on the American people,” he said.

Democrats across the ideological spectrum have been critical of the appointment of Mr. Miller, an architect of Mr. Trump's mass deportation machine that became an issue in the midterm elections. Nationally, about 6 in 10 voters said the administration's actions on immigration enforcement had “gone too far,” according to The AP Voter Poll.

Mr. Jeffries also said he supports a pending resolution from Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky, to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth. Mr. Jeffries said Democrats would be discussing it when they return to the Capitol this week. “Hegseth has got to go,” he said.

“I'm a hard yes on the Hegseth resolution,” Mr. Jeffries said.

Mr. Hegseth in a video dismissed the impeachment push as “all about the politics of personal destruction.” He said it “won't work with me."

New senators express scepticism about Schumer

At least two new incoming Democratic senators expressed some reservations on Sunday (November 8, 2026) about Democratic leader Chuck Schumer, who's expected to be re-elected to his post after leading his party back to the majority.

Mr. Hamilton said he's told Mr. Schumer, who is currently running unopposed, that he means no disrespect but that the New Yorker is a polarising figure in Kansas and Mr. Hamilton is aiming for someone less divisive.

“What I'd be looking for is a leader who can lead from the centre, somebody who can bring Republicans and Democrats together,” Mr. Hamilton said. “It feels like it is a time for fresh and new ideas and somebody who can unite us instead of dividing us.”

Mr. Hamilton said he wants to get to know the other Democratic senators better before he makes any recommendations.

Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan, whom Mr. Schumer did not back in the Democratic primary, said he had been committed to Sen. Chris Van Hollen, but acknowledged that the Maryland Democrat does not appear to be running for the post.

Mr. El-Sayed said he and Mr. Schumer, who put $67 million into Mr. El-Sayed's general election campaign, “figured out how to work together” after the primary.

“The question to me is, who wants to be the leader who's going to make sure that we deliver on the mandate that we just got?” Mr. El-Sayed said.

Mr. Blanche was interviewed on “Fox News Sunday” and CNN's “State of the Union.” Mr. Garcia also was on CNN, Mr. Jeffries spoke on ABC's “This Week,” Mr. Hamilton and Mr. Sanders were on CNN and NBC, and Mr. El-Sayed appeared on ABC

World.title: Fire engulfs Jammu’s Nehru Market, guts around 12 shops
World.content:
Fire gutted at least a dozen shops in the historic Nehru Market in the heart of Jammu city on Sunday (November 8, 2026) night, while a separate blaze broke out at the district police lines in Kathua district, officials said.

No casualties were reported in either incident, which occurred amid widespread bursting of firecrackers on Deepavali.

All the same, the exact cause of the blazes is yet to be ascertained.

A massive fire swept the Warehouse Nehru Market, one of Jammu's oldest wholesale hubs of food grains, essential commodities and other daily-use items.

The Fire and Emergency Services Department said the fire began in one of the shops at around 9.15 p.m. and spread quickly to adjoining establishments due to storage of edible oil.

The market has been serving traders, retailers and consumers since the 1950s.

Fire tenders from several stations across Jammu city were rushed to the spot, officials said. At the site, Divisional Commissioner, Jammu, Vikas Kundal, said the fire had been largely brought under control.

"Fire and Emergency Services personnel, police teams and the civil administration are present at the spot. The fire has been brought under control, and efforts are underway to extinguish the remaining flames in the last one or two shops," he told reporters.

Warehouse Association president Deepak Gupta blamed the delayed response of the fire and emergency services for the spread of the flames.

"What started as a small fire has engulfed around 15 shops and threatens to spread further. This is a complete failure and gross negligence on the part of the fire brigade. Despite the fire station being barely five minutes away, only two fire engines arrived after an hour and a half," he alleged.

Mr. Gupta said the fire brigade officials did not even answer phone calls at first.

BJP MLA Vikram Randhawa said at least eight shops were gutted in fire.

"It is deeply unfortunate that this incident occurred on Diwali, destroying eight shops and causing estimated losses of crores of rupees and comes days after a massive fire in Shiv Market near the Jammu Railway Station destroyed dozens of shops," he said.

The lawmaker said that the administration should have stationed at least two to three fire tenders at each major market, especially after the Shiv market incident.

"The Fire and Emergency Services have failed to learn from past incidents. The authorities must take these lapses seriously," Mr. Randhawa said.

In the border district of Kathua, a store room at the district police lines went up in flames at 9.50 p.m.

Fire tenders have rushed to the spot and efforts were on to douse the conflagration.

World.title: Production suspended at Iraq’s Khor Mor gas field after drone attack, sources say
World.content:
​Production ⁠was halted on Sunday (November 8, 2026) at Iraq’s Khor Mor ‌gas field, one of ‌the largest ‌in ⁠the Kurdistan region, after ⁠a drone attack targeted the field, two ​security sources ‌said.

Smoke was seen rising from the field, the two ‌sources said. An ​engineer working at the field ⁠said a gas storage facility ‌was hit during the attack, with all crew ordered to go into shelters for ‌fear of further attacks.

The ​major gas field provides supplies ⁠for regional power generation.

World.title: Egypt train collision kills 7, injures 112: Health Ministry
World.content:
Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital on Sunday (November 8, 2026), derailing several carriages, killing seven people and injuring more than 100 others, according to the authorities.

Egypt’s railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to the city of Aswan.

The Health Ministry said 112 people were injured and were now being treated in hospitals around the Giza area.

The Ministry said the injuries ranged from bruises and abrasions to fractures of the limbs, pelvis and vertebrae, as well as head and facial lacerations and chest injuries.

Forty-five patients had been discharged after receiving treatment, while seven others were expected to be released later.

President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said he was following the accident “with great concern”, and had directed authorities to conduct an urgent investigation to “hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent”.

Witnesses described chaotic rescue efforts after the collision, as villagers, first responders and railway workers scrambled to reach passengers trapped inside overturned carriages.

Abdel Wahed Mohamed, 31, who was sitting at a nearby cafe when the collision occurred, said the Aswan-bound train had stopped, when the Fayoum-bound train crashed into it.

“The train overturned at around 1:30 pm. Six carriages overturned,” he said, adding that victims suffered a range of injuries, including head wounds and broken limbs.

Another witness, Ahmed Moussa, 25, said rescuers dug beneath one overturned carriage to reach trapped passengers.

“There were people piled on top of each other inside,” he said, adding that he saw two women among the dead.

Taha Abdel Tawab, 43, said he “saw a young man leaving the train carrying his dead father”.

AFP journalists saw several passenger carriages strewn across the tracks and surrounding farmland.

One carriage lay on its side beside the railway embankment, while another had been torn open by the force of the impact, exposing twisted metal, shattered seats and passengers’ belongings.

Heavy machinery

Rescue workers used cranes and heavy machinery to right overturned carriages as ambulances ferried the injured to nearby hospitals.

Villagers gathered around the cordoned-off wreckage, watching recovery operations continue into the evening.

One victim was a resident of the nearby village, according to local witness Reda Kamel Labib, who criticised rescue delays caused by inadequate transport infrastructure in the area.

First responders and passersby helped lift one of the victims out of the wreckage in a black body bag, AFP images showed.

Authorities said they had launched an investigation into the cause of the crash, which occurred in Giza’s Al-Ayyat area, the site of Egypt’s worst-ever rail disaster.

In 2002, more than 370 people were killed when a fire swept through a train carrying holiday travellers south of Cairo. In 2009, multiple train crashes in the area killed dozens.

Egypt’s 110 million people depend heavily on rail transport, but the network — one of the largest in Africa — has suffered repeated deadly accidents.

Over the past decade, Egypt has poured billions of dollars into updating its transport infrastructure, including new highways and high-speed rail lines, but has yet to overhaul much of its ageing rail network.

World.title: Infiltrators lurking across the border, will send them back from the same way they enter: Adhikari
World.content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday (November 9, 2026) said that infiltrators are lurking across the border and promised to send them back the same way they try to enter into India.

Mr. Adhikari spent Diwali afternoon with Border Security Force (BSF) personnel at Hingalganj in North 24 Parganas in West Bengal.

After touring the area on a BSF speedboat in the Ichhamati river that serves as a border between India and Bangladesh, the CM said that he could see no fencing on the Bangladesh side and infiltrators lurking along the border. “Bangladeshis are there. If they find a gap, they will enter India in a hurry,” he said.

Mr. Adhikari said lakhs of infiltrators have been pushed back into Bangladesh after the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power. “We will search infiltrators and send them back from the very same way they are coming. Search will go on for 15 kilometres from the border,” he said.

The BJP government came to power in West Bengal on the promise of pushing back infiltrators and the BJP government has been making claims of sending back thousands of infiltrators.

Blaming the previous Trinamool Congress government for non-cooperation with the BSF, Mr. Adhikari said that a wonderful coordination has been achieved between the West Bengal police and the BSF under his government.

“I, as the chief minister of the state, apologise to you for the derogatory remarks and behaviour of the previous regime towards BSF and CRPF,” he said.

The BJP government in West Bengal has handed over about 1,777 acres of land across nine border districts to the BSF for fencing and setting up outposts along the India-Bangladesh border.

India shares a 4,096-kilometre border with Bangladesh, of which about 2,216 km lies along West Bengal.

The Chief Minister said that most of issues have been sorted and land for erecting fencing along Ichhamati has been given. Mr. Adhikari said West Bengal’s Department of Irrigation and Waterways will construct the fencing along the 71-kilometre stretch of river.

He said that his government will introduce ‘Seema Mitra’ award for the BSF, the SSB and State police personnel from 2027 to recognise their exceptional work related to guarding the country’s border. He said a selection committee will be set up to decide the awardees from the forces.

World.title: Air pollution over 50 times WHO limit in parts of Delhi as people defy ban on firecrackers on Deepavali
World.content:
As Delhiites burst firecrackers well past the 10 p.m. deadline set by the Supreme Court for Deepavali night, air pollution shot up to over 50 times World Health Organisation (WHO) limits in parts of the city, official data showed.

The level of PM2.5 (a major pollutant) in Akshardham was 760.99 micrograms per cubic meter at 11 p.m. on Sunday (November 8, 2026), as per Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) data. This is about 50.73 times the WHO permissible limit of 15 micrograms per cubic meter for a 24-hour period.

Deepavali 2026: All you need to know about Supreme Court-permitted time slots, green crackers and other directives

PM2.5 (Particulate Matter 2.5) are fine inhalable particles, which can get into lungs and bloodstream and lead to a range of respiratory and other diseases.

The level of PM2.5 in Anand Vihar was 767 micrograms per cubic meter at 11 p.m. on Sunday (November 8, 2026), as per DPCC data — This is about 51.13 times the WHO permissible limit.

The level of PM2.5 in Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium was 702 micrograms per cubic meter, as per DPCC data, which is about 46.8 times the WHO permissible limit.

Also Read | Supreme Court calls Deepavali fireworks a ‘religious practice’, allows green crackers for two days in Delhi-NCR

The overall air quality of Delhi continued to be in the “very poor” category while many parts of the city continued to reel under “severe” air quality.

Every winter, air pollution spikes in Delhi-NCR and many parts of the larger Indo-Gangetic Plains, mainly due to meteorological factors such as lower wind speeds and a drop in temperature. Also, pollution from stubble burning during October and November and bursting of firecrackers during the festive season add to existing pollution from vehicles and dust, worsening the air quality.

World.title: PML-N retains both Gujranwala's NA-77 and Sahiwal's PP-203, unofficial results show
World.content:
LAHORE: The ruling PML-N retained Gujranwala’s National Assembly constituency NA-77 and Sahiwal’s Punjab Assembly constituency PP-203 in Sunday’s by-election.

Both seats had fallen vacant after the deaths of their respective lawmakers in September. Polling in the constituencies began at 8am and concluded at 5pm, with the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) reporting an uninterrupted and largely peaceful process.

In NA-77, PML-N candidate Rashid Basheer Virk was among 11 candidates contesting for the seat left vacant after the Sept 11 demise of his father, Chaudhry Mehmood Bashir Virk, a five-time MNA.

He secured victory by bagging 43,365 votes, while Pakistan Markazi Muslim League’s (PMML) Mohammad Ibrahim remained runner-up with 30,218 ballots, according to the Form-47 seen by Dawn.

Form-47 is the provisional consolidated statement of results of the vote count of all polling stations in a constituency, prepared by the returning officer (RO) concerned.

In PP-203 of Chichawatni, PML-N’s Muhammad Asad Hanif Jutt won with 42,114 votes, defeating his closest rival, Muhammad Awais Mahmood of Tehreek-i-Ehsas Pakistan (TEP), who secured 24,512 votes, according to its Form-47.

Both by-elections were marked by a low voter turnout, with 15.7 per cent in NA-77 and 27.6pc recorded in PP-203, according to Forms 47.

The by-poll was held following the death of PML-N MPA Chaudhry Muhammad Hanif Jutt. This was the second time that a by-election was held in the constituency after the 2024 general elections.

Notices were also issued to several PML-N lawmakers for alleged violations of the election code, mostly over visiting polling stations in the two constituencies.

Earlier in the day, Chief Election Commissioner Sikander Sultan Raja visited the provincial election chief’s office, where he was briefed on the polling process in both constituencies, ECP said.

After the balloting process concluded, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, whose PML-N is in power in the province, made multiple posts on X, claiming her party was in the lead in both NA-77 and PP-203.

In one post, CM Maryam wrote, “This electoral victory is no ordinary victory. It is a resounding public rebuke to conspiracy peddlers, hate mongers and those who refuse to read the writing on the wall.”

She contended that the results portrayed that the “politics of delivery is far more enduring than the politics of hate and revenge”.

“I am glad politics has returned to delivery and performance. Wake up and smell the coffee… or keep sleeping in denial!” the PML-N leader added.

Notices over alleged electoral conduct violations

While the polling was under way, notices, copies of which are available with Dawn, were issued to Punjab MPA Qudsia Batool, MNA Saira Afzal Tarar and Parliamentary Secretary for Information and Culture Shazia Rizwan for alleged violation of the Code of Conduct after reports emerged on social media that the three had visited various polling stations within NA-77, a statement issued by the office of the provincial election commissioner said.

Notices were also issued over alleged violations of the Code of Conduct to PML-N’s MNA Syeda Nosheen Iftikhar and MPA Hina Arshad Warraich for allegedly visiting polling stations.

The officials were directed to appear at the Election Complex in Gujranwala for an explanation at 3pm.

Separately, PML-N leader and Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari claimed in a post on X that supporters of PMML candidate Qazi Ibrahim Gujjar were caught “openly stamping ballots” with the election commission staff present.
